how_built.label: Spine
how_built.text: The 2026 Builder 100 (ranked by 2025 closings), cross-checked against Pro Builder's 2026 list. The publisher blocks automated reads, so the list was read from the Internet Archive's copy of the publisher's page and is tagged Reported.

how_built.label: Research
how_built.text: About 200 research agents, one per builder part (leadership; division and regional leaders; financing and M&A), reading SEC filings, company sites and press releases, trade and local press, and state officer records. Every fact carries a source link, a retrieval date and a confidence tag. LinkedIn was never opened; no paywall was bypassed.

how_built.label: Regional heads
how_built.text: A second targeted pass on the 25 largest builders. 81 of 163 regions at those builders have a publicly named head.

how_built.label: Accuracy check
how_built.text: A fresh agent that did not do the research re-opened the sources for the highest-stakes rows on every builder: 1,299 rows checked, 1,199 held (92%), 51 corrected, 39 downgraded to Inferred, 10 removed.

how_built.label: Result
how_built.text: 100 builders, 2,105 people (342 land, 234 finance, 140 regional heads); 70.1% of people rows Verified; an average of 41.6 people per public builder against 15.1 per private builder; 22 builders with a publicly named land banker; 336 debt instruments.

how_built.label: Where the method ran out
how_built.text: (a) Some builders publish no one below their executive officers, so their regional heads are marked "not publicly disclosed" (for example NVR, Tri Pointe, and K. Hovnanian's group presidents). (b) Filings report land banking in aggregate and rarely name the land banker, so counterparties are named for only 22 builders. (c) Private builders disclose almost nothing about financing. (d) Names seen only in third-party directories or search snippets are kept as leads and tagged Inferred. (e) State-level volumes are not public, so geography is by presence, not by size.

ranking.name: Builder 100

profile.org_note: Corporate (Arlington, TX) -> 14 internal homebuilding operating regions, each with a region president, a region CFO and region legal counsel -> 92 operating divisions (division president, controller, and the division's own land entitlement, acquisition and development staff) across 128 markets in 38 states; the 14 internal regions roll up into six reporting segments (Northwest, Southwest, South Central, Southeast, East, North), and the company does not publish the internal region map. Land deals are negotiated by the division, approved by the region president, then approved and funded at corporate by an executive officer: per the 2026 proxy the CEO (Romanowski) directly oversees six regions, the COO (Murray) six and the CFO (Wheat) two, each 'including approval of investments in land and lots'. No corporate head of land is publicly named. Finance contacts: CFO Bill Wheat (capital structure, financing, cash management), Treasurer Collin Dawson and SVP Real Estate Finance Jeff Tebeaux (both named only in Texas Comptroller officer reports). Majority-owned (about 62%) lot developer Forestar Group has its own officers and six regional offices and sells about 86% of its lots to D.R. Horton. The 2026 proxy also names Ryan and Reagan Horton (sons of the founder, 5%+ holders) as a related-party land seller and land banker to the company. The company does not publish the names or territories of its internal regions, so the region names shown here (West, South, East, North) are third-party labels. The 2025 Texas officer lists for DRHI, Inc. and D. R. Horton, Inc. name ten Region Presidents (Brundage, Davern, Etheridge, Farris, Hill, R. Horton, Lindhorst, Pentecost, Saltzberg, Whitehurst) for the 14 internal regions; third-party executive lists label Farris West, Rick Horton South and Hill East, and Horton and Lindhorst both sit on the Texas division entities. The six 10-K reporting segments are accounting roll-ups with no published leader.
profile.summary: Largest US homebuilder by closings every year since 2002: 84,202 homes closed and $33.0B consolidated revenue in fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-09-30), 92 divisions in 128 markets across 38 states, mostly entry-level and first move-up product at an average closing price of $363,600. Deliberately land-light: 570,600 lots owned and controlled at 2026-09-30, of which 77% (440,100) are controlled through purchase contracts and 68% of fiscal 2026 closings were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties; it owns about 62% of lot developer Forestar Group (NYSE: FOR), and its proxy states it routinely assigns land contracts to third-party lot developers and land bankers.

financing.summary: D.R. Horton funds itself with operating cash flow (US$3.5bn in FY2026), a US$3.3bn unsecured revolver agented by Mizuho, and investment-grade senior notes (A3 / BBB+ / A-); consolidated debt to capital was 20.8% at 9/30/2026 against a stated long-term target of about 20%, and it returned US$4.1bn to shareholders in the year. It controls 77% of its 570,600 homebuilding lots through land and lot purchase contracts (US$28.7bn remaining purchase price secured by US$2.6bn of deposits) and owns only about a 1.5-year supply. The controlled position is supplied by its 62%-owned lot developer Forestar (38,400 lots; 23% of FY2026 finished-lot purchases) and by a wide base of third-party lot developers that the company does not name; no institutional land banker is named in D.R. Horton's filings. The room for a land banker is mostly indirect: Horton has no set target for the controlled position, wants finished lots rather than self-development, and Forestar sells lots to unnamed lot bankers who expect to resell them to Horton (146 lots in FY2026, down from 927 in FY2025). With US$7.2bn of liquidity and an A-range balance sheet, Horton does not need land-bank capital for funding; the pitch has to be about returns, lot delivery and developer capacity.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light by purchase contract. Stated strategy: control a significant portion of the land and finished-lot position through purchase contracts and prioritise buying finished lots from Forestar and other land developers over self-development. Expects to own a one- to two-year supply of lots; no set target for the controlled lot position. 68% of FY2026 homes closed (70% in Q4) were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties, up from 65% in FY2025. FY2026 investment in lots, land and development was US$8.2bn; in Q4 it was US$2.0bn, of which US$1.4bn was finished lots, US$500m development and US$120m land (Q4 FY2026 call). Lot costs rose 6% in FY2026.

lots.source_title: D.R. Horton FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-11-18)
lots.note: Homebuilding segment only. total_controlled = owned + controlled through land and lot purchase contracts. 77,300 of the owned lots are finished. Controlled lots include 38,400 Forestar-owned lots (19,800 under contract, 18,600 under right of first offer). Remaining purchase price of controlled lots US$28.7bn, secured by US$2.6bn of earnest money (US$2.0bn / US$198.9m of that with Forestar). years_supply 6.8 = 570,600 lots / 84,202 homes closed in FY2026; the company presents 1.5 years owned and 5.2 years controlled (Q4 FY2026 investor presentation) and says it expects to own a one- to two-year supply. Prior year 9/30/2025: 591,900 total, 147,000 owned, 444,900 controlled (75%). By region at 9/30/2026 (owned / controlled): Northwest 10,500 / 16,900; Southwest 17,300 / 31,200; South Central 30,900 / 115,400; Southeast 27,600 / 103,300; East 28,600 / 104,600; North 15,600 / 68,700.

land_banking.description: Publicly traded lot developer, about 62% owned by D.R. Horton. Under the June 2017 Master Supply Agreement Horton's divisions buy finished lots from Forestar; at 9/30/2026 Horton had 19,800 Forestar lots under contract and a right of first offer on a further 18,600. Forestar sold 11,629 lots to Horton in FY2026 for US$1,291.5m (86% of its lots sold), about 23% of Horton's finished-lot purchases.
land_banking.source_title: D.R. Horton FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-11-18)
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m = remaining purchase price of Horton's lot contracts with Forestar (US$2.0bn, secured by US$198.9m of earnest money). Per Forestar's FY2026 10-K the supply agreement gives Horton a right of first offer on up to 100% of lots in Horton-sourced projects and up to 50% in Forestar-sourced projects, and runs until Horton owns under 15% of Forestar or June 29, 2037; Horton's consent is needed for Forestar debt that would take leverage above 40%. Forestar is separately capitalised (US$1.3bn liquidity, 6.7% net debt to capital) and its debt is not guaranteed by Horton. A Forestar stockholder derivative suit (Mississippi PERS v. D.R. Horton, Del. Ch., filed 2025-04-29) challenges lot-sale transactions between the two companies. Forestar's Executive Chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired 2026-10-31; CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman and CEO on 2026-11-01. Verification 2026-11-19: Forestar FY2026 10-K states revenues from lot sales to D.R. Horton of US$1,292.2m on 11,629 lots (vs US$1,291.5m in the description; the small gap was not resolved). Forestar Group Inc. is listed on the NYSE as FOR. Second source for the same relationship: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1406587/000162828026068139/a9302026exhibit991.htm, which is the source on the Forestar row in the land-finance scan.

land_banking.counterparty: Lot bankers buying from Forestar for resale to D.R. Horton (not named)
land_banking.description: Forestar reports that its lot sales to customers other than D.R. Horton included 146 lots in fiscal 2026 and 927 lots in fiscal 2025 sold to lot bankers who expect to sell those lots to D.R. Horton at a future date. The lot bankers are not identified.
land_banking.source_title: Forestar Q4 and fiscal 2026 results release (2026-10-29)
land_banking.note: Lot counts from Forestar's Q4 FY2026 release; dollar values (US$33.4m in FY2026, US$83.4m in FY2025) from Forestar's FY2026 10-K, which words it as 'a lot banker' (singular) where the release says 'lot bankers'. amount_usd_m and lots are the fiscal 2026 flow, not a balance. This is the only place in either company's filings where land-banker involvement in Horton's lot supply is stated; volume fell about 84% year on year.

land_banking.counterparty: Third-party land and lot developers (not individually disclosed)
land_banking.description: Horton controls about 401,700 lots outside Forestar through land and lot purchase contracts with land developers and land sellers, which it does not name. Contracts are generally non-recourse beyond the deposit, and most lots are expected to be purchased within three years. 68% of FY2026 homes closed were on lots developed by Forestar or third parties.
land_banking.source_title: D.R. Horton FY2026 Form 10-K (filed 2026-11-18)
land_banking.note: Derived: 440,100 controlled lots less 38,400 Forestar lots; US$28.7bn total remaining purchase price less US$2.0bn with Forestar. Related deposits about US$2.4bn of the US$2.6bn total (cash US$2.4bn plus US$231.4m of promissory notes and surety bonds). Only US$78.5m of remaining purchase price carries specific-performance terms. FY2026 write-offs of earnest money and pre-acquisition costs on terminated homebuilding contracts were US$72.5m (US$114.3m in FY2025). The company says it has made significant progress expanding its land developer base and reducing self-development (Q4 FY2026 investor presentation). Counterparty names and any land-banker share of these contracts are not disclosed.

profile.org_note: Single CEO since 2026-01-01: Stuart Miller (Executive Chairman, CEO and President). Under him, COO Jim Parker (East) and EVP Homebuilding David Grove (West) - Area Presidents until 2026-06-05 - oversee eight Regional Presidents listed on the live leadership page under 'Lennar Homebuilding and Land' (Northeast: Mignone; Florida East/North: Gonzalez; Southwest Florida: McMurray; Atlanta/Alabama/Nashville/Gulf Coast: Jensen; Midwest: Burgess; AR/KS/MO/OK: Taylor; AZ/CO/UT: Walker; CA Coastal/Central Valley/San Diego/Las Vegas: Parness), each over Division Presidents who run land buying locally; Texas, the Carolinas, Tampa/Orlando and the Northern California/Pacific Northwest/Idaho/Inland Empire markets have no published regional head. There is no published corporate land chief: per the 10-K corporate handles strategy, land and business acquisitions and financing, land approvals run through the regional and division presidents (several are former VPs of Land), and land-bank/capital structuring sits with CFO Diane Bessette, Treasurer Lauren Dudley and tax head Michael Petrolino; Greg McGuff, styled Regional President and described in early 2026 as leading 'land banking optimization', the Investor Marketplace and SFR, has been off the leadership page since spring 2026. SEC segments (East, Central, South Central, West) differ from these operating regions.
profile.summary: Delivered 82,583 homes in fiscal 2025 (FYE Nov 30) and was selling in 1,708 communities at year-end, across the 26 states in its 10-K segments plus Delaware, West Virginia and Iowa communities in 2026 releases. The most land-light large builder: about 488,000 homesites owned and controlled at 2026-08-31 with fewer than 2.5% owned; 98% were controlled via options with land banks, land sellers and JVs at FY2025 year-end. Millrose Properties (spun off Feb 2025, externally managed by Kennedy Lewis) is the core land banker and Lennar supplied 88% of Millrose's 2025 option-fee revenue, but the 10-K says Lennar also relies on other land banks for land Millrose cannot acquire, which is the opening for Domain.

financing.summary: Lennar is the most land-light of the large builders: at Aug 31, 2026 it owned about 2% of roughly 488,000 homesites and controlled 98% through options with land banks, land sellers and joint ventures. Its main land financier is Millrose Properties, the REIT it spun off in February 2025 and exited as a shareholder in November 2025 (managed by Kennedy Lewis); Millrose had about $5.9B invested under the Lennar Master Program Agreement at Sep 30, 2026 at an 8.5% yield. Lennar's 10-Q says it bought a significant portion of its land from three land banks in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (two at fiscal 2025 year-end); only Millrose is named, and TPG Angelo Gordon's Essential Housing program is the other one documented publicly. Non-refundable option deposits and pre-acquisition costs have grown to $7.2B (from $3.5B at Nov 30, 2024), and Lennar estimates the land banks' total capital outlay on its controlled homesites at about $18.5B, so the pool of Lennar land-bank paper is very large but concentrated in a few providers. Corporate funding is investment-grade and unsecured: a $3.795B revolver (upsized and extended to 2031 in October 2026), a $1.75B term loan due May 2028, and $2.65B of senior notes after a $600M issue in October 2026; net homebuilding debt to capital rose to 12.7% from 2.8% nine months earlier as cash fell to $1.15B and $650M was drawn on the revolver (cash plus undrawn revolver was about $3.6B at Aug 31, 2026 by our arithmetic; the company did not state a liquidity figure).
financing.land_strategy: Land-light / 'asset-light manufacturing' model, in Lennar's words a pure-play, asset-light homebuilder with just-in-time delivery of finished homesites. Since 2019 it has moved land off balance sheet into 'land option platforms' (land banks) and land developer agreements; the June 2026 investor deck calls the shift complete ('land is now administered through third parties'). Controlled share went from 28% (Q4 2018) to 82% (Nov 30, 2024) to 98% (Nov 30, 2025 and Aug 31, 2026). No numeric target is stated beyond maintaining the land-light model; land banks fund horizontal development up to pre-agreed budgets and Millrose limits purchases to land Lennar expects to use within five years.

lots.source_title: Lennar prospectus supplement (424B5) dated 2026-10-13 for the 2029 and 2032 senior notes, via Lennar investor-relations SEC filings viewer; total homesite count from the Q3 FY2026 earnings release (2026-09-16)
lots.note: Lennar states approximately 488,000 homesites owned and controlled (Q3 FY2026 earnings release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920760/000162828026062287/ex991-2026831x8kq3.htm) and about 2% owned / 98% controlled through option contracts with third parties and unconsolidated JVs (prospectus supplement). Exact owned and optioned counts for Aug 31, 2026 were not in the sources opened; 98% / 2% of 488,000 implies roughly 478,000 controlled and 10,000 owned (derived, not stated). Last stated counts: 11K owned (2%) and 486K controlled (98%) at Feb 28, 2026 (June 2026 investor presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920760/000119312526268580/d31288dex991.htm). Years of owned supply is no longer reported. total_controlled here is owned plus controlled.

land_banking.description: Lennar's primary land bank. Under the Master Program Agreement and Master Option Agreement of Feb 7, 2025, Millrose buys and develops land Lennar designates and Lennar holds options with set takedown schedules, paying deposits and monthly option payments. At Sep 30, 2026 Millrose had $5.87B of invested capital under the Lennar agreement at an 8.5% weighted average yield (3.8-year weighted remaining life); in Q3 2026 Lennar took down $620.9M and Millrose redeployed $545.7M into Lennar land and development.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-10-26)
land_banking.note: Amount is Millrose's invested capital under the Lennar Master Program Agreement, not Lennar's cost. Millrose's whole portfolio was 156,729 homesites in 834 communities and 30 states; the Lennar homesite count is not broken out. Lennar's share of Millrose's capital is falling: pro forma for the Dream Finders / Beazer funding about 42% of Millrose's asset base is outside the Lennar agreement.

land_banking.description: Lennar's own balance-sheet exposure to Millrose: $1.3B of deposits and pre-acquisition costs on real estate under Millrose option contracts at Aug 31, 2026, up from $1.0B at Nov 30, 2025.
land_banking.source_title: Lennar Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 (filed 2026-10-02), note: Variable Interest Entities
land_banking.note: Millrose is one of the three 'Land Banks' the note describes; no amounts were due to the Land Banks for land purchases at quarter end.

land_banking.description: Seed transaction: in the February 2025 spin-off Lennar contributed $5.6B of land (about 87,000 homesites) and $1.0B of cash to Millrose, including $584.0M of option deposits paid under the Master Option Agreement, and took back options on the land.
land_banking.source_title: Lennar FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-01-28), note: Variable Interest Entities
land_banking.note: The spin-off press release of Feb 7, 2025 gives the land figure as $5.5B; the 10-K figure is used. The ~$1.0B cash figure is from Millrose FY2025 10-K Item 1, not the Lennar VIE note.

land_banking.description: Rausch Coleman land: on Feb 10, 2025 Millrose bought Rausch Coleman's land (about 25,000 homesites, roughly $859M cash net of Lennar-funded option deposits and holdbacks) while Lennar bought the homebuilding operations; Lennar paid Millrose a further $90.4M of option deposits and holds options on the land.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1
land_banking.note: The $90.4M additional option deposit is from Lennar's FY2025 10-K VIE note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/920760/000162828026003870/R17.htm). Millrose has since funded the land side of other builder acquisitions (New Home Co. / Landsea in 2025; Dream Finders / Beazer in 2026).

land_banking.description: Founder's Rights Agreement: gives Lennar an evergreen Capital Priority Right over a set amount of Millrose's capital, the right to match any lower option rate Millrose gives another builder, a consent right over Millrose leverage above 1:1 debt to equity and over pooling Lennar assets as shared collateral, and pause rights. Amended Aug 27, 2026: capital Millrose raises solely to buy completed build-to-rent homes is now excluded from Lennar's priority (alongside the first $2B of debt and equity Millrose raises), and Lennar's consent right over pledging its optioned properties in shared-collateral financings was restated.
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Form 8-K dated 2026-08-27 (Item 1.01, amendment to Founder's Rights Agreement)
land_banking.note: Amendment terms are from exhibit 10.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000119312526378466/d83131dex101.htm); whether $2B is a changed figure is not clear because the original text was not read. Description of the rights is from Millrose's FY2025 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000201720626000002/ck0002017206-20251231.htm). The same 8-K amended Millrose's management agreement with Kennedy Lewis (investment guidelines and reimbursable expenses).

land_banking.description: Completed-home sale: in Q3 2026 Millrose bought 1,233 completed single-family homes from Lennar across 18 states as a single-family rental pilot, at an aggregate cost basis of about $333M (about $213M of it financed with limited-recourse secured debt).
land_banking.source_title: Millrose Properties Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-10-26)
land_banking.note: Not a lot-option deal: Millrose is taking finished-home inventory from Lennar. Count of homes confirmed in Millrose's Q3 2026 10-Q SFR note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000119312526447297/R16.htm); lots field left empty because these are homes, not lots.

land_banking.description: Programmatic land bank dating to 2020. A Master Agreement dated Oct 8, 2020 between AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. and Lennar's Essential Housing Financing, LLC (Lennar Corporation joined as parent guarantor) set up the 'SPV-1 Program': the owner buys land Lennar nominates, grants lot options on a fixed takedown schedule, reimburses development costs, and is protected by an option fee and a parent termination fee; owner equity for the program was capped at $1.0B.
land_banking.source_title: Lennar FY2020 Form 10-K, Exhibit 10.12: Master Agreement with AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. (Oct 8, 2020)
land_banking.note: Amount is the equity cap of the first program, not land deployed and not a current balance. The agreement is 2020 vintage; later program sizes and whether Angelo Gordon is one of the three 'Land Banks' in Lennar's fiscal 2026 10-Q are not disclosed. Notices went to AGWIP Asset Management (Scottsdale) and Angelo, Gordon & Co. (New York).

land_banking.description: Reported current terms: Hunterbrook, citing a California county pension fund's (SBCERA) materials, says Lennar posts a 19.9% upfront deposit with Angelo Gordon (treated as first loss, about twice the roughly 10% at Millrose), with a maximum 40-month term, a rigid monthly takedown schedule, and termination rights and fees if Lennar falls behind; a TPG document cited a 15% IRR on the first Lennar land bank.

competitor_relationships.description: Millrose bought 1,233 completed homes from Lennar across 18 states for an aggregate cost of about $333M (about $270K to $280K per home), financed with $213M of limited-recourse secured debt at SOFR+120 bps and about $120M of equity. Underwritten at roughly a 5% going-in cap rate, about 8% unlevered and 10-12% levered IRR; about 10% of homes rented as of 2026-10-26; leasing managed by Evergreen Residential. Management says no further purchases since quarter-end and that rent-to-own is still being designed.
competitor_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27); underwriting detail from the Q3 2026 call transcript (Reported)

competitor_relationships.builder_name: Unnamed 'Borrower A' (development loan; listed among Lennar related-party balances)
competitor_relationships.description: Secured residential development loan across multiple US markets at 12% paid-in-kind interest; carrying amount $287.7M at 2025-12-31, maturity 2026-01-31 extended on 2026-01-29 to 2026-07-31. The Q3 2025 10-Q lists $302.7M of development loan receivables among balances with Lennar, so this borrower appears to be Lennar-related (identity not disclosed).
competitor_relationships.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, schedule of development loans secured by residential properties

competitor_relationships.description: TPG's own description (March 2026): Lennar is the anchor customer; a 'proprietary sourcing arrangement' / exclusive first look makes Essential Housing one of Lennar's most significant land partners. EHF-1 (2020, $1.0bn equity, about $3.1bn originated, about 110 projects) was 100% Lennar and is fully monetised. Deposit 19.9%. Lennar's share of EHF-2/3 is not disclosed.
competitor_relationships.source_title: TPG Essential Housing Fund IV presentation to SBCERA, March 2026 (Exhibit A to SBCERA File 26-114), pp. 7, 10; EHF III deck p. 13

competitor_relationships.description: Anchor relationship. Master Agreement of 8 Oct 2020 created the 'SPV-1 Program': AG Essential Housing Company 1, L.P. buys land Lennar designates and grants Lennar lot options on a set takedown schedule; Lennar pays an option fee (deposit) at closing and Lennar Corporation guarantees a termination fee. Owner equity for the program capped at $1,000m. Dollar figure is the equity cap, not land deployed.
competitor_relationships.source_title: Lennar FY2020 10-K, Exhibit 10.12

competitor_relationships.description: Sept 2026: AGWIP Asset Management, as land banker for Lennar, bought 132.24 acres / 444 lots in north Phoenix (117th Ave and Deer Valley Road) for $60.14m cash; closed 15 Sep 2026 (Vizzda).
competitor_relationships.source_title: KTAR News, 20 Sep 2026

competitor_relationships.description: Ontario, CA: TPG Angelo Gordon bought 23 acres at 13150 Archibald Ave from Lennar Homes for $49.6m (265 planned units); Lennar had bought the site under two months earlier. Article does not state an option, so the land-bank reading is an inference from the seller being Lennar. A second Ontario site (30 acres, $65.1m, 333 units, seller Richland Communities) closed alongside; builder not named.
competitor_relationships.source_title: Commercial Observer, 22 Dec 2023

competitor_relationships.description: Rialto, CA (Inland Empire): TPG Angelo Gordon bought 41.3 acres for $44.5m in Dec 2023 as land-banking partner for Lennar Homes, which holds the option; planned 429 attached/detached condos ('Renaissance Liberty'). Sellers Lewis Group and Hillwood. Data from Vizzda via trade press.
competitor_relationships.source_title: Commercial Observer, 23 Jan 2024

competitor_relationships.description: Hunterbrook, from SBCERA materials: Lennar's deposit with AG's Essential Housing fund is 19.9% of land value, max 40-month term, rigid monthly takedowns, termination fee; AG reported a 15% IRR on its first Lennar land bank.
competitor_relationships.source_title: Hunterbrook: What Lennar Owes

ma.counterparty: Quarterra Group (majority interest sold to TPG Real Estate)
ma.description: Lennar sold a majority interest in its Quarterra multifamily development subsidiary to TPG Real Estate, which made a $1.0B strategic commitment; Lennar retained a minority stake and legacy JVs were excluded. Announced Jan 6, 2026.
ma.map_impact: Takes most of the multifamily platform out of Lennar and brings TPG in as a capital partner at the platform level; no change to homebuilding divisions or lots. Quarterra CEO Brad Greiwe stays.
ma.source_title: TPG and Lennar Announce Strategic Partnership to Recapitalize Quarterra (2026-01-06)
ma.note: Price and exact ownership split not disclosed. Sale month from Lennar's FY2025 10-K.

ma.counterparty: Millrose Properties, Inc. (remaining ~20% stake)
ma.description: Split-off exchange offer: Lennar swapped its remaining 33,298,754 Millrose Class A shares for 8,049,594 of its own Class A shares, cutting investments and equity by $1.1B and booking a one-time $156.1M loss.
ma.map_impact: Lennar no longer owns Millrose and is no longer its related party; the relationship is now purely contractual (Master Program Agreement and Founder's Rights Agreement). Millrose is free-standing as it adds other builders.
ma.source_title: Lennar FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-01-28), note: Business Transaction
ma.note: Completion date from Millrose's FY2025 10-K.

ma.counterparty: Rausch Coleman Homes
ma.description: Lennar completed the purchase of the homebuilding operations of Rausch Coleman Homes (Fayetteville, Arkansas), which delivered about 5,300 homes in 2024 at an average price near $230,000. Lennar recorded $312.6M of assets (mainly homes under construction and finished homesites) and $73.0M of liabilities; cash paid net of cash acquired was $254M. Millrose bought the land (about 25,000 homesites, roughly $859M) and Lennar holds options on it.
ma.map_impact: Rausch Coleman (about 5,300 closings) is now inside Lennar's count rather than a separate builder. Adds Lennar markets in Arkansas (Bentonville/Fayetteville, Little Rock, Jonesboro), Oklahoma (Tulsa, Stillwater), Alabama (Birmingham, Tuscaloosa) and Kansas City, and deepens Houston, San Antonio, Oklahoma City, Huntsville and the Florida Gulf Coast. Shows the template: the land banker buys the target's land, the builder buys only operations.
ma.source_title: Lennar Completes Acquisition of Rausch Coleman Homes (2025-02-10)
ma.note: Asset, liability and cash figures from Lennar's FY2025 10-K (Business Transaction note and MD&A); land figures from Millrose's FY2025 10-K. Total price not disclosed.

ma.counterparty: Millrose Properties, Inc.
ma.description: Taxable spin-off of about 80% of Millrose to Lennar stockholders (120,980,401 Class A and 11,819,811 Class B shares); Lennar contributed $5.6B of land (about 87,000 homesites) and $1.0B of cash and kept about 20% non-voting. Millrose listed on the NYSE as MRP, externally managed by Kennedy Lewis.
ma.map_impact: Creates the public land banker that now competes with Domain for other builders' business while holding most of Lennar's former land. Moves Lennar to roughly 98% optioned homesites and makes Millrose's manager (Kennedy Lewis) the counterparty for most Lennar land decisions.
ma.source_title: Lennar Form 8-K dated 2025-02-07 (Items 7.01, 8.01, Millrose spin-off completion)
ma.note: Cash contribution (~$1.0B, incl. $585M of cash deposit liabilities) and the Kennedy Lewis manager are from Millrose FY2025 10-K Item 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2017206/000201720626000002/ck0002017206-20251231.htm); the cited 8-K states only the share counts, ~20% retention and the MRP listing.

industry_deals.description: Berkshire Hathaway has been buying Lennar shares on the open market; this is not an acquisition, and the date shown is the date of the report. ResiClub reports from Berkshire's SEC filings that Berkshire raised its Lennar holding by 94% in Q3 2026 and by about 260% since the start of 2026, to around 11% of Lennar; an earlier ResiClub piece (2026-08-20) put the holding at 13.1M Class A shares plus Class B, worth just over $1.2B, with a small new D.R. Horton position of 3,600 shares. No bid for Lennar has been reported.
industry_deals.map_impact: No row merges. The owner of the new Taylor Morrison / Clayton platform (ranks 6 and 12) is now also a roughly 11% shareholder of rank 2 Lennar, which matters for anyone reading Lennar's and Millrose's ownership and for speculation about further Berkshire housing moves.
industry_deals.source_title: ResiClub: Warren Buffett's successor makes third big housing market bet this year, now owning around 11% of Lennar (2026-10-05)

industry_deals.description: Closed 2025-02-10 (previously announced). Lennar bought the homebuilding operations of Fayetteville, Arkansas-based Rausch Coleman, which delivered about 5,300 homes at an average price of about $230,000 in calendar 2024. Millrose Properties, just spun off from Lennar, bought Rausch Coleman's land and Lennar holds options on it. Lennar did not disclose a price; Construction Briefing (2025-05-13) cited a $900 million transaction value.
industry_deals.map_impact: Rausch Coleman no longer exists as a separate ranked builder: its roughly 5,300 annual closings are inside Lennar (#2). Lennar gained new markets in Arkansas (including Bentonville/Fayetteville and Little Rock), Tulsa, Birmingham and Kansas City. First builder acquisition financed with Millrose land banking, the template later used for New Home Co / Landsea.
industry_deals.source_title: Lennar press release: Lennar Completes Acquisition of Rausch Coleman Homes (2025-02-10)

profile.org_note: Homebuilding runs through about 35 local divisions (each under a division president, with its own VP or director of land acquisition) grouped into four geographic operating Areas, West (Chris Edgar), Central (Charlie Tipton), Southeast (Rich McCormick) and North (Tony Barbee), plus a fifth non-geographic Manufacturing/ICG area (Ryan Melin); the 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports list the same five area presidents, who sit under COO Matt Koart. The Areas do not match the six SEC reporting segments (Northeast: MD, MA, NJ, PA, RI, VA; Southeast: GA, NC, SC, TN; Florida; Midwest: IL, IN, KY, MI, MN, OH; Texas; West: AZ, CA, CO, NV, NM, OR, UT, WA), and the company does not publish which divisions sit in which Area. There is no published corporate head of land: deals are sourced by division land teams and approved up through area presidents and the COO, with corporate finance (Treasurer Bryce Langen for structured land transactions, SVP Finance David Carrier for asset management) as the land-finance gatekeepers and the Board's Finance and Investment Committee reviewing certain land acquisitions.
profile.summary: Third-largest US homebuilder by the company's own description: 1,014 active communities in 47 markets across 26 states at year-end 2025, selling under Pulte Homes, Centex, Del Webb, DiVosta and John Wieland. It controlled 234,632 lots at 31 Dec 2025, 57% of them under option (133,528 optioned, 101,104 owned), and invested $5.2 billion in land acquisition and development in 2025. Growth moves in the last year are new-market entries run from existing divisions (Cincinnati, Florida Panhandle via a 1,326 to 2,653 homesite contract with St. Joe, Utah).

financing.summary: PulteGroup is investment grade (Baa1/BBB+/A-) and lightly levered: $1.8B of senior notes, no notes due before 2031, an undrawn $1.75B Bank of America-agented revolver to 2031, and debt-to-capital of 12.1% (3.0% net) at 2026-09-30. It funds land mainly from operating cash flow ($5.2B land spend in 2025, about $5.3B guided for 2026) while buying back about $1.3B of stock a year. It controls 224,275 lots, 54.6% under option. Most options are with land sellers, and land bankers hold only about 7% of controlled lots. Management's stated future mix is about 20% land-banker options (from 7%), 50% seller options and 30% owned. That plan, together with its 70% optioned goal and Fitch tying an upgrade to fewer owned lots, makes Pulte a large and growing land-bank buyer.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving lighter. Long-term goal: control 70% of the pipeline through options, with about 3 years of owned land. Mix was 43% owned / 50% seller options / 7% land-banker options at YE2025, and the future goal is about 30% / 50% / 20%. Over 80% of optioned lots are with the underlying land seller, which Pulte calls more flexible and cheaper. Land-banker deals are struck parcel by parcel, each a discrete transaction. Deals are sourced locally and approved centrally against a risk-scored IRR hurdle (18-19% for low-risk projects, 25-30% for high-risk ones). In 2026 Pulte has re-underwritten options and walked away from some (optioned lots 148,663 at mid-2025 to 122,515 at Q3 2026).

lots.source_title: PulteGroup Q3 2026 earnings call slides (2026-10-22), 'Land Pipeline' slide
lots.note: Slide states '224K lots under control, with 55% held via option'; pct_optioned is 122,515 / 224,275. years_supply is our calculation: 224,275 lots / 27,796 trailing-12-month closings (Q4 2025 7,821 + Q1 2026 6,102 + Q2 6,997 + Q3 6,876); owned lots alone = about 3.7 years. Year-end 2025 (10-K): 234,632 controlled, 101,104 owned, 133,528 optioned (56.9%); by segment optioned/controlled: Northeast 7,202/10,873, Southeast 36,519/55,372, Florida 34,345/60,194, Midwest 21,660/31,979, Texas 19,162/35,382, West 14,640/40,832. Peak optioned was 148,663 at 2025-06-30; Pulte has since walked away from option contracts (optioned lots down about 26,000 in 15 months).

land_banking.description: Pulte's own breakdown of lots under control: options with land bankers were about 3% (2023), 6% (2024) and 7% (2025) of controlled lots; it uses 'established land-banking relationships' to option individual parcels, each as a discrete transaction. The stated future mix is about 50% seller options, about 20% land-banker options and about 30% owned.
land_banking.source_title: PulteGroup 2026 Investor Presentation, Raymond James conference (2026-03-02), slide 'Strategic and Efficient Land Option Strategy'
land_banking.note: 7% of 234,632 lots at 2025-12-31 is roughly 16,000 land-banked lots (our calculation from a rounded chart percentage). Reaching ~20% on a ~225,000-lot pipeline would mean ~45,000 land-banked lots, nearly 3x today. Counterparty names are not disclosed. Chart values read from slide text; the 3% label sits on the 2023 column.

land_banking.description: Option contracts with variable interest entities (typically land banks and seller-created entities): $416.5M of deposits and pre-acquisition costs against $3,254.1M remaining purchase price at 2026-09-30. Pulte is not the primary beneficiary of any; none are consolidated. Total options: $1,245.2M deposits, $9,436.4M remaining purchase price.
land_banking.source_title: PulteGroup 10-Q Q3 2026, Note 2 House and Land Inventory (R7)
land_banking.note: VIE option book was $436.3M deposits / $3,307.7M remaining price at 2025-12-31. Deposit write-offs from abandoned options: $23.1M in 9M 2026. Separately, $136.7M 'consolidated inventory not owned' includes land sold to third parties with a Pulte repurchase option.

profile.org_note: Four homebuilding segments (Mid Atlantic, North East, Mid East, South East) plus mortgage banking; segments roll up regions of several metro divisions run by Division Managers, with Market, Regional and Senior Regional Managers above them and Area Presidents over a segment-sized area (titles per NVR's 2016 release; a Jan 2026 posting seeks a Regional Manager for Columbus, Cincinnati and Dayton). No corporate land head is named: each division's General Manager of Land sources lot deals, regional managers carry land-acquisition responsibility, and the full Board approves lot and raw-land contracts above policy thresholds under its lot acquisition policy; finance and treasury sit in Reston under CFO and Treasurer Daniel Malzahn.
profile.summary: NVR builds under Ryan Homes, NVHomes and Heartland Homes in 37 metropolitan areas across 16 eastern and midwestern states plus Washington, D.C., with about 6,300 employees at year-end 2025. It is the original land-light builder: it generally does not develop land and buys finished lots from third-party developers under fixed-price lot purchase agreements with deposits of up to about 10%. At 30 September 2026 it controlled about 185,300 lots, roughly 176,000 of them under lot purchase agreements secured by about $1.03 billion of cash deposits, with only small positions in four joint ventures (about 7,850 lots) and land under development (about 1,450 lots). Headquarters moved in 2026 to 1900 Oracle Way, Suite 300, Reston, VA (previously 11700 Plaza America Drive).

financing.summary: NVR (Ryan Homes, NVHomes, Heartland Homes) is the purest land-light model among large US builders: it controls about 185,300 lots, of which about 176,000 (95%) sit under finished-lot purchase agreements (LPAs) with third-party developers, backed by about $1.03 billion of forfeitable cash deposits; it owns almost no land (one parcel of about 1,450 lots) and holds four minority land JVs. Its own balance sheet is net cash: $1.09 billion of homebuilding cash against a single $900 million 3.00% note due May 2030, an undrawn $300 million Bank of America revolver to March 2030 and an undrawn $150 million U.S. Bank mortgage repurchase line; Moody's rates it A3. It returns cash through buybacks ($1.82 billion in 2025, $1.23 billion in the first nine months of 2026) rather than buying land. For a land banker the opening is the developer side: NVR does not take land-bank options itself in any public source, but every lot it buys comes from a developer who must finance horizontal development, and NVR assigns its raw-land contracts (about 38,700 lots) to developers and signs LPAs with them. Deposit stress is rising (allowance up to $156 million on about 24,000 LPA lots), which points to developers and lot prices under strain in some of its markets.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light by design and in the company's own words: NVR generally does not develop land and buys substantially all finished lots under LPAs with forfeitable deposits (typically up to 10% of the lot price), so its exposure is limited to the deposit. Raw land it contracts for is normally assigned to a developer, who then sells NVR the finished lots under an LPA; it develops land itself only rarely (one parcel left, about 1,450 lots) and buys some lots through minority JVs. No numeric option target is stated; in practice about 95% of controlled lots are under LPAs.

lots.note: Owned = land under development only (about 1,450 lots, carrying value $21.8M); a further about 7,850 lots come from four minority JVs ($80.2M invested) and are in the total but in neither owned nor optioned. NVR does not report finished lots held in house inventory as a separate count. pct_optioned = 176,000/185,300. Years supply computed by us: 185,300 / trailing-12-month settlements of 20,009 (FY2025 21,915 minus 9M2025 16,247 plus 9M2026 14,341, from the 10-K and Q3 release). Excludes about 38,700 lots under raw-land contracts ($46.7M deposits, about $13M refundable). Trend: 162,400 (2024-12-31), 175,300 (2025-09-30), 180,100 (2025-12-31; Mid Atlantic 60,100, North East 19,000, Mid East 28,100, South East 72,900 per FY2025 10-K), 185,300 (2026-09-30).

profile.org_note: The Q3 2026 10-Q says Meritage has twelve homebuilding operating segments (one per state) rolled up into three reportable segments, West, Central and East, reviewed by CEO Phillippe Lord as chief operating decision maker; internally, region or area presidents (for example a Texas region, a Florida region and an Arizona area) run groups of the 23 division offices, but the company names none of them in filings or releases. Land deals start with division land VPs, who prepare a corporate approval package, and every deal goes to a corporate land acquisition committee of executive management and key operating leaders; deals above a set size also need Executive Chairman Steven Hilton, and the Board's Asset Management Committee reviews large land, JV and land-banking transactions. There is no named corporate land head or treasurer: CFO Hilla Sferruzza runs finance and capital markets, and the COO seat has been empty since May 2025.
profile.summary: Scottsdale-based public builder of entry-level and first move-up spec homes in 12 states and 25 markets; 15,026 homes closed in 2025. It held 77,625 lots at 31 December 2025 (55,861 owned, 21,764 under purchase or option contracts) and aims for a four-to-five-year supply. Management has said it still targets about 40% of lots off balance sheet against roughly 31% optioned at 30 September 2026 (third quarter 2026 call transcript), so there is stated room for more lot-option and land-bank financing.

financing.summary: Meritage is an investment-grade (BBB-/Baa3/BBB-), balance-sheet land owner: at September 30, 2026 it controlled 71,765 lots, 69% owned and 31% optioned, a 5.3-year supply, and it funds land from operating cash, $1.825 billion of unsecured notes and an undrawn $980 million revolver (cash $677 million, about $1.6 billion of total capacity). The mix has moved the wrong way for a land banker since 2024: owned share rose from 62% at year-end 2024 to 72% at year-end 2025 after the company walked from about 7,200 optioned lots in 2025, and the FY2025 10-K says its participation in land options is limited at this time. No land banker is named in any filing, but in Q1 2026 a new specific-performance structure appeared (consolidated real estate not owned, $126.7 million and 3,960 lots by Q3 2026, with $59.9 million booked as financing proceeds), which reads like a first land-bank-style financing with an undisclosed counterparty. With land spend cut about 40% year over year, $100 million a quarter of buybacks planned and $300 million of 5.125% notes due June 2027 (callable at par from December 6, 2026), there is real room for off-balance-sheet lot capital on roughly 49,000 owned lots, but management has not publicly set an option target.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most. The FY2025 10-K states a goal of a four-to-five-year lot supply, says the company is buying mainly undeveloped or partially developed land and developing it itself because finished lots are scarce, and says its participation in land options is limited at this time. Option contracts typically carry non-refundable deposits of 5% to 20% of purchase price, and land purchases are financed through working capital including corporate borrowings. No owned/optioned target is stated in the FY2025 10-K or the 2026 10-Qs. Mix by quarter from the company's analyst decks: 62% owned / 38% optioned at 12/31/2024 (85,613 lots), 72% / 28% at 12/31/2025 (77,625), 70% / 30% at 3/31/2026 (75,481), 69% / 31% at 6/30/2026 (73,233) and 9/30/2026 (71,765).

lots.source_title: 3Q26 Analyst Call slides, slide 9 (Land & Development Investment); Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 3
lots.note: Total (71,765), 69% owned / 31% optioned and 5.3 years supply are stated on the slide. The owned and optioned counts are derived, not stated: the Q3 2026 10-Q Note 3 gives 18,619 lots under committed purchase and option contracts plus 3,960 lots under specific-performance purchase contracts (22,579, which is 31% of 71,765), leaving 49,186 owned. A further 18,025 uncommitted lots under refundable contracts are not counted in the controlled total. At 12/31/2025 the 10-K states the split outright: 55,861 owned plus 21,764 committed option/purchase lots = 77,625.

land_banking.description: From Q1 2026 Meritage reports purchase contracts with a specific performance obligation, recorded on balance sheet as consolidated real estate not owned with a matching liability. It booked $59.9 million of proceeds from these liabilities as a financing cash inflow in Q1 2026. At 9/30/2026: 3,960 lots, $126.7 million of real estate not owned and $115.2 million of related liabilities. The filings do not call this land banking and name no counterparty.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-10-30), Notes 1 to 3 and financing cash flows
land_banking.note: None existed at 12/31/2025 (FY2025 10-K shows zero). Build-up: 3,161 lots / $65.2 million at 3/31/2026; $70.3 million liability at 6/30/2026; 3,960 lots / $126.7 million at 9/30/2026. Reading it as a land-bank-style financing is this researcher's interpretation of the accounting, not a company statement.

land_banking.counterparty: Not disclosed (various land sellers and development entities)
land_banking.description: Off-balance-sheet purchase and option contracts at 9/30/2026: 36,644 lots with a total purchase price of $2.83 billion secured by $170.8 million of cash deposits. Of these, 18,619 lots ($1.62 billion, $131.8 million of deposits) are committed and 18,025 lots ($1.21 billion, $39.0 million of deposits) are uncommitted and still in evaluation. None requires Meritage to buy; exposure is limited to deposits and capitalised pre-acquisition costs.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-10-30), Note 3 (lots under option table)
land_banking.note: The 10-Q says lots are acquired from various development entities under purchase and option agreements; no counterparty, land banker or program size is named. At 12/31/2025 the equivalent table showed 36,329 lots, $2.12 billion purchase price, $174.2 million deposits, of which option contracts with non-refundable deposits were 9,559 lots / $947.6 million.

Corporate head of land (chief land officer, SVP or VP of land, national land acquisition or land development): not publicly disclosed. No such officer appears in the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 proxy, the management-team page or any company release; the 10-K says only that the corporate management team leads land acquisition decisions through a corporate land acquisition committee whose members are not named.

profile.org_note: Three homebuilding areas (East, Central, West; also the 10-K reporting segments), each under an Area President who oversees roughly 5 to 9 divisions run by Division Presidents (Charlotte is styled a "region" under Charlotte Regional President Andrew Bodary); Financial Services is a fourth segment under Tawn Kelley. Divisions source land through their own VP Land Acquisition / VP Land Development (who report to the Division President), and deals are approved centrally by the Investment Committee chaired by Erik Heuser, Chief Corporate Operations Officer, with board approval above a set threshold; since 2026-07-24 the company is a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary and is to absorb Clayton Properties Group, but no post-merger field org chart is public.
profile.summary: National builder (Scottsdale, AZ) in 12 states and about 20 markets, selling entry-level, move-up and Esplanade resort-lifestyle homes, plus Yardly build-to-rent. At Q1 2026 it owned or controlled 75,626 lots, 51% off balance sheet, against a stated target of at least 65% controlled; it spent about $2.2 billion on land in 2025 and uses land banking (including an existing Kennedy Lewis land-bank agreement and a $3 billion Kennedy Lewis Yardly facility), seller financing and JVs. Berkshire Hathaway bought it for about $8.5 billion enterprise value (closed 2026-07-24); combined with Clayton Properties it is roughly the fourth-largest US homebuilding operation (about 23,000 closings in 2025), so land and capital decisions now sit inside a Berkshire balance sheet.

financing.summary: Taylor Morrison was a public builder moving to a land-lighter model until Berkshire Hathaway bought it for $72.50 a share in cash (about $6.8 billion equity, $8.5 billion enterprise value); the merger closed on 2026-07-24 and the company is now a wholly owned Berkshire subsidiary being combined with Clayton Properties Group. Its last public balance sheet (2026-03-31) showed $1.475 billion of senior unsecured notes (2028, 2030, 2032), an undrawn $1.0 billion Wells Fargo-agented revolver to December 2030, $787 million of land-secured project/seller debt and about $1.6 billion of liquidity. Off balance sheet it used land banking heavily: 10,002 for-sale lots ($1.79 billion purchase price) plus 4,476 build-to-rent lots ($980 million) sat in third-party land banks, and for-sale land-bank lots grew from 6,895 (end 2024) even as total controlled lots fell. Kennedy Lewis (manager of Millrose) is the only named land banker, with a $3 billion Yardly build-to-rent facility signed in July 2025 on top of an existing for-sale land-banking agreement. Room for another land banker is now an open question: the controlled share of lots had already slipped from 60% (Sept 2025) to 51% (March 2026) against a stated target of at least 65%, and the new parent holds roughly $350 billion of cash and Treasury bills and could fund land on balance sheet. Taylor Morrison stopped SEC reporting in August 2026, so no lot or debt data newer than 2026-03-31 is public.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving land-lighter until the buyout. The FY2025 10-K describes an asset-light approach that finances land through land banking arrangements, joint ventures, seller financing and option contracts, with the goal of raising the share of homebuilding lots controlled rather than owned. At its March 2025 Investor Day the company set a target of at least 65% of homebuilding lots controlled (alongside about 20,000 closings by 2028). Actual controlled share peaked at 60% (June and Sept 2025), then fell to 54% at year-end 2025 and 51% at 2026-03-31 as total lots dropped from about 85,000 to 75,626. Strategy under Berkshire ownership has not been publicly stated. Within the controlled bucket the mix shifted toward land banking: land-bank lots rose from 6,895 (2024-12-31) to 8,498 (2025-12-31) and 10,002 (2026-03-31), while option-contract lots and other controlled lots (single takedowns, JV share) fell from 42,540 to 28,942.

lots.note: Latest public quarter (company deregistered in August 2026 after the Berkshire buyout). total_controlled = owned + controlled homebuilding lots. Owned 36,682 = 15,732 undeveloped, 8,000 under development, 12,950 finished. Controlled 38,944 = 6,193 under land option purchase contracts, 10,002 under land banking arrangements, 22,749 other (single-transaction takedowns and the company's share of unconsolidated JV lots). Q1 2026 earnings release states 51% controlled and 6.2 years of supply on trailing-twelve-month closings, of which 3.0 years owned. Trend from earnings releases: 85,051 lots / 60% controlled (2025-06-30); 84,564 / 60% (2025-09-30); 78,835 / 54% (2025-12-31); 75,626 / 51% (2026-03-31). Build-to-rent (Yardly) land-bank lots (4,476) are reported separately and are not in these totals. Aggregate purchase price of assets under option contracts and land banking: $3.4 billion; land deposits on balance sheet: $388.3 million. Year-end comparison (FY2025 10-K inventory note): owned 36,009 and controlled 42,826 at 2025-12-31 (options 8,632; land banking 8,498; other 25,696) versus owned 36,718 and controlled 49,435 at 2024-12-31 (options 9,529; land banking 6,895; other 33,011).

ma.counterparty: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
ma.description: All-cash acquisition at $72.50 per share (about $6.8 billion equity value, $8.5 billion enterprise value, 24% premium). Agreement signed 2026-05-31; HSR waiting period expired 2026-07-06; stockholders adopted the agreement on 2026-07-22 (75.8 million votes for, 2.3 million against); closed 2026-07-24. Taylor Morrison is now a wholly owned Berkshire subsidiary and will be combined with Clayton Properties Group.
ma.map_impact: Ownership changes from public (TMHC) to subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway; no more SEC filings, so lot, debt and officer disclosures stop at mid-2026. Taylor Morrison (Builder 100 #6) and Clayton Properties Group (#12) become one Berkshire site-built platform: nearly 23,000 closings in 2025, 21 states, 52 markets, 700+ communities, described as the fourth-largest US homebuilding operation. Sheryl Palmer stays CEO and leads the integration from Scottsdale; brands (Taylor Morrison, Esplanade, Yardly) are kept. The post-closing Taylor Morrison board is Sheryl Palmer, Todd Merrill, Curt VanHyfte and Erik Heuser; the independent directors resigned. Land and finance decision rights may shift toward Berkshire/Clayton, and the need for third-party land banking may fall.

industry_deals.description: Berkshire Hathaway completed its purchase of Taylor Morrison on 2026-07-24 for $72.50 per share in cash, about $6.8B equity value and $8.5B enterprise value. Sheryl Palmer stays CEO and oversees integrating Taylor Morrison (including Esplanade, Yardly build-to-rent and Taylor Morrison Home Funding) with Berkshire's site-built builders in Clayton Properties Group (15 regional builders). Combined 2025 closings were nearly 23,000 across 21 states, 52 markets and 700+ communities.
industry_deals.map_impact: Rank 6 Taylor Morrison is no longer public and now shares an owner with rank 12 Clayton Properties Group. Berkshire says Taylor Morrison will lead a unified site-built operation, and Taylor Morrison's CMO told ResiClub (2026-08-20) that all of Clayton's site-built builders will roll up under Taylor Morrison while manufactured/modular stays with Clayton Homes; so the two rows effectively become one Berkshire platform of about 23,000 closings, the 4th largest US builder (level with NVR). Sheryl Palmer leads it. acquirer_builder_id is null because Berkshire itself is not a ranked builder; its ranked subsidiary is clayton-properties-group.

Whether Charlotte and Raleigh report to Steve Kempton: his bio names Florida and Atlanta only, although both divisions are in the East reporting segment.

profile.summary: KB Home (NYSE: KBH) is a large public homebuilder with about 50 markets in 11 states, built around a Built to Order model. It owned 57% and optioned 43% of its lots at FY2025 year end, after dropping 24,596 optioned lots that no longer met its underwriting, and it cut land spending in 2025 to buy back shares. In 2026 it entered Atlanta, said it will move its headquarters from Los Angeles to Tempe, AZ in spring 2027, and changed CEO. The CFO seat is open and the corporate land head retires at the end of November 2026, so land and finance contacts are changing.

financing.summary: KB Home (NYSE: KBH; FY ends Nov 30) finances land on its own balance sheet: in June 2025 its then-CFO said it uses 'extremely limited land banking or other off-balance sheet vehicles', and no land-bank counterparty is named in any 2025-2026 filing or release. At Aug 31, 2026 it owned or controlled 61,581 lots (37,129 owned, 24,452 optioned, ~40% optioned, down from 49% optioned at FY2024) after walking away from 24,596 controlled lots in FY2025 and 8,777 more in the first nine months of FY2026. Funding is a $1.2B unsecured revolver (Bank of America agent, due Nov 2030; $415M drawn at Q3 FY2026), a $360M unsecured term loan (Wells Fargo agent, due Nov 2029) and four unsecured note series totalling $1.34B, with the next maturity the $300M 6.875% notes due June 15, 2027; liquidity fell to $942M and debt-to-capital rose to 35.7% (net of cash ~33.9%, derived) versus a stated ~30% target, while buybacks continued ($175M in 9M FY2026). Room for a land banker: owned-lot share is ~60% and rising, leverage is above target with a 2027 maturity ahead, and the land chief (EVP Real Estate & Business Development Albert Praw) retires Nov 30, 2026 with the CFO seat filled only on an interim basis by the CEO since May 2026, so land-finance relationships are in transition.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, balance-sheet funded. 10-K: seeks to own or control land for the next three to five years of forecast production and a one- to three-year supply per product line per community; typically ties land up with small option payments or earnest-money deposits at pre-set prices, develops in smaller phases, assets generally 50-250 lots, and may sell or monetize land. Optioned share fell from 49% (Nov 2024) to 43% (Nov 2025) to 40% (Aug 2026) as KB cancelled options that no longer met underwriting. Management (Q2 2025 call) framed balance-sheet land funding with 'extremely limited land banking' as a transparency and cost advantage. Remaining purchase price on all option contracts at Aug 31, 2026: $358.3M (rest of 2026), $859.0M (2027), $297.3M (2028), $98.5M (2029), $4.0M (2030). Land spend (land + development + fees) was $2.84B FY2024, $2.61B FY2025, $1.79B in 9M FY2026 (West Coast 47%); West Coast holds $3.21B of the $5.98B inventory. Entered Atlanta organically in May 2026 (110 homesites).

lots.source_title: KB Home Q3 2026 investor presentation (2026-09-21)
lots.note: Owned/optioned from the deck's lot-position chart; total and 'approximately 60% owned / 40% under contract' confirmed in the Q3 FY2026 press release and 10-Q MD&A. By segment (total lots, 10-Q): West Coast 20,471; Southwest 10,165; Central 18,967; Southeast 11,978. 9,549 of the optioned lots carry deposits refundable at KB's discretion. Prior points: Nov 30, 2025 64,612 (37,137 owned / 27,475 optioned; segment split WC 20,750, SW 11,142, Central 20,614, SE 12,106 per FY2025 10-K); Nov 30, 2024 76,703 (51% owned). years_supply is derived (not company-stated): 61,581 lots / 11,116 trailing-12-month deliveries (3,619 in Q4 FY2025 + 7,497 in 9M FY2026).

Successor to Albert Z. Praw as corporate head of real estate / land: not named (retirement 8-K, 16 Nov 2026).
Capital markets head / head of land banking or land finance: no such role is published; corporate treasury and land approval are central functions (FY2025 10-K).

Job titles of the 20 published local land acquisition contacts are not on the contacts page; KB Home was recruiting VP / Director of Land Acquisition roles in 2026 (Fresno, Boise area, Fairfield CA per job-board search snippets) but does not name holders.
Atlanta (Georgia) land contact: none published on the Corporate Contacts page; Division President Bill Schmidt leads land acquisition there.
KB Home investor-relations governance/management pages are behind a bot check; not used.
Treasurer: Thad Johnson per 2026 Texas Comptroller records; no 2025-2026 KB Home filing or release names the Treasurer, so his current title is confirmed only by state records.
Regional president for Central segment / Texas: not publicly disclosed (Brett Dietz inferred from the Texas officer record only).
Regional president for Colorado: not publicly disclosed (Colorado division president Kevin McAndrews reports to an unnamed leader).
Regional president for Arizona (Phoenix, Tucson): not publicly disclosed.
Regional president for Washington (Seattle): not publicly disclosed.
Regional president for Southern California inland (Los Angeles/Ventura, Inland Empire): not publicly disclosed.
Successor corporate land head after Albert Praw retires on 30 Nov 2026: not publicly disclosed (also not on any 2026 state officer record seen).
Credit agreement (Bank of America agent, 12 Nov 2025) signature pages would show the Treasurer but could not be reached (sec.gov blocked curl; WebFetch truncates).

Division and regional land leaders (VP / Director of Land Acquisition, Land Development, Forward Planning): none confirmed. KB Home does not name them in press releases or filings, and per-market land searches were not run. Three HBA board listings give KB Home people without titles (Las Vegas, Tucson, Bay Area) and are recorded as affiliation-only leads.

Corporate land: Albert Z. Praw, EVP Real Estate and Business Development, gave notice on 16 November 2026 that he retires on 30 November 2026 and will advise on land relationships and transactions for up to a year (8-K filed 2026-11-16). Belongs in the corporate file; no successor named in the filing.

Regional structure: only four regional executives are named publicly (East Region; Northern California; Coastal Southern California; Las Vegas/Idaho). No regional president was found for Texas, Colorado, Arizona or Seattle. The last 'Central Regional President' named in a release was Larry Oglesby in December 2020 and is not carried here.
Who the regional presidents / regional general managers report to: not stated publicly (Robert McGibney ran operations as President and COO until he became CEO on 1 March 2026).
South Bay / Silicon Valley division president: none named since Kevin Kimball (last quoted May 2024). Regional General Manager Oren Hershkovich is quoted on South Bay communities in 2025 and 2026.
Fresno / Central California: no separate division president named; Fresno releases quote Oren Hershkovich and Madera releases quote Matt Sauls.
Boise: current division president uncertain (Stan Katanic last quoted October 2025; the April 2026 Idaho release quotes the regional general manager).
Charlotte and Raleigh: no 2026 confirmation of the division presidents (last company releases February and March 2025).

Dallas and Houston: both division presidents changed in 2026 without an appointment release; start dates and backgrounds of Ben Clark and Marc Tindall, and where Marcia Dillon and Brett Dietz went, were not found.
Phones and emails for division leaders: KB Home publishes only the general line 888-KB-HOMES.
Local business-journal, Builder / HousingWire and conference-speaker sources per market: not checked. They would most likely add land leaders and settle Boise, Charlotte and Raleigh.

M&A 2025-2026: none found. EDGAR 8-Ks since Jan 2025 show no Item 2.01 (acquisition) and the 2025-2026 press releases list no deal; the Atlanta entry (May 2026, 110 homesites, Whitley Meadows in Bethlehem, GA) was organic. KB was named as a possible takeover target in Barron's (June 2026), seen only in another agent's search snippet; no approach reported, so not listed.

Land-banking counterparties (Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon, Domain/DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton, Forestar): no public link to KB Home found in the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 10-Qs, earnings releases, the Q2 2025/Q1 2026/Q3 2026 call transcripts or one web search. The filings name no land financier or option counterparty.
Net debt-to-capital: not company-reported (gross debt-to-capital 35.7%; net ~33.9% derived from $2,109.1M debt, $159.0M cash, $3,801.5M equity).

Credit ratings from Moody's/S&P/Fitch: current levels and outlooks not confirmed from a primary source (agency pages paywalled; one search snippet claiming a July 2026 S&P downgrade could not be confirmed and is not used).
Revolver and term-loan lender-by-lender commitments: not publicly disclosed (signature pages and Schedule 1.1 not in the filed exhibits). LOC facility bank: not named.
Lot count split by option type (VIE vs non-VIE, land banker vs developer): not publicly disclosed; only dollar purchase prices and deposits.
JV partner names (other than KBHS partner GR Alliance) and JV locations outside California: not publicly disclosed.
Successor to Albert Praw (EVP Real Estate & Business Development) and a permanent CFO: not announced as of 2026-11-19.

profile.org_note: Six reportable homebuilding regions since Q1 2026 (Pacific Northwest, California, Desert, Mountain, Texas, East; Q3 2026 10-Q segment note), each a group of brand divisions; this replaced the FY2025 three-region layout (West, Mountain, East) after Woodside, Holt and Chesmar were merged in, and the CEO is the sole chief operating decision maker. Regional presidents run division operations (land, construction, sales) and report up to corporate in Denver; divisions source land through Division VPs of Land Acquisition, but every real estate acquisition must be approved by the real estate Asset Management Committee (CEO David Viger, CFO Robert Martin, the Chief Legal Officer, two Sekisui House, Ltd. representatives and at least one other corporate officer). No corporate land chief is published; treasury sits with VP, Treasurer Clare Wilson under the CFO. A sister company, North America Sekisui House, LLC (NASH, Arlington VA), invests in land and master-planned communities and is linked from shus.com, but is not part of Sekisui House U.S. in the filings.
profile.summary: Seventh- or eighth-largest US builder (11,712 closings and about $6.4 billion of revenue in 2025), wholly owned by Japan's Sekisui House and built on the former M.D.C. Holdings platform, selling in 14 states under Richmond American, Woodside, Holt, Chesmar, Hubble and SHAWOOD. It is land-heavy: 35,216 lots controlled at 2025-12-31, of which 28,728 owned and only 6,488 (about 18%) optioned, and the parent's FY2026-28 plan names 'land acquisition methods to enhance ROA' as a US priority while targeting 13,600 deliveries in 2028. It still files voluntarily with the SEC (may stop at any time), which is the main public window into its officers and debt.

financing.summary: Sekisui House U.S., Inc. (SHUS, the renamed M.D.C. Holdings) is a wholly owned, voluntary SEC filer that since January 2026 holds all four Sekisui House U.S. builders (Richmond American, Woodside/Hubble, Holt, Chesmar). It funds itself with $1.5 billion of legacy MDC senior notes (nothing due before January 2030), a $1.40 billion bank revolver led by U.S. Bank ($229 million drawn at September 30, 2026, used to pay down the intercompany lines from its parent) and retained equity of $5.5 billion; the Japanese parent (S&P BBB+, JCR AA) stands behind SH Residential Holdings' bank loans. The group owns most of its land: about 38,300 owned versus 7,900 optioned lots at mid-2026 (17% optioned), close to four years of supply against a stated two-to-three-year target, and no third-party land banker is named in any filing or parent presentation reviewed. The parent's current plan calls for 'land acquisition methods to enhance ROA', working down roughly 10,000 low-margin lots, and using sister company North America Sekisui House (NASH) master-planned communities for about 5,000 lots, so the room for an outside land banker is real but would compete with an in-house affiliate and a cheap balance sheet. Net homebuilding debt to capital is only about 23% (researcher's calculation), earnings are thin (Q3 2026 net loss of $1.7 million after $42 million of California impairments), and deliveries are guided down to 9,500 for 2026.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most of its land. In its own framing (FY2025 10-K) the builders buy finished lots or develop lots as needed, often control lots through option contracts backed by cash or letter-of-credit deposits, and keep a two-to-three-year land supply; every land purchase goes to a real estate Asset Management Committee that includes two Sekisui House, Ltd. representatives. The parent's Seventh Mid-Term Management Plan (March 2026, updated September 2026) adds three land themes: 'land acquisition methods to enhance ROA', a shift of land buying from entry-level toward move-up and elite product, and a reduction of low-margin lots; it also targets 20% 'collaboration' with sister master-planned-community developer NASH (13% in the prior plan). No stated owned/optioned percentage target was found.

lots.source_title: Sekisui House, Ltd. Financial Factbook, Second Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026 (2026-09-10), p.19 U.S. homebuilding 'Inventory quantity of lots and units'
lots.note: Parent-reported figures for the whole U.S. homebuilding business at the end of its Q2 FY2026; the U.S. builders report on a calendar year, so the date is taken as June 30, 2026 (inferred from matching revenue). Same table shows end of FY2025: 40,614 owned + 11,263 optioned = 51,877 (restated to new counting criteria), plus 4,363 unsold started homes at Q2. pct_optioned and years_supply are calculated here: 46,182 lots / 11,712 homes delivered in 2025 = 3.9 years (4.9 years on the revised 2026 plan of 9,500 deliveries). Cross-checks from SHUS's own SEC filings: FY2025 10-K MD&A showed 28,728 owned + 6,488 optioned = 35,216 at 2025-12-31 for SHUS before Chesmar and Holt were contributed (West 18,191; Mountain 9,992; East 7,033) with an option purchase price of about $535 million; the Q3 2026 10-Q note shows 6,775 lots under option at 2026-09-30 with $76.4M cash and $4.0M letter-of-credit deposits at risk. The owned-lot count at 2026-09-30 sits in the 10-Q MD&A, which could not be retrieved in this run (see gaps). The parent's September 2026 presentation rounds the land position to about 50,000 lots: about 26,000 in active communities, 19,000 in inactive communities and about 5,000 NASH collaboration lots.

land_banking.description: SHUS controls lots through option contracts with third-party sellers, secured by a cash deposit or letter of credit; its exposure is generally limited to the deposit. At September 30, 2026 it had $76.4M of cash deposits and $4.0M of letters of credit at risk on options for 6,775 lots. No seller, developer or land banker is named, and the company says it is not the primary beneficiary of any option counterparty.

land_banking.description: Sister company under Sekisui House that runs the U.S. master-planned community business (about 21,300 lots held at mid-2026). The parent counts about 5,000 'NASH collaboration lots' inside the roughly 50,000-lot U.S. homebuilding land position and is pushing SHUS home sales inside NASH communities: collaboration in seven states as of March 2026, with a 20% collaboration target for FY2026 to FY2028 versus 13% in the prior plan. In effect an in-house lot pipeline that competes with outside land bankers.

ma.counterparty: Chesmar Homes, LLC and Holt Group Holdings, LLC - sister companies contributed by parent SH Residential Holdings
ma.description: Second and final phase of the 'One Company' reorganization: the parent contributed Chesmar (Texas) and Holt (Oregon, Washington) to Sekisui House U.S., Inc. for no consideration. Their combined stand-alone revenue for the nine months to September 30, 2025 was $1.10B and net assets were $959.9M. Sekisui House, Ltd. confirmed completion on January 6, 2026.
ma.map_impact: From January 2026 all four builders report through Sekisui House U.S., Inc. In Q1 2026 the divisions were realigned into six homebuilding segments (Pacific Northwest, California, Desert, Mountain, Texas, East), so old brand-level reporting lines no longer match the org chart. Four directors joined the SHUS board on January 1, 2026 (Jennifer Whip, David Barclay, Yoshiyuki Kamiya, Shigeki Enomoto) and two left. The parent expects about $50M of annual G&A savings from closing and merging divisions and locations, so more division-level title changes are likely. The Builder 100 rank already counts the combined group (11,712 closings in 2025).
ma.source_title: Sekisui House U.S., Inc. Form 8-K dated December 31, 2025 (Items 2.01, 5.02)
ma.note: Completion notice: https://www.sekisuihouse.co.jp/company/financial/library/ir_document/2026/20260106-1e.pdf. Segment realignment: Q3 2026 10-Q segment note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/773141/000077314126000019/R9.htm). G&A savings figure: parent presentation of September 10, 2026 (https://www.sekisuihouse.co.jp/company/financial/library/ir_document/2026/2026_kessan/p20260910e.pdf).

Holdings for no consideration. MDC had been renamed Sekisui House U.S., Inc. on September 4, 2025. Woodside's Salt Lake City holding company and SH Services, LLC were slated to be absorbed; the parent says back-office and sales overlaps are being cut and divisions consolidated. profile.org_note: Five reporting segments per the FY2025 10-K and July 2026 10-Q (North; Mid-Atlantic; South = Arkansas, Florida, South Carolina, Texas; Mountain; Pacific); management runs President/COO Seth Ring -> Regional Presidents (named: Todd Callahan Pacific, Mark Bailey Utah/Mountain, Tom Murray Florida, Rob Paul Texas & Arkansas; North and Mid-Atlantic not public) -> Group Presidents -> Division Presidents, and the South segment is split across at least two regional presidents. No corporate land head is published: land is sourced by division and regional land VPs (e.g. VP Land Acquisition Dustin Bowersett) and approved up the line to the COO/CEO, while land financing (options, land banking, JVs) sits with CFO Gregg Ziegler and Treasurer Ryan McKenna.
profile.summary: Largest US luxury builder: 11,292 homes delivered for $10.8 billion of home sales revenue in FY2025 (year ends October 31) at a $960,000 average price; FY2026 guidance is 10,500 to 10,600 deliveries at about $1.0 million. At July 31, 2026 it controlled 75,486 lots (31,817 owned, 43,669 optioned, 58% optioned) across 471 selling communities; the FY2025 10-K counts 24 states plus D.C., and Arkansas (Buffington Homes) was added in 2026. Management says it turns first to seller financing, joint ventures and traditional options and uses land banking 'carefully and modestly': about 20% of FY2026 revenue comes from land-banked communities and about 30% of optioned lots are land-banked. The whole top team changed in twelve months (CFO Nov 2025, CAO Feb 2026, CEO Mar 2026, President/COO Jun 2026, plus a new Treasurer), so relationships are being reset.
