financing.summary: Toll Brothers is an investment-grade luxury builder (Moody's Baa2, S&P BBB, Fitch BBB+) that funds itself with cash flow, $1.75 billion of unsecured senior notes, a $650 million bank term loan and an undrawn $2.375 billion revolver; at July 31, 2026 it held $1.06 billion of cash and net debt to capital was 15.6%. It controls about 75,500 lots, of which about 58% are optioned rather than owned, mostly through land purchase contracts with sellers and developers ($8.16 billion aggregate purchase price, $872 million of deposits) and through 21 land development joint ventures. Its filings show it also uses third-party 'land bank programs' (cash-flow lines for sales to and repurchases from land bank programs appear from fiscal 2025), but the flows are small ($52 million of proceeds in fiscal 2025, $20 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026) and no land banker is named. Liabilities for consolidated inventory not owned have grown from $389 million (October 2024) to $857 million (July 2026), which shows growing use of structured, off-balance-sheet-style lot control. Room for a land banker exists but Toll is not capital-constrained: it has no notes due before March 2027, is buying back about $700 million of stock in fiscal 2026 and describes its direction as 'more asset-light'.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving toward land-light. Toll says it seeks option agreements to defer land purchases until closer to home delivery, and lists controlling land through options before taking title as a main way it improves capital efficiency; it also buys lots from land development joint ventures, which it calls more capital efficient but generally more expensive than outright purchases. No numeric optioned target is stated in the filings read; optioned share was about 55% at October 2024, 57% at October 2025 and 58% at July 2026.

lots.source_title: Toll Brothers FY2026 third quarter results press release (8-K exhibit 99.1)
lots.note: Release states about 75,500 lots owned and optioned, about 42% (31,800) owned; its home-sites table gives 31,817 owned and 43,669 optioned. About 18,100 owned lots were substantially improved. Years of supply is derived, not stated: total lots divided by fiscal 2026 delivery guidance midpoint (10,550 homes). Fiscal year-end comparison (10-K): about 76,100 lots at October 31, 2025, about 33,000 owned and 43,100 optioned. Q3 land spend was about $451.9 million for about 2,784 lots. Fiscal Q4 2026 results are due December 8, 2026.

land_banking.counterparty: Undisclosed land bank programs (land bankers not named in filings)
land_banking.description: Toll's cash flow statement carries two financing lines for land bank programs: proceeds from sales to land bank programs and payments for repurchases from them. Fiscal 2025: $52.1 million of proceeds and $91.5 million of repurchases. First nine months of fiscal 2026: $19.8 million of proceeds and $27.6 million of repurchases. The arrangements are treated as financings and the counterparties and program size are not disclosed.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: condensed consolidated statements of cash flows
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m is the nine-month fiscal 2026 proceeds figure. Fiscal 2025 figures are from the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/794170/000079417025000112/R7.htm), where both lines are zero for fiscal 2024 and 2023. The FY2025 10-K risk factors also say land financing may come indirectly through land banks or other land financing vehicles. No narrative description of the programs was found in the notes read.

land_banking.counterparty: Land sellers and developers under option / purchase contracts (not named)
land_banking.description: The bulk of Toll's optioned position is land purchase contracts. At July 31, 2026 the aggregate purchase price was $8.16 billion ($8.09 billion with unrelated parties, $76 million with unconsolidated entities) against $872.4 million of deposits; $847.7 million of the remaining cash required is already accrued. 326 of the contracts are with variable interest entities (aggregate price $7.53 billion, deposits $862.3 million); Toll is not the primary beneficiary of any.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: Commitments and Contingencies note (land purchase contracts)
land_banking.note: VIE contract figures are from the Inventory note of the same 10-Q (R9.htm). Accrued expenses include $856.9 million of 'liabilities related to consolidated inventory not owned' at July 31, 2026, up from $754.8 million at October 31, 2025 and $388.8 million at October 31, 2024 (10-Q R13.htm and FY2025 10-K R13.htm). The lots figure is total optioned lots from the Q3 release and includes lots optioned from joint ventures. Comparison: $7.54 billion aggregate price and $744.5 million deposits at October 31, 2025.

land_banking.counterparty: Toll's own land development joint ventures (partners not named)
land_banking.description: Toll sources finished lots from land development joint ventures it co-invests in. At July 31, 2026 it expected to buy about 8,600 more home sites from these ventures over several years at prices to be set later, on top of $76.1 million of contracted purchases from unconsolidated entities. It bought $117.4 million of land from unconsolidated entities in the first nine months of fiscal 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended July 31, 2026: land purchase contracts details
land_banking.note: FY2025 10-K: the land development JVs owned about 28,900 home sites at October 31, 2025, of which 832 were under contract to Toll; expected further purchases were then about 8,800 sites.

ma.description: Toll bought substantially all the assets and operations of Buffington Homes of Arkansas, a private builder based in Fayetteville founded in 2010 and described as the largest luxury builder in northwest Arkansas. The deal brought nine active or coming-soon communities and about 1,500 home sites owned or controlled. Announced April 21, 2026; closed May 2026. Price not disclosed; accounted for as an asset acquisition and not material. Builder Advisor Group (Tony Avila) advised the seller.
ma.map_impact: Adds a new market (Fayetteville/Bentonville) and a new state, Arkansas. Founding partners Clay Carlton and Mike Lamberth stay on and focus on land acquisition and development, so they are the land contacts for northwest Arkansas; Buffington's senior leadership and employees joined Toll. Adds about 1,500 lots (about 2% of Toll's total); no change to Toll's rank. Buffington should be removed or marked as acquired if it appears as a separate builder.

ma.note: Closing month is from the Acquisition note of the July 31, 2026 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/794170/000079417026000102/R8.htm); the exact closing day is not disclosed. after_ranking is set true because closing was in May 2026, although the announcement (April 21) came before the ranking was published. This is Toll's 16th builder acquisition since 1995 and its first since Rialto Homes in 2022.

ma.counterparty: Kennedy Wilson

profile.summary: Top-10 public builder focused on affordable and entry-level homes: 10,387 new homes delivered and $4.1 billion of revenue in 2025, in 16 states and 45-plus markets under the Century Communities and Century Complete (online, finished-lot) brands. It held 60,916 lots at year-end 2025, 57.1% owned and 42.9% optioned, down from 80,632 a year earlier after walking away from contracts, and spent about $1.2 billion on land and development in 2025. Growth is by buying local builders for their lot pipelines: HistoryMaker Homes (Dallas-Fort Worth, October 2026, with an ongoing land-development relationship with its sister company Jabez Development) followed Anglia Homes and Landmark Homes of Tennessee in 2024.

financing.summary: Century Communities (NYSE: CCS) funds itself with two $500M senior unsecured notes series (3.875% due 2029, 6.625% due 2033), a $1.2B senior unsecured revolver agented by U.S. Bank (upsized and extended to November 2030 on 2026-09-30) and retained equity of about $2.6B; mortgage repurchase lines fund Inspire Home Loans and secured bank construction loans fund the Century Living apartment arm. It held 60,969 lots at 2026-09-30, 45.1% controlled through option contracts with land sellers and developers, backed by only about $85M of deposits. Management said on the Q3 2026 call that it uses land banking only on a very limited basis, does not cross-collateralize deals, and is moving toward lower-deposit control structures; no land banker is named in the filings or releases read. Leverage is rising: revolver borrowings went from $51.5M at year-end 2025 to $456.0M at 2026-09-30, net homebuilding debt to net capital went from 25.9% to 34.9%, and the roughly $160M HistoryMaker Homes purchase on 2026-10-07 was funded on the revolver. Management's stated priority is to hold or reduce debt to capital over the next couple of quarters, which is the opening for off-balance-sheet lot financing, particularly for the expanded Dallas-Fort Worth pipeline.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning toward options. The FY2025 10-K lists 'favoring lot option contracts to optimize returns and manage our risk to land holdings' as a strategic priority and says land is generally bought for cash, in bulk or through option contracts; no percentage target or years-of-supply target is stated. Local management sources land and the corporate office approves acquisitions above set limits. Century Communities brand lots range from entitled land needing development to finished lots; Century Complete typically buys lots ready for permits. In 2025 the company cut its pipeline hard: controlled lots fell 41.8% (44,876 to 26,116) and total lots fell from 80,632 to 60,916, with $11.2M of option-termination charges. Controlled lots have since grown again to 27,496 (45.1%) at 2026-09-30.

lots.source_title: Century Communities Q3 2026 results press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2026-10-28)
lots.note: Company terms are 'owned' (54.9%) and 'controlled' (45.1%). Year-ago: 62,239 total, 36,483 owned, 25,756 controlled. Recent path: 80,632 (2024-12-31), 60,916 (2025-12-31), 58,537 (2026-03-31), 60,128 (2026-06-30). years_supply is derived, not company-stated: 60,969 lots divided by 9,991 trailing-twelve-month home deliveries (10,387 in FY2025 less 7,357 in 9M 2025 plus 6,961 in 9M 2026). Figures are before the HistoryMaker Homes acquisition of 2026-10-07; the HistoryMaker lot count was not disclosed. Segment-level lot table is an image in the 10-K and was not readable.

Management cited more than 27,000 optioned lots secured by about $85M of deposits (about 3% of equity) at 2026-09-30.

profile.org_note: Fifteen markets, each an operating segment, roll up into two reportable segments (East, Central); management uses two named regional presidents (Texas: Lindsay Motley; Florida and Tennessee: Dan Fitzpatrick), while Atlanta, the Carolinas, Phoenix and Denver have no published regional president and appear to report to COO Ryan Lewis (inferred). Each division has its own land acquisition and development staff, but corporate (Alpharetta) gives final approval on every land acquisition and allocates capital; the corporate land head is SVP of Land Acquisition & Strategy Thad DiGiuro, and financing runs through CFO/CAO Zack Sawyer with VP and Corporate Controller Michael Escarra (no treasurer is named). The CEO, CFO and COO are the chief operating decision makers. Published investor contact: investor.relations@ashtonwoods.com.
profile.summary: Largest private US homebuilder by closings (10,080 homes closed in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026; average price $355,000), building in 15 Sunbelt and Southeast markets across 8 states under Ashton Woods Homes (design-led move-up) and Starlight Homes (entry-level; 57% of orders in the quarter ended August 31, 2026 per HousingWire). It is already very land-light: 54,317 lots controlled at August 31, 2026, of which only 12.2% (6,650) were owned and 87.8% (47,667) were under purchase and option contracts, with about a 5.5-year supply at fiscal year-end. Privately held (99% by Little Shots Nevada L.L.C., family trusts linked to Great Gulf Group) but reports like a public company because of its senior notes, and entered Denver in 2025 as its newest market.

financing.summary: Ashton Woods USA L.L.C. (Ashton Woods Homes and Starlight Homes) is a private, family-owned builder with public Rule 144A notes, so it posts 10-K/10-Q/8-K-style reports on its own site. It is already one of the most option-heavy builders: 87.8% of its 54,317 controlled lots were under purchase or option contracts at Aug 31, 2026, backed by $641.0M of nonrefundable deposits against about $4.0B of remaining purchase price. Corporate funding is three unsecured notes series ($1.2B, first maturity Aug 2029) plus an undrawn $550M Wells Fargo-agented unsecured revolver (Nov 2029); liquidity was $707.1M. Land-banking counterparties are not named in any filing: the company describes sale-and-option-back deals with unnamed investors ($601.2M of real estate not owned), a fast-growing set of investor-funded lot purchase agreements (three at May 31, 2026, ten at Aug 31, 2026), and fifteen lot purchase agreements with affiliates of its owner families. Room for a land banker is in displacing or adding to those unnamed providers rather than converting owned land, since only 6,650 lots are owned.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light by design. The company's stated approach is a 'strategic focus on optioned lots' that keeps unused inventory dollars off the balance sheet (88% optioned at Nov 30, 2025; 87.8% at Aug 31, 2026), buying land only after entitlement. The annual report frames it as a balance between land owned and developed for its own use and lots controlled through option contracts; no numeric optioned-lot target is stated. Its risk factors say it relies on 'land banking' or 'off-balance sheet' arrangements and would be at a disadvantage if they were not available on satisfactory terms.

lots.source_title: Ashton Woods USA L.L.C. Quarterly Report, Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026; not filed with the SEC, posted on company IR site)
lots.note: Lot counts and 87.8% are as stated in the report. years_supply 5.3 is computed here: 54,317 lots / 10,212 trailing-twelve-month closings (FY2026 10,080 + Q1 FY27 2,191 - Q1 FY26 2,059). The company's own stated figure at May 31, 2026 was about 5.5 years (0.6 owned, 4.9 controlled) on 55,718 lots (6,466 owned, 49,252 under contract). Owned 6,650 = 4,487 finished lots + 2,163 lots in land under development or held for future development; a further 3,886 homes under construction or completed are not counted as lots. By segment: East 23,636 controlled (2,871 owned, 20,765 optioned); Central 30,681 (3,779 owned, 26,902 optioned). A year earlier (Aug 31, 2025): 57,973 controlled, 8,662 owned, 49,311 optioned (85.1%). In the three months to Aug 31, 2026 it bought 2,587 lots for $266.6M and spent $75.5M on land development.

land_banking.description: Ashton Woods sells land it owns to investors and concurrently takes a lot purchase option back; because the repurchase is treated as a financing under ASC 606, the lots stay on its balance sheet as real estate not owned. $601.2M of real estate not owned and $457.4M of related liabilities (net of $143.8M cash deposits) at Aug 31, 2026.
land_banking.source_title: Ashton Woods USA L.L.C. Quarterly Report, Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026; not filed with the SEC, posted on company IR site)
land_banking.note: Counterparties are not identified in any company report. Essentially flat versus May 31, 2026 ($601.4M real estate not owned, $444.9M liabilities, $156.6M deposits). Deposits equal roughly 24% of the recorded real estate. No specific-performance obligation; deposits are forfeited if lots are not taken.

land_banking.counterparty: Not publicly named (investors who buy lots the company identifies)
land_banking.description: Classic land-bank structure in the company's words: it identifies lots, finds an investor to buy them, then options them back in staged takedowns for a nonrefundable deposit. Ten such lot purchase agreements (one with owner-family affiliates) were consolidated under ASC 470-40 at Aug 31, 2026: $139.8M real estate not owned and $109.3M of liabilities net of $30.5M deposits.
land_banking.source_title: Ashton Woods USA L.L.C. Quarterly Report, Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026; not filed with the SEC, posted on company IR site)
land_banking.note: Up from three agreements, $90.3M real estate not owned and $66.9M liabilities (net of $23.4M deposits) at May 31, 2026, so seven new consolidated investor arrangements were added in the June to August 2026 quarter. Only arrangements where the company judges itself economically compelled to buy are recorded here; other investor-funded options sit off balance sheet and are not separately quantified.

land_banking.counterparty: Affiliates of the owner families behind Little Shots Nevada L.L.C. (called 'the Investors' in the reports)
land_banking.description: Related-party lot banking: fifteen lot purchase agreements with affiliates of the five families that own 99% of Ashton Woods. Initial deposits were 20% to 30% of the purchase price, with no specific-performance requirement; 3,496 lots remained to be purchased for $106.3M at Aug 31, 2026. Four of the agreements are recorded as real estate not owned.
land_banking.source_title: Ashton Woods USA L.L.C. Quarterly Report, Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended Aug 31, 2026; not filed with the SEC, posted on company IR site)
land_banking.note: At May 31, 2026 it was thirteen agreements, 3,595 lots and about $114.3M (FY2026 annual report). The five families are those related to Elly Reisman, the Estate of Norman Reisman, Bruce Freeman, Seymour Joffe and Harry Rosenbaum. Amounts overlap with the two rows above where the agreements are consolidated.

land_banking.counterparty: Not publicly named (all land sellers, developers and investors under purchase and option contracts)
land_banking.description: Whole option book at Aug 31, 2026: 47,667 lots under purchase and option agreements. Unconsolidated agreements carried $3.2B of remaining purchase price against $467.7M of cash deposits; agreements recorded under ASC 606 or ASC 470-40 carried a further $944.6M against $174.3M of deposits. Total nonrefundable deposits were $641.0M and the remaining purchase price under option agreements with nonrefundable deposits was $4.0B.

The filings do not split the book between land-banker, developer and land-seller options, and name no counterparty. Deposits average roughly 15% of remaining purchase price on the unconsolidated book and 18% on the consolidated book. The first three rows are subsets of this one.

profile.org_note: Clayton Properties Group (CPG) is the site-built arm of Clayton Home Building Group, which sits under Clayton Homes (CEO Kevin Clayton), a wholly owned Berkshire Hathaway company. Clayton Home Building Group CEO Keith Holdbrooks and COO Colt Davis (Chairman of CPG, Inc.) sit above CPG; Mike Rutherford is President of CPG, Inc. and leads its acquisitions. Each acquired brand keeps its own leadership (brand CEO/president, division or market presidents and its own land team, e.g. Summit's VP of Land & Development and Elite's VP of Land Acquisition and Development), so land is bought brand by brand. No CPG-level head of land or treasury is published; group finance sits with Clayton CFO Jim Stariha, and Clayton set up an in-house land bank (about $182 million, reported January 2024). Since 24 July 2026 Taylor Morrison CEO Sheryl Palmer oversees integrating CPG with Taylor Morrison, and several CPG brand sites say they will join Taylor Morrison in 2027, so land and finance decisions are likely moving to Taylor Morrison's team (inference).
profile.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's site-built homebuilder: about 10,000 homes in 2025 (9,953 closings, #12 on the 2026 Builder 100) through roughly 13 to 15 acquired regional brands in about 17 states, with about 67,300 homesites owned and controlled and a $1.2 billion backlog at end-2025. It is funded inside Berkshire (no public debt) and keeps buying builders (McGuinn Homes, July 2026). Berkshire bought Taylor Morrison in July 2026 and is merging the two into one site-built platform under Sheryl Palmer, so CPG's land strategy is likely to follow Taylor Morrison's, which already uses third-party land banks.

financing.summary: Clayton Properties Group (CPG) is the site-built division of Clayton Homes, a wholly owned Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary. It has no public debt, no ratings and no disclosed bank facility; it is funded inside Berkshire, whose insurance and other businesses held $352.3 billion of cash and Treasury bills at 30 Sep 2026, so capital is not a constraint and a land banker's pitch here is balance-sheet efficiency, not liquidity. Berkshire discloses one land number: about 67,300 homesites owned and controlled at 31 Dec 2025 (about 66,000 a year earlier), with no owned versus optioned split. The only public land-banking item for CPG itself is a January 2024 trade report that Clayton set up an in-house land bank to take about $182 million of land obligations off its nine builders; no outside land banker has been named for CPG. The picture changed on 24 Jul 2026: Berkshire bought Taylor Morrison for cash, and Taylor Morrison's CEO Sheryl Palmer is to integrate it with CPG into one site-built platform (about 23,000 closings in 2025). Taylor Morrison already uses third-party land banks (10,002 homebuilding lots with a $1.79 billion aggregate purchase price at 31 Mar 2026, counterparties unnamed in its filings), so land-finance decisions for the CPG builders may move to Taylor Morrison's team in Scottsdale (the last point is an inference from the stated leadership, not a company statement).
financing.land_strategy: Not stated by the company. Berkshire reports CPG's homesites as one 'owned and controlled' figure, so the mix is not public: treat as mixed / undisclosed. A January 2024 trade report, citing one unnamed senior executive, said the aim was an NVR-style 'asset-light' model using an in-house land bank. No target percentage has been published. Since July 2026 the site-built builders are being unified under Taylor Morrison's management, whose own last 10-K says it is working to raise the share of lots controlled through options, seller financing, joint ventures and land banking.

Owned vs optioned split: not publicly disclosed. years_supply is my arithmetic, not a company figure: 67,300 homesites / about 10,000 site-built homes in 2025 (same page of the 10-K). Prior year, from the 2024 10-K: about 66,000 homesites, 18 states, backlog about $1.46 billion. Latest quarter: Berkshire's 10-Qs give no homesite count; the Q3 2026 10-Q shows Berkshire-wide real estate inventory (cost of developing housing communities and site-built homes) of $2,361 million at 31 Dec 2025, before Taylor Morrison, and $10,586 million at 30 Sep 2026 including it. Total here is CPG only and excludes Taylor Morrison (75,626 lots owned and controlled at 31 Mar 2026 per its own 10-Q) and McGuinn Homes.

ma.counterparty: Taylor Morrison Home Corporation (bought by CPG's parent, Berkshire Hathaway)
ma.description: Berkshire agreed on 31 May 2026 to buy Taylor Morrison for $72.50 a share in cash (about $6.8 billion equity, $8.5 billion enterprise value) and closed on 24 Jul 2026. Berkshire says Taylor Morrison CEO Sheryl Palmer will oversee integrating Taylor Morrison's brands with the site-built operations that make up Clayton Properties Group, and that Taylor Morrison 'will lead' a unified site-built operation.
ma.map_impact: Biggest change to this map. CPG (Builder 100 rank 12, 9,953 closings) and Taylor Morrison (rank 6, 12,997) become one Berkshire platform: nearly 23,000 closings in 2025, 21 states, 52 markets, 700+ communities, described as the fourth-largest US builder. Leadership of the combined business sits with Taylor Morrison's management in Scottsdale, so the people to call on for CPG land and finance are likely to shift from Clayton in Tennessee to Taylor Morrison's land and finance team (inference from the stated leadership). Trade press reports the Clayton site-built builders will roll up under Taylor Morrison while factory-built stays with Clayton, with brand decisions still open. Financing: Taylor Morrison brings an existing third-party land-banking programme, $1,475 million of senior notes and a $1 billion Wells Fargo-led revolver into a parent that pays cash.
ma.source_title: Berkshire Hathaway Completes Acquisition of Taylor Morrison (news release, July 24, 2026)
ma.note: Role is 'Merger' because CPG is neither buyer nor target: its parent bought a sister company that is being combined with it. The roll-up and brand-review detail is Reported (ResiClub, 20 Aug 2026, quoting Taylor Morrison's CMO), not from the release. The release says CPG is 'a collection of 15 established regional and local homebuilders'; Berkshire's 2025 10-K and Clayton's site say nine builders, and Clayton's site lists 13 brands (the nine plus Berkeley Building Co., Elite Homes, Legacy Homes and Silverthorne Homes).

ma.counterparty: McGuinn Homes (South Carolina)
ma.description: Mungo Homes, a CPG builder, announced the acquisition of McGuinn Homes, a 40-year-old builder active in Aiken, Columbia, Greenville, Hilton Head and Sumter SC and Augusta and Savannah GA. McGuinn has about 75 staff and is projected to close nearly 800 homes in 2026. Terms not disclosed. Whelan Advisory advised McGuinn.
ma.map_impact: McGuinn Homes is itself on the 2026 Builder 100 (rank 65, 993 closings in 2025), so that row becomes part of Mungo / CPG / Berkshire and founder Wade McGuinn's son Kelly McGuinn stays with Mungo in a senior operating role. Adds Augusta GA and Aiken SC to Mungo's footprint and deepens Columbia, Greenville, Savannah and Hilton Head. Mungo alone closed more than 3,700 homes on $1.4 billion of revenue in 2025. Trade press says build-to-rent has at times been most of McGuinn's business, which fits Taylor Morrison's Yardly rental arm.
ma.source_title: Mungo Homes Acquires McGuinn Homes, Expands Southeast Presence (Mungo Homes news, July 2, 2026)
ma.note: Status left as 'Announced' because the release announces 'the acquisition' without stating a closing date; its wording reads as completed and ResiClub (8 Jul 2026) describes McGuinn as acquired. Lots acquired and price: not disclosed. The build-to-rent point and McGuinn's closings history (309 in 2022, 337 in 2023, 581 in 2024, 993 in 2025) are Reported (ResiClub). Verifier 2026-11-19: status Announced -> Closed (HousingWire/The Builder's Daily, 2026-07-01, says Clayton Home Building Group confirmed Mungo acquired McGuinn); map_impact corrected: the source says founder Wade McGuinn's son Kelly stays with Mungo, not that Wade joins.

financing.summary: M/I Homes funds land almost entirely on its own balance sheet: cash of $620.6M, an undrawn $900M unsecured revolver (PNC agent, matures September 2030) and just two unsecured notes series totalling $700M (4.95% due February 2028, 3.95% due February 2030). Homebuilding debt-to-capital was 18% and company-stated net debt-to-capital 2% at September 30, 2026; cash plus revolver availability ($808.9M after letters of credit) is about $1.43B (our sum, not a company-reported figure). It controls 48,934 lots, 52% under option or contingent purchase contracts with unnamed land sellers ($1.7B aggregate purchase price, $78.4M of deposits), and it developed over 80% of its lots itself in 2025. No land banker is named in its filings, and on the Q3 2026 call the CEO said the company does virtually no land banking and prefers to control its land, while conceding that perhaps it should have. Room for a land banker is therefore a greenfield conversation rather than a share-take from a rival: $1.85B of lots and land sits on balance sheet, the company keeps buying back stock ($250M authorisation, August 2026), and the $400M 2028 notes (callable at par) are the next financing decision.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owner-developer. The 10-K states a target of roughly a three-to-five-year lot supply, acquired mainly through contingent purchase agreements and options with minimum cash down and takedowns where available; every purchase is approved by a corporate land acquisition committee. Over 80% of lots were developed internally in 2025. At September 30, 2026 it owned 23,425 lots (about 2.5 years, per the earnings call) and had 25,509 under contract, about five years in total. At year-end 2025 owned lots were 10,487 developed, 6,361 under development and 8,804 undeveloped. Land spend was $523.7M purchases plus $645.6M development in 2025, and $345.5M plus $413.5M in the first nine months of 2026. Management says it does virtually no land banking or other off-balance-sheet land structures, will not start selling land, and will be more careful on new deals.

profile.org_note: Three homebuilding reporting segments (Southeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest; the 10-Q says the company is organised mainly by region) sit over roughly 27 local divisions, each led by a Division President who, per the June 2026 release, now reports up to COO Clint Szubinski; no segment-level regional president is publicly named (Liesel Cooper's 2024 regional role over Colorado and the ex-Crescent divisions is unconfirmed since), and Beazer (acquired 2026-10-20) has not yet been placed in a segment. Land deals start with divisional VPs of Land (who report to the Division President with a dotted line to a Regional VP of Land, e.g. Matt Childers for Texas/Colorado/Arizona, and to SVP of Land Batey McGraw) and are approved by the six-person Asset Management Committee (CEO Patrick Zalupski, CFO Anabel Ramsay, McGraw, National President Doug Moran, SVP Finance Michelle Murrhee, GC Robert Riva), with deals of $75M or more going to the Board and financing going to land bankers, where 49%-owned DF Capital holds a right of first offer.
profile.summary: Builder 100 #14 before the deal; after closing the ~$2.2B all-cash purchase of Beazer Homes on 2026-10-20 it calls itself the sixth-largest US builder by revenue, in 26 of the top 50 MSAs. It runs a stated 100% land-light model: 52,574 lots controlled through finished-lot option and land bank option contracts at 2026-09-30 (before Beazer; $490M of lot deposits), and its deal deck showed about 87,900 pro forma lots, 78% optioned. At the Beazer closing it sold pre-acquisition Beazer land to Millrose for a $572.1M land bank facility (the deck had named Kennedy Lewis as the buyer), and it has said it will deleverage over 18 to 24 months and drop Beazer land deals that miss its return thresholds.

financing.summary: Dream Finders is very land-light: it does not report owned lots at all and controls its pipeline (52,574 lots at 2026-09-30) through finished-lot and land bank option contracts, and a related-party fund (DF Residential III, run by 49%-owned DF Capital) holds a right of first offer on its land bank deals. On 2026-10-20 it closed a $2.2B all-cash purchase of Beazer Homes, and Millrose Properties (Kennedy Lewis) financed about $1.07B of it: roughly $580M to land-bank about 7,000 Beazer homesites and $500M of 12% Series B preferred. Corporate funding is a Bank of America-led unsecured revolver (about $1.7B of commitments, $1.2B drawn before the deal), $600M of its own notes due 2028 and 2030, and $650M of assumed Beazer notes due 2031 and 2032 now being exchanged into Dream Finders paper. Leverage is the constraint (48.1% net homebuilding debt to net capitalization before Beazer, with $675M of 12% preferred on top) and management calls deleveraging a key priority; for a competing land banker the openings are Beazer's remaining owned land and deals outside DF Residential III's criteria, but Millrose now sits in both the land and the capital structure.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light. The company calls it an 'asset-light lot acquisition strategy': it generally avoids owning land under development and buys finished lots just in time through finished lot option contracts and land bank option contracts, with deposits averaging about 10% of the land price and option fees paid on the land banker's outstanding capital. No numeric target is stated. The 2026-08 merger presentation showed the combined Dream Finders plus Beazer position as 78% optioned and 22% owned.

lots.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Q3 2026 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1 to 2026-10-29 8-K)
lots.note: Dream Finders reports only a 'controlled lot pipeline' (lots under finished lot and land bank option contracts); owned lot counts are not disclosed in its 10-K, 10-Q or earnings release, so total, owned and percent optioned are left blank. Standalone and pre-Beazer. Down from 63,121 at 2025-12-31 (Southeast 23,616; Mid-Atlantic 23,517; Midwest 15,988) and 63,509 at 2026-06-30; management said it is terminating option deals that miss return thresholds and expects abandonment charges in Q4 2026. Against 2026 guidance of about 9,250 closings the pipeline is roughly 5.7 years (computed, not stated). Beazer adds 24,489 controlled lots (2026-06-30; 60.0% of its 23,083 active lots optioned). The merger presentation put the combined position at about 87,944 lots, 78% optioned and 22% owned.

land_banking.description: At the Beazer closing, DFH sold certain pre-acquisition Beazer land assets to Millrose and took back options to buy the homesites over time, on terms DFH says match its existing land bank option contracts. DFH received $572.1M, used to redeem Beazer's $350M 7.250% notes due 2029, repay Beazer's revolver and pay deal costs.
land_banking.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Subsequent Events note
land_banking.note: Lot count is Millrose's figure (about 7,000 homesites, more than half finished, weighted average life about 2.5 years); Millrose reports about $580M funded net of option deposits, plus an $8.0M commitment fee to Millrose (Millrose Q3 2026 release and deck). DFH's 8-K names the provider as Millrose and/or affiliates, including Kennedy Lewis Investment Management. DFH's pro forma exhibit shows larger gross sale figures (about $683M of proceeds on land carried at about $794M, plus about $44M of deposits); not reconciled here. Option fee rate: not disclosed.

land_banking.description: Commitment letter signed with the Beazer merger agreement: Kennedy Lewis and/or affiliates committed an $800M land bank facility to fund part of the merger consideration, conditioned on the merger, the preferred investment and permanent or bridge debt. During the earlier hostile pursuit Kennedy Lewis gave DFH a 'highly confident' letter for land bank financing.
land_banking.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Form 8-K (Beazer merger agreement and financing commitments)
land_banking.note: Committed size $800M; amount actually funded at closing was $572.1M through Millrose (managed by Kennedy Lewis). Whether the unused balance of the commitment remains available is not disclosed. Verifier 2026-11-19: removed the claim that Kennedy Lewis was DFH's land-banking adviser from February 2026; neither the 8-K nor DFH's press release supports it (the release lists Goldman Sachs, BofA Securities, Zelman and Vestra as financial advisers and Kennedy Lewis only as the source of a highly confident letter, https://investors.dreamfindershomes.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/58/dream-finders-homes-releases-investor-presentation-to).

land_banking.counterparty: DF Residential III, LP (managed by DF Capital Management)
land_banking.description: Related-party land bank fund in its investment period. It holds an exclusive right of first offer on DFH land bank financing projects that meet its criteria. DFH had $47.9M of lot deposits with the fund controlling 3,631 lots. DFH and key executives committed $57.6M to the fund, 55.9% contributed.

ma.counterparty: Beazer Homes USA, Inc.
ma.description: All-cash merger at $33.50 per share, about $878.4M of equity consideration and about $2.2B enterprise value; Beazer is now a wholly owned subsidiary and delisted. Began as private approaches from 2026-02-05, went public and hostile on 2026-05-11 at $25.75, raised to $32.00 on 2026-07-08, and signed at $33.50 on 2026-08-06. Funded by $675M of Series B preferred, a $572.1M Millrose land bank facility, revolver borrowings and cash.
ma.map_impact: Beazer stops being a separate builder: fold its row under Dream Finders. Combined company is about 12,800 CY2025 closings and $6.6B revenue (sixth-largest listed US builder by revenue, per DFH), about 520 communities in 26 markets, adding California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware and deepening Maryland, Texas, Florida, the Carolinas, Georgia and Arizona. Beazer's nine directors (including Allan Merrill) resigned and were replaced by DFH's board; Beazer's officers stayed in place at closing; the integrated reporting structure for its land and division leaders has not been published. Beazer's Atlanta treasury relationships (JPMorgan revolver, 2029 notes) are gone; about 7,000 Beazer homesites moved to Millrose, and DFH has flagged option terminations and abandonment charges in Q4 2026.
ma.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Form 8-K (completion of Beazer acquisition)
ma.note: Combined figures from the 2026-08-07 merger presentation and 2026-10-20 closing release. Whether the Beazer brand continues is not stated; DFH plans to move Beazer communities to Dream Finders floor plans. DFH targets more than $100M of annual cost synergies and a return to pre-deal leverage in 18 to 24 months.

industry_deals.description: Dream Finders completed its all-cash purchase of Beazer on 2026-10-20 at $33.50 per share, about $2.2B enterprise value; Beazer was delisted from the NYSE. Dream Finders expects $100M+ of annual run-rate cost synergies, will move Beazer communities onto Dream Finders floor plans and aims to bring leverage back to current levels within 18-24 months. The combined company builds in 26 of the top 50 MSAs. Millrose provided about $1.07B of land-bank and preferred-equity financing (see the Millrose profile).

Horton) joined the Dream Finders board as co-chairman in July 2026 during the bid. The closing release names no continuing role for Beazer CEO Allan Merrill or other Beazer executives.

gaps: Regional and division coverage is thinner than a large public builder deserves: the people list rests on SEC filings, the company's investor site, CEO shareholder letters and a few trade articles.
Treasurer: not publicly disclosed (CFO Anabel Ramsay was the last named Treasurer, 2018-2021, and the proxy says she supervises treasury and investor relations).
Chief Accounting Officer / Controller: none named; the CFO signs as Principal Financial and Accounting Officer.
Investor relations / capital markets head: no named person; the company publishes only investors@dreamfindershomes.com.
Regional land heads other than Matt Childers (Texas / Colorado / Arizona): job postings confirm a Regional VP of Land layer but name no one for the Southeast or Mid-Atlantic.
Reporting line of the SVP of Land (to the CEO, COO or National President): not disclosed.

Division presidents: sourced only for Jacksonville, Orlando, DC Metro, Denver and Fayetteville (plus a stale 2024 name for Tampa). Not found in this run: Southeast Florida, Southwest Florida, Atlanta, Savannah / Hilton Head, Charlotte, Raleigh, Wilmington, Myrtle Beach, Charleston, Greenville, Nashville, Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio (Coventry Homes), Phoenix.

Beazer Homes after closing (2026-10-20): the combined leadership structure, the fate of Beazer CEO Allan Merrill and CFO David Goldberg, and who runs Beazer's divisions and land team inside DFH are not disclosed. Beazer's nine directors resigned at closing; its officers continued in role on closing day per its 8-K. See the beazer-homes file for Beazer's own roster.
Series B preferred investors (12% convertible preferred, $675M across two closings) each hold a board observer right, but neither the investors nor any observer is named in the 8-K.
Builder magazine's 2025 Builder of the Year feature (which names more DFH leaders in captions): not read.
Crescent Homes founder Ted Terry, Liberty Communities founder Neil Koelbl and Green River Builders founder Brian Hurley: post-acquisition roles at DFH not stated in the releases.
Regional president for Southeast (FL, GA, Hilton Head SC): not publicly disclosed.
Regional president for Mid-Atlantic (DC Metro, NC, SC, Nashville): not publicly disclosed (Liesel Cooper's 2024 scope covered Charleston, Greenville and Nashville; unconfirmed since 2024).
Regional president for Midwest (Texas / Coventry Homes, Colorado, Phoenix): not publicly disclosed (Cooper's 2024 scope covered Colorado; Coventry Homes publishes no president).

Regional president for the Beazer Homes markets inside DFH: not publicly disclosed; no combined org chart since closing on 2026-10-20. Beazer's own pre-merger area presidents (e.g. Bruce Craig per stockanalysis.com; Jay Thrower, Charleston/Myrtle Beach, per an undated Beazer release seen only in a search snippet) are leads for the beazer-homes file.
Reporting lines between Division Presidents and the COO: the June 2026 release says the COO leads the divisions; whether any regional layer sits between them is not disclosed.

Texas Comptroller officer records (2026 reports) for Dream Finders Homes LLC, Dream Finders Holdings LLC, DFH Coventry LLC and the Texas-formed Dream Finders Homes, Inc. (registered 2026-06-09) list only the CEO, CFO and COO, so they add no regional names.

Division and regional land leaders: no divisional VP / Director of Land Acquisition, Land Development or Entitlements for Dream Finders is named in any public source opened. Job postings show the structure without names: a divisional VP of Land reports to the Division President and works with a Regional VP of Land and the National VP of Land (career.com posting, Chantilly VA, 2026-09). Only Regional VP of Land Operations Matt Childers (Texas and West) is named.

Regional presidents: only Liesel Cooper (Colorado plus Carolinas/Nashville scope announced 2024) is named. No regional president is published for Florida, Mid-Atlantic/Carolinas or Texas. The segment heads for Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest are not disclosed; COO Clint Szubinski (June 2026) runs operations.

No division leader found for: Southeast Florida, Southwest Florida, Savannah GA, Hilton Head / Bluffton SC, Charleston SC, Greenville SC, Myrtle Beach SC, Nashville TN, Raleigh NC, Wilmington NC, Southern Coast NC, Triad NC, Goldsboro NC, Charlotte NC (HBA board affiliation only: Jeff Ott), Auburn AL, Northern Colorado, Atlanta GA (post-acquisition leader not named), the DF Luxury Homes custom division (Jacksonville), and Craft Homes (Orlando).

Beazer Homes (DFH subsidiary since 2026-10-20): no post-closing division roster has been published, and Beazer's own releases and site name no division or area presidents. Only directory leads (theorg.com, unverified) were found: Las Vegas, Houston and Atlanta division presidents and two land executives. Nothing found for Beazer Phoenix, Southern California / Riverside, Sacramento, San Diego, Dallas, San Antonio, Indianapolis, Maryland / Delaware, Northern Virginia, Nashville, Orlando, Raleigh, Charleston or Myrtle Beach.

Former acquired-company leaders not carried as current: Ted Terry (Crescent Homes founder/CEO, named in the Feb 2024 acquisition release; no later source), Brian Hurley (Green River Builders founder/CEO, May 2025 release reads as a hand-off), Jack Rostetter (named President of a Carolinas division after the 2020 H&H acquisition; Leslie Groves now leads Fayetteville) and Henri Rodier (listed as Coventry CEO on theorg.com, undated).

For the corporate file, directory leads at Beazer (theorg.com, unverified): Erica Champion, Chief Investment Officer; Jim Moore, SVP of Operations; Henry Sprague, Corporate Land Acquisition Manager (profile updated 2026-01); Josh Turner, Land Development Manager (2026-07).
Division leaders in the remaining markets above (Florida, Carolinas, Nashville, Atlanta, Texas, Beazer markets): not searched by name, so these markets are unsearched rather than confirmed vacant.

Key metrics are as of 2026-09-30 and exclude Beazer. Post-closing balance sheet (after $650M of assumed Beazer notes, about $100.8M face of Beazer junior subordinated notes, about $323M more revolver borrowings and $675M of Series B preferred) will first appear in the fiscal 2026 10-K; the pro forma exhibit to the 2026-10-20 8-K is the only combined view so far.

None of TPG Angelo Gordon, Domain, DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton or Forestar appeared in the filings read; press was not searched for them.
No public link to Domain Real Estate Partners or TPG Angelo Gordon found in the filings reviewed.
Credit ratings (Moody's, S&P, Fitch): not stated in the filings reviewed and not confirmed in this run (web search unavailable).
Land bank option fee rates, total remaining purchase price under option, and the terms (rate, deposit percentage, pooling or cross-termination) of the Millrose facility: not publicly disclosed.
Whether the unused part of Kennedy Lewis's $800M land bank commitment (about $228M above the $572.1M funded) remains available: not disclosed.
Holders of the $175M of Series B preferred not bought by Millrose: not named ('certain institutional investors').
Identity of the 51% owner of DF Capital Management, and the size of DF Residential II and III: not disclosed in the filings reviewed.
Mortgage warehouse lender names and maturities, and the nature of $38.7M of 'other borrowings': not disclosed in the 10-Q debt note.
Whether the $900M bridge commitment was drawn or simply terminated at closing: not explicitly stated; the closing 8-K describes no bridge borrowing.
Size of Dream Finders' pre-deal shareholding in Beazer (described only as a top-10 shareholder): not disclosed in the documents read.

financing.summary: DRB Group is not a stand-alone borrower: it is a 92.48%-owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry (via Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc.), files nothing with the SEC, has no rated debt, and publishes no lot counts, credit lines or lenders of its own. Trade press says Sumitomo funds DRB by keeping earnings in the business and adding shareholder loans; the parent in turn carried JPY 1,659.7 billion of interest-bearing debt at 30 September 2026 after buying Tri Pointe Homes with a JPY 835.1 billion SMBC bridge loan, about JPY 260 billion of which still has to be moved to permanent financing. The Brightland Homes piece folded into DRB in April 2025 (now DRB Group Texas, LLC) was lightly levered: USD 1,470.4M of total assets against USD 870.8M of net assets at December 2024. Land: Sumitomo says its U.S. builders should use option contracts to cut the financial burden of land, yet the five pre-Tri Pointe builders, of which DRB is by far the largest, cut optioned lots 23.7% in the year to September 2026 (to 23,500 of 73,971, about 32%) while owned lots held flat at about 50,500. For a land banker that is the opening: a stated parent policy in favour of options, a falling option ratio, a parent focused on deleveraging and protecting its rating, and no named land banker or lot-option financier anywhere in the public record.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owned, with a parent-stated push toward options. DRB historically develops its own land: its releases say it 'develops land for its two builders' (DRB Homes, DRB Elevate 55+) and its DRB Group Development arm does fee-based entitlement, land development and build-to-rent work for investors. Under Sumitomo Forestry's U.S. plan (Integrated Report 2026), the land holding strategy is to reduce financial burden through option contracts, restrain spec starts and control inventory risk; DRB management methods (on-site decision authority, financial controls) are being rolled across the merged DRB/Brightland platform, and 'financing initiatives' are listed among the integration's efficiency measures. Division leaders own land decisions inside a central capital-allocation framework (HousingWire, May 2026). No DRB-specific owned/optioned target is published.

land_banking.counterparty: Not publicly disclosed (option and purchase contracts under the parent's option-contract policy)

land_banking.description: Biscayne Homes' Tampa communities, acquired by DRB in March 2024, sit in master plans developed by Metro Development Group, so Metro is a lot source for DRB's Tampa operation. Terms (finished-lot takedowns or options) are not stated.

Verifier 2026-11-19: source URL corrected from /news/ to /news/post/ (old path redirected to the homepage); release confirms the Metro master-plan location. Sumitomo release https://sfc.jp/english/news/pdf/20240329_01.pdf also says Biscayne had a strong relationship with Metro and a pipeline of numerous lots.

Group lots rise to 106,415 and the parent's leverage to about 1.4x net D/E, which tightens the capital DRB can draw and strengthens the case for off-balance-sheet lots. The parent also plans to have DRB and the other builders use Tri Pointe's mortgage company.

Land deals are sourced by division VPs of Land Acquisition and presented to senior leaders, with the CEO (chief operating decision maker), President Alexander Hovnanian, COO Michael Wyatt and CFO Brad O'Connor the decision-makers; no corporate head of land is publicly named, and the Treasurer (Paul Eberly per aggregators) is not named in filings.
profile.summary: Family-controlled public builder (NYSE: HOV, Matawan NJ; fiscal year ends Oct 31) delivering 5,496 consolidated homes plus 935 in joint ventures in FY2025 across 13 states, with the West (AZ, CA, TX) its largest segment by Q3 FY2026 revenue ($354M of $704M). It is one of the most land-light public builders: 87% of its 34,373 controlled lots were optioned at July 31, 2026, it uses sale-and-option-back land banking and JVs, and it is actively hiring VPs of Land Acquisition in Florida and Southern California. Leadership turned over on Nov 1, 2025: Alexander Hovnanian became President and Michael Wyatt COO under Chairman/CEO Ara Hovnanian.

financing.summary: Hovnanian is one of the most option-heavy public builders: 87% of its 34,373 domestic controlled lots were optioned at July 31, 2026, the highest share in its history, and it describes its approach as a 'land-light strategic focus'. It pays for control with deposits ($348.8M of cash deposits against $3.4B of optioned land and lots) and with sale-and-option-back land banking that it books as financing ($285.1M of land-banked inventory not owned and a $164.9M liability at July 31, 2026, up from $164.9M and $94.1M at October 31, 2024); it also recycles capital by contributing communities to unconsolidated joint ventures. Corporate debt was fully refinanced in September 2025 into $900M of unsecured notes due 2031 and 2033 (8.0% and 8.375%), leaving no note maturity before April 2031 and an undrawn $125M secured revolver to June 2028. Liquidity was $379.8M at July 31, 2026 against a stated target of $170M to $245M. No land banker, option counterparty or JV partner is named in the filings opened, so the room for a land banker is large in volume but the current split between providers is not public.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light, in the company's own words ('land-light strategic focus', 'disciplined land-light strategy'). The 10-K says it prefers a 'risk-averse land acquisition strategy' and acquires land through options where possible. No numeric target for the optioned share is stated; the actual share rose from 85% (Oct 31, 2025) to 86% (Jan 31 and Apr 30, 2026) to 87% (Jul 31, 2026). Land banking is done by selling parcels to a land banker and taking an option to buy back finished lots on a schedule.

lots.source_title: Hovnanian Enterprises Reports Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter Results (8-K Exhibit 99.1)
lots.note: Domestic consolidated lots only (excludes unconsolidated JVs and the Saudi Arabia business). The release gives the total, the 87% optioned share and 6.8 years' supply on trailing twelve-month deliveries, but not the owned and optioned counts; 87% implies roughly 29,900 optioned and 4,500 owned (derived, not published in the release). The exact owned/optioned table by segment is in the 10-Q MD&A, which could not be loaded in this run. Trend: 40,246 lots at Jul 31, 2025; 35,883 at Oct 31, 2025 (85% optioned); 35,560 at Jan 31, 2026 (86%); 33,632 at Apr 30, 2026 (86%). About 3,000 lots were optioned or acquired in Q3 FY2026 and 962 were walked away from (3,712 in the nine months).

profile.org_note: Flat, market-led structure: per the company's news page, each of its 19 markets is led by an area president or division president who selects preliminary sites, monitors lot completion and runs building; the only multi-market leader confirmed in 2025-2026 is Texas region president Ken McDonald (DFW and Austin), with Houston under a senior division president, and all division operations roll up to COO Ladd Fargo. Land deals originate with the division/area president and division land teams; at corporate, President and Vice Chairman Chris Weekley covers developer relationships and land, and no Chief Land Officer or corporate land/treasury head is named publicly.
profile.summary: Houston-based private builder founded in 1976, operating in 19 markets across 13 states with about 1,790 team members and nearly 300 communities; its press-kit fact sheets show roughly 5,850 closings in 2025, led by Houston (1,148), Dallas/Ft. Worth (943), Tampa (471), Jacksonville (446), Austin (393) and Phoenix (381). Ownership is unusual: per the company, about a third is held by charitable trusts and about a third by team members through an ESOP set up in 2018. It both buys finished homesites from master-plan developers (156 lots in Verona, Pasco County, from Eisenhower Property Group in July 2026) and self-develops (Starkey Ranch in Tampa and a 42-acre parcel in Gilbert, AZ in 2025), and it has a stated goal of doubling closings; a new CFO from private equity arrived in August 2026.

financing.summary: David Weekley Homes (legal entity Weekley Homes, LLC, Houston) is privately held and publishes no financial statements, so its lot position, bank lines and leverage are not public. The one public debt instrument is a $400M 4.875% senior notes issue due 15 September 2028 (co-issuer Weekley Finance Corp., issued September 2020 to take out its 2023 and 2025 notes); that maturity is about 22 months away and is the visible refinancing event. The company describes itself as asset-light ('a home builder, not a land speculator') and has historically optioned finished lots from master-planned-community developers rather than developing land. It already has a programmatic land banker: a joint venture with Värde Partners announced April 2024, which opened with two Phoenix projects of more than $100M and named Tampa, Atlanta, Orlando and Charlotte as target markets. Room for another land banker exists (19 markets, only one named provider, facility size undisclosed), but Värde is the incumbent and the CFO fronted that deal.
financing.land_strategy: Asset-light by its own description. The CFO called it a 'long-standing asset-lite strategy' when announcing the Värde land-banking JV (April 2024), and the company site says it avoided land speculation and has 'minimal land exposure'. A 2013 trade profile (stale, for context only) said it generally optioned lots at an average option cost of a little over 5% of lot value, stayed out of land development except in rare cases, and drew about 60% of its business from master-planned communities. More recent evidence shows some self-development: the Värde JV has Weekley managing sourcing and land development, and in August 2025 the company closed on and began developing a 42-acre parcel in Gilbert, AZ. No stated owned/optioned target is public.

land_banking.description: Joint venture to land bank residential communities for David Weekley Homes nationally. Värde provides the land-banking facility; Weekley manages sourcing and land development. At announcement it had closed two Phoenix projects with more than $100M of total project costs and expected more deals in the following months. Target markets named: Phoenix, Tampa, Atlanta, Orlando, Charlotte.
land_banking.source_title: Värde Partners and David Weekley Homes Announce Land Banking Joint Venture (Värde press release)
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m is the stated project cost of the first two projects ('more than $100 million'), not the facility size, which is described only as 'significant capacity'. Lot counts and project names not disclosed. Quoted: Heather Humphrey (CFO, David Weekley Homes) and Brendan Bosman (Senior Managing Director, Värde). No public update on the JV found for 2025 or 2026.

profile.org_note: No formal region or segment layer is published: the company's own releases and office list show about 17 local divisions, each under a Division President (or General Manager), reporting to CEO Steve Alloy and the Reston corporate team; the only regional title on record is Eric Marks, Regional President over Florida (2024 release), and the acquired Holiday Builders runs as its own Florida subsidiary under Bruce Assam. Land deals start in division land teams (Directors / VPs of Land) and go to a Reston corporate land department for review: a 2025 company job posting has corporate land staff reviewing division land acquisitions and budgets, and job-board listings seen in search results (not opened) have Directors of Land Acquisition reporting to a Senior Vice President of Land Acquisition (name not public); CEO Steve Alloy fronts big land and M&A deals, CFO Randy Kotler covers financing and treasury, and large approvals go to parent Daiwa House.

profile.summary: Builder 100 #18 (5,320 closings in 2025, about $2.4B revenue) and Daiwa House's largest US homebuilder. It mainly sells entry-level and first-time move-up homes across VA, MD, WV, the Carolinas, GA and FL. Since Sept 2025 it has bought Windsor Homes' assets (about 2,100 NC lots), United Homes Group (closed 2026-05-04, $221M EV, about 1,192 closings) and Holiday Builders (closed late July 2026, about 1,050 closings, ~10,600 FL lots). That should push it toward about 7,500+ annual closings across 19+ metros. The core company is land-heavy by choice, with in-house entitlement and development and a $700M data-center land sale in 2025. The acquired businesses (UHG ~96% optioned, using land banks and a Kennedy Lewis term loan that was repaid at closing) bring option-based land books, which is the opening for a land banker.

financing.summary: Stanley Martin Homes is a private company, wholly owned by Japan's Daiwa House Industry through Daiwa House USA Holdings since February 2017. It funds itself from the parent's balance sheet: it has no public notes, no rating of its own and no disclosed credit facility, and it paid for United Homes Group (enterprise value about $221M) with cash on hand. CEO Steve Alloy calls the company land-heavy by choice. It owns and entitles hard sites itself, has an in-house land development arm (Prestige, bought in 2024), and in October 2025 sold a Prince William County tract to Amazon Data Services for about $700M. Its three 2025-2026 acquisitions bring in land-light books, though. United Homes Group controlled 96% of its roughly 7,200 lots through options, including land-bank partners and the founder's related-party developers, and it carried a $70M Kennedy Lewis term loan that Stanley Martin repaid at closing. Holiday Builders adds about 10,600 controlled Florida lots. The opening for a land banker is the parent's balance sheet. Daiwa's debt-to-equity ratio is 1.16x after hybrids (1.25x before) against a stated aim of below 1.0x by March 2027. Daiwa has also said it will balance US land investment with recovery of capital, while lifting its US forecast to 9,000 homes, with about 1,500 coming from the two 2026 acquisitions.
financing.land_strategy: Land-heavy at the core company, by its own framing. In November 2025 CEO Steve Alloy told The Builder's Daily that most national builders have sold owned land in favour of options, but Stanley Martin is not wired that way: it targets difficult sites that need complex engineering or rezoning and keeps land development and engineering staff in-house. In May 2024 Stanley Martin Holdings bought Prestige Corporate Development (land acquisition, development and lot sales, more than 8,000 lots controlled around Charlotte) and Prestige Site Works (site-development contractor). Its Integrated Report message credits growth to strategic land acquisitions and M&A, backed by Daiwa's financial strength. The acquired companies run differently. United Homes Group described itself as land-light, with 96% of about 7,200 lots under option at 31 Dec 2025. Holiday Builders bought scattered and finished lots. No owned-versus-optioned target is published for the combined company.

land_banking.description: UHG's merger information statement names GSH Land Fund, LLC as a third-party land bank for United Homes Group (now a Stanley Martin subsidiary). The land purchase, option and land-banking agreements needed counterparty consents for the merger. Who owns or manages the fund is not stated.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10)
land_banking.note: The 'GSH' prefix matches UHG's operating subsidiary Great Southern Homes, Inc. That a land bank uses the name suggests a dedicated vehicle, but its sponsor is not public (my inference). This is a lead for Domain: an existing land-bank book now inside Stanley Martin.

land_banking.counterparty: Unnamed land bank partners of United Homes Group (aggregate)
land_banking.description: UHG controlled finished lots through option contracts with third-party developers, related-party developers and land bank partners. Deposits were typically 15-20%, with staggered takedowns, and UHG usually paid development costs on land-bank deals and was reimbursed the following month. At 31 Dec 2025 lot deposits totalled $40.5M against $270.6M of remaining purchase price (6,941 option lots), down from $48.2M and $352.2M a year earlier. UHG also sold finished lots to a land banker with an option to buy them back, booked as financing at about 80% of carrying value.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group FY2025 10-K, Note 2 Variable Interest Entities (filed 2026-03-13)
land_banking.note: amount_usd_m is the aggregate remaining option purchase price across all option counterparties, not land-bank funding alone. Max exposure on the lot sale-repurchase financing was $0.2M at 31 Dec 2025 ($1.9M at 31 Dec 2024). Option forfeitures in 2025 were under $0.1M. Lot table and the 15-20% deposit terms are from the 10-K Item 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/uhg-20251231.htm).

land_banking.counterparty: Land to Lots, LLC; PC Land Development Co., LLC; Pennington Development, LLC (Nieri-affiliated 'PC Entities')
land_banking.description: These are related-party land developers tied to UHG's controlling stockholder and former executive chairman Michael Nieri, and historically a large share of UHG's developed-lot pipeline. On 22 Feb 2026, alongside the merger agreement, UHG signed 'PC Property Agreements' with them covering Camellia Park, Palomino Oaks, Southbridge, Winter Farms and Halton Oaks. The agreements speed up UHG's purchases of lots and raw land at reduced overall contract prices. Stanley Martin knew of and approved them, and included the properties in its valuation.
land_banking.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C information statement (filed 2026-04-10), background of the merger and PC Property Transactions
land_banking.note: Lot counts and prices not disclosed. Related-party lot deposits were $4.9M at 31 Dec 2025 ($6.8M at 31 Dec 2024), per 10-K Note 10 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R17.htm). The deal moves this land from founder-owned option supply onto the balance sheet.

land_banking.counterparty: Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. (through Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc.)
land_banking.description: Parent and main capital source. Daiwa House USA Holdings acquired the equity of Stanley Martin and made it a subsidiary in February 2017. The Stanley Martin CEO says growth through land acquisitions and M&A has been backed by the group's financial foundation. This is parent equity and funding, not a lot-option programme.
land_banking.source_title: Daiwa House Group Global Business: Stanley Martin (company page)
land_banking.note: CEO message in Daiwa Integrated Report 2026 (https://www.daiwahouse.com/English/ir/ar/pdf/daiwahouse_IR2026E_all.pdf, p.41). The amounts Daiwa has lent or contributed are not disclosed. Verifier 2026-11-19: the cited Daiwa page states the Feb 2017 equity acquisition (made a subsidiary) but not a 100% stake, so the description no longer says 100%.

debt.instrument: United Homes Group syndicated secured revolving line of credit (Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, 10 Aug 2023)
debt.rate: SOFR + 275-350 bp (7.48% weighted average at 31 Dec 2025)
debt.lenders_agent: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. (administrative agent; Wells Fargo Securities sole lead arranger); lenders Regions Bank, Flagstar Bank, United Bank, Third Coast Bank
debt.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (Item 1.02: credit agreements repaid and terminated at merger closing)
debt.note: Principal is the $220M commitment. $78.2M was drawn at 31 Dec 2025 (Wells $21.2M, Regions $17.9M, Flagstar $16.3M, United $13.0M, Third Coast $9.8M), with $56.4M available on a $136.0M borrowing base. Secured by homes under construction and developed lots. Covenant relief came through the Fourth Amendment (29 Sep 2025) and Fifth Amendment (31 Mar 2026). All loans were repaid and commitments terminated at the 4 May 2026 closing. Terms from the FY2025 10-K debt note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R16.htm). Wells Fargo and the four banks are relationship leads for Stanley Martin's Carolinas business.

debt.instrument: United Homes Group $70M subordinated term loan (Credit Agreement, 11 Dec 2024)
debt.rate: Adjusted Term SOFR + 675-775 bp (11.52% weighted average at 31 Dec 2025; 12.40% effective)
debt.lenders_agent: Kennedy Lewis Agency Partners LLC (administrative agent)
debt.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (Item 1.02)
debt.note: Guaranteed by UHG and secured by a pledge of 100% of Great Southern Homes, Inc. Maturity was the earlier of 11 Dec 2030 and the revolver maturity (effectively 2 Aug 2027). It funded the redemption of $80M of convertible notes. A change of control required prepayment with the applicable premium cut by 50%, and UHG carried the embedded derivative at $4.6M at 31 Dec 2025. Carrying value $67.45M at 31 Dec 2025. Covenant relief came through the KL First Amendment (29 Sep 2025) and Second Amendment (31 Mar 2026). Repaid at the 4 May 2026 closing; payoff amount not disclosed. Terms from the 10-K debt note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1830188/000183018826000009/R16.htm).

debt.instrument: Stanley Martin Homes / Stanley Martin Holdings bank or parent credit lines (terms not disclosed)
debt.source_title: United Homes Group DEFM14C (Parent intends to finance the merger with cash on hand; no financing condition)
debt.note: No Stanley Martin facility, lender, size or maturity is public. Stanley Martin has no SEC filings of its own. The only public statement is that it paid for UHG with cash on hand, and Daiwa describes its US builders as funded by the group. Row kept so the gap shows in the debt table.

debt.instrument: Parent-level funding: Daiwa House Industry consolidated interest-bearing liabilities (not Stanley Martin debt)
debt.rate: about 1.3% to 1.4% funding rate in Japan
debt.source_title: Daiwa House Consolidated Financial Results, first six months of FY ending March 2027 (11 Nov 2026)
debt.note: Yen figures, not converted: interest-bearing liabilities excluding leases 3,717.7 billion yen at 30 Sep 2026. Debt-to-equity 1.25x, or 1.16x counting 250 billion yen of hybrid bonds and loans at 50% equity credit. Balance-sheet lines at 30 Sep 2026: short-term bank loans 1,134.6bn, CP 255.0bn, bonds 643.0bn plus 51.0bn current, long-term bank loans 1,425.2bn plus 208.9bn current. Daiwa also has zero-coupon convertible bonds due 2029 and 2030 (conversion-price notice of 26 Jun 2026). The funding rate is from the 11 Nov 2026 analyst Q&A (Q16). How much is on-lent to Stanley Martin is not disclosed.

capital_events.description: Parent guidance: Daiwa aims to cut debt-to-equity from 1.16x (Sep 2026) to below 1.0x by March 2027, and is considering reducing interest-bearing liabilities rather than adding to them. It raised the FY2026 US single-family forecast from 8,000 to 9,000 homes, with about 1,500 from UHG and Holiday and existing operations roughly flat at 7,776.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House Q&A at earnings conference, FY2026 2Q (Q2, Q13, Q14)
capital_events.note: A tighter parent balance sheet alongside a bigger, more option-dependent Stanley Martin is the clearest public case for off-balance-sheet lot capital. No such arrangement has been announced.

capital_events.description: Parent guidance: after four years of heavy investment in US single-family land, Daiwa said the next three to four years will balance investment with recovery of capital. It added that US sales growth reflects continued M&A and strategic land buying.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House Q&A at earnings conference, FY2026 1Q (Q2, Q4, Q10, Q13)
capital_events.note: Same Q&A: debt-equity was 1.1x at end-June 2026. Holiday Builders was not in the FY2026 forecast, and goodwill amortisation will limit its profit contribution.

capital_events.description: At the UHG merger closing, all loans under UHG's Wells Fargo-agented revolver and Kennedy Lewis-agented term loan were repaid, commitments terminated and liens released. Stanley Martin funded the merger with cash on hand, with no financing condition.
capital_events.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (Items 1.02, 2.01)
capital_events.note: Payoff amounts not disclosed. Drawn balances at 31 Dec 2025 were $78.2M revolver and $70M term loan principal. Cash-on-hand statement from the DEFM14C.

capital_events.description: UHG signed the Fifth Amendment (Wells Fargo revolver) and Second Amendment (Kennedy Lewis term loan), waiving the DSCR and leverage covenants until the Stanley Martin merger closed. If the merger missed 31 May 2026, UHG had 60 days to refinance and repay in full.
capital_events.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-04-03 (Item 1.01)
capital_events.note: UHG's final projections in the DEFM14C showed likely DSCR (1.89x and 1.99x vs 2.00x) and leverage (2.33x vs 2.25x) shortfalls in Q1-Q2 2026.

capital_events.description: Parent ratings dated 25 Mar 2026: Daiwa House Industry long-term AA- from R&I and AA from JCR. R&I short-term (CP) a-1+ dated 15 Jul 2026. Stanley Martin has no rating of its own.
capital_events.source_title: Daiwa House Investor Relations: Ratings
capital_events.note: Integrated Report 2026 describes the R&I AA- as unchanged.

capital_events.description: Land sale: Stanley Martin sold the Devlin Tech Park tract in Prince William County, VA (190 acres) to Amazon Data Services for about $700M, against roughly $51M assembled in 2021-2022. It had first rezoned the land for 516 homes, then pursued a data-centre rezoning through a two-year court fight.
capital_events.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Land-heavy, future-ready: Stanley Martin's $700M pivot (5 Nov 2025)
capital_events.note: Article gives $700M in the lead and $709M in an Alloy quote, and 190 acres sold out of a 270-acre assembly. Daiwa's FY2025 management-policy deck refers to a 'large-scale land transaction by the U.S. subsidiary' in FY2025 (https://www.daiwahouse.com/English/ir/challenge/pdf/FY20254Q_presentation_material_en.pdf); linking it to this sale is my inference. A large one-off cash inflow ahead of the 2026 acquisitions.

capital_events.description: United Homes Group (acquired by Stanley Martin in 2026) amended both credit facilities for temporary covenant relief: the Fourth Amendment to the Wells Fargo-agented revolver and the First Amendment to the Kennedy Lewis term loan.
capital_events.source_title: United Homes Group FY2025 10-K, Note 9 Debt
capital_events.note: UHG 8-K filed 2025-10-01 (Item 1.01) reports the same amendments.

joint_ventures.description: Coastal Loans, LLC is a mortgage joint venture between Holiday Builders (a Stanley Martin subsidiary since July 2026) and Acrisure Mortgage. Not a land JV.
joint_ventures.source_title: Holiday Builders blog: Celebrating Success - Coastal Loans (26 Feb 2025)
joint_ventures.note: Whether the JV continues after the acquisition is not stated. Stanley Martin's own mortgage and title businesses (First Heritage Mortgage, First Excel Title) are group brands, not JVs (Stanley Martin Holdings release, 13 May 2024). No land or homebuilding JV found.

competitor_links.relationship: Kennedy Lewis Agency Partners LLC was administrative agent and lender group lead on United Homes Group's $70M subordinated term loan (Dec 2024, SOFR + 675-775 bp). competitor_links.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (Item 1.02)
