financing.summary: Smith Douglas is one of the most land-light public builders: it buys finished lots just in time through lot-option contracts with third-party developers and unnamed land bankers, and at 2026-09-30 owned only 517 unstarted lots (2.1% of its 24,724 controlled lots). Land banking is an established, growing channel: land bank deposits rose from $34.2M on 3,232 lots (end 2024) to $62.8M on 5,637 lots (end 2025), and total option deposits were $142.3M against a $1.42B remaining option purchase price at 2026-09-30. Corporate funding is a single $325M unsecured Wells Fargo-agented revolver (maturity May 2029; $99.0M drawn, about $204.1M available at 2026-09-30) with no public notes and no disclosed ratings. With cash at $5.9M, revolver use up from $40M to $99M in nine months, and a first self-developed Houston community (Pinemoor, 216 lots), the company has room and reason to add off-balance-sheet lot capital in its Southeast and Texas markets; no land-bank counterparty is publicly named.
financing.land_strategy: Land-light, 'just-in-time' finished-lot model in the company's own framing: acquires finished lots through lot-option contracts with third-party developers and land bankers (deposits typically 5-20% of price, non-refundable after a 60-120 day inspection period, staggered takedowns); in land-bank deals it assigns its land or lot contracts to the land banker, which funds development and sells finished lots back over time with interest on the outstanding lot price, and the company may also agree to develop the lots at a fixed cost. Targets: about a four-year lot supply in every market, no more than about two months of owned finished lots and four months of started lots on the balance sheet; 96% of unstarted controlled lots were optioned at end 2025 and 2024. No formal percent-optioned target is stated.

profile.summary: Shea Homes is the homebuilding arm of the Shea family's J.F. Shea Co. and one of the largest private US builders: 2,605 closings and about $2.6B revenue in the 2026 Builder 100 (rank 34). It builds in 11 states through regional divisions and its Trilogy 55+ resort brand, and in Colorado and elsewhere acts as master developer selling lots to other builders. Land decisions start in the divisions and go to a corporate land committee, so the division presidents (several with land-acquisition backgrounds) and the corporate committee are the land banker's entry points.

financing.summary: Shea Homes Limited Partnership (with co-issuer Shea Homes Funding Corp.) is the homebuilding arm of the family-owned J.F. Shea Co. It funds itself with retained cash flow plus Rule 144A high-yield notes; it stopped filing with the SEC in 2015 and now posts reports only behind a click-through investor page, so lot counts, the revolver and land-option terms are not public. FINRA bond data shows one notes series clearly outstanding (4.75% due April 2029, about $299M). The 4.75% notes due February 2028 now show zero outstanding, which suggests they were retired, but no redemption notice was found. S&P rates the issuer BB- with a stable outlook (upgraded April 2024) and put adjusted leverage at 2.2x and debt to capital at 28% at year-end 2024. No land-banking or lot-option financier has been publicly tied to Shea. Its land model rests on long-held California, Arizona and Colorado master-plan positions plus joint development deals, so a land banker would be pitching a new tool, not taking share from an incumbent.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning to owned and master-planned land. S&P describes Shea as a long-term land holder and master-planned-community developer in California, Arizona and Colorado. In 2018 S&P said it was shifting toward less capital-intensive projects with shorter cycles, and in 2021 it credited 'land strategies' that reduce capital outlays and limit direct land risk. In 2026 Shea is adding smaller 'boutique' Trilogy 55+ communities (under about 550 homes, e.g. ThreeOaks in Culpeper VA, Ridgecrest in Peoria AZ, Verterra in Bonney Lake WA), first Trilogy communities in Texas and Colorado, and a return to Carolinas townhomes. No owned/optioned target has been published.

profile.org_note: One reportable segment, run centrally from Las Vegas, NV (headquarters) and Calabasas, CA (investor relations and certain corporate functions), with 28 more leased offices in 16 states for operations and development staff. Only three people are executive officers: CEO Bryan Smith, CFO Chris Lau (whose published remit includes treasury and capital markets) and CAO/CLO Sara Vogt-Lowell; the 10-Q names the CEO and COO as the chief operating decision maker. AMH Development, the in-house homebuilding arm, was led by an Executive Vice President of Development (Brent Landry, per a 2024 company release); market-level development and land leaders are not published, and the only named regional leader is on the property-operations side (Florida). States listed are those with AMH-built communities on communities.amh.com; markets listed are the 14 metros with 2026 development deliveries and lots. The rental portfolio as a whole spans 24 states and 30+ markets.
profile.summary: Single-family-rental REIT (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa2) that builds homes to keep and rent, not to sell: 60,626 operating homes in 24 states plus 4,068 in joint ventures at 2026-09-30. AMH Development delivered 2,322 homes in 2025 (1,879 wholly owned, 443 to two 20%-owned joint ventures) and guides to 1,700 to 2,100 in 2026; its land pipeline has been cut from about 14,000 lots in 2022 to 5,422 at 2026-09-30 (5,066 owned, 356 optioned), with the most lots in Atlanta, Phoenix, Seattle and Charleston. Plausible but low-priority land-banking customer: the 10-K says it has used land-banking arrangements and may again, but it unwound its one disclosed arrangement in 2025 (land sold to an unnamed land banker in 2022 with finished-lot buyback options; consolidated land not owned fell from $89.7 million at year-end 2024 to zero at year-end 2025), owns about 93% of its lots, borrows unsecured at a 4.48% average rate, and is slowing development to fund share buybacks, so near-term need is small.

financing.summary: AMH is a single-family-rental REIT that builds homes to keep and rent (AMH Development), and it funds that land and construction from its own investment-grade, fully unencumbered balance sheet: $5.22B of debt at 2026-09-30, all unsecured (ten senior notes series totalling $4.8B, maturing 2028 to 2052, plus $420M drawn on a $1.25B Wells Fargo-agented revolver), rated BBB/Baa2 stable, at 5.2x net debt and preferred to adjusted EBITDAre, with no maturities until the $500M February 2028 notes. It owns nearly all of its land (5,066 of 5,422 lots, about 93%) and has cut the pipeline from a peak of about 14,000 lots earlier in the decade; 2026 wholly owned development is sized to be match-funded by $500M+ of home sales, while cash flow goes to buybacks (about $463M from November 2025 to September 2026). It has used a land banker before: in June 2022 it announced a $500M land banking facility with Värde Partners, and its filings show land sold to an unnamed land banking entity in 2022 with buyback options on finished lots, carried as $89.7M of consolidated land not owned at year-end 2024 and fully repurchased by year-end 2025 ($82.0M paid in 2024, $54.0M in 2025). So AMH is a plausible land-banking customer (the 10-K says it may use land banking again, and it already works with institutional capital through four 20%-owned JVs, two with J.P. Morgan Asset Management), but near-term need looks small while development is being scaled back and lots are being sold; the opening would be a renewed growth phase or a wish to take lots off balance sheet in specific markets such as Atlanta, Phoenix, Seattle or Charleston.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most. AMH buys and develops its own land for built-for-rent communities (it says it typically spends $300,000 to $500,000 to acquire and develop land and build each rental home), with a small optioned share (356 of 5,422 lots, about 6.6%, at 2026-09-30). The 10-K says it has used land banking arrangements in the past and may in the future, paying non-refundable deposits for options on land or finished lots at pre-determined prices. No stated owned/optioned target. The 2026 wholly owned development plan (1,300 to 1,500 homes, $500M to $600M) is 'match funded' with disposition proceeds, development spending was scaled back 'given the current capital markets environment' (Q3 2026 10-Q), and AMH is a net seller of some land: 688 land lots were in escrow for sale at 2026-09-30, and land purchase commitments were $110.8M (option contracts excluded).

lots.source_title: AMH Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Release and Supplemental Information Package (2026-11-04), AMH Development Pipeline Summary (page 22)
lots.note: Owned = lots for future delivery across 14 development markets (largest: Atlanta 774, Phoenix 537, Seattle 519, Charleston 503); optioned = lots optioned (counterparties not disclosed). pct_optioned (356/5,422) and years_supply (5,422 lots / about 1,900 total 2026 deliveries at the guidance midpoint) are calculated here, not company figures. The pipeline was 7,756 lots at 2025-12-31 (7,088 wholly owned, 668 JV) and peaked at about 14,000 earlier in the decade (November 2026 investor deck chart, rounded; peak year not legible in the extracted text). The pipeline covers lots for both wholly owned and 20%-owned JV deliveries.

financing.summary: Maronda Homes is a private, family-owned builder (founded 1972 by William J. Wolf, home office in Imperial, PA) that publishes no financial statements and has no SEC registrant, so no notes, ratings, cash or leverage figures are public. The company describes itself as owning its homesites, including a large scattered-lot inventory in Florida and the Mid-Atlantic, and it runs land acquisition division by division (the contact page lists a separate land-opportunity desk for each of roughly 14 regions). The only lender names that surface are Bank of America and Wells Fargo: a public-records aggregator shows them as the largest mortgagees of record on Maronda entities, and they were reported as the lead banks in the 14-bank secured revolver behind the 2011 Chapter 11 filing of three Maronda entities. No land banker, lot-option financier or outside equity partner is publicly linked to Maronda, and no M&A was found for 2025 or 2026; growth has been by opening new states (South Carolina announced April 2026; Maryland, Indiana, Alabama, Virginia and West Virginia now on the site). For a land banker this reads as an owned-land, bank-financed balance sheet that is stretching into several new markets at once, which is where off-balance-sheet lot capital would have the most room.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most (company framing, no stated option target). The FAQ says Maronda owns numerous homesites in multiple areas and builds on customer-owned lots in certain communities; the January 2026 blog says it owns premium lots across various streets and locations and offers an extensive inventory of homesites across its Florida and Mid-Atlantic regions. It also builds in conventional communities, including some lots taken over from other builders. No owned-versus-optioned split, lot count or years of supply is published.

profile.summary: Ranked about No. 37 in the US and No. 18 among private builders (company, May 2026). A 98-year-old family builder across 12 metros in 8 states, focused on move-up and semi-custom buyers, with townhome, Pure Style and build-on-your-lot lines. financing.summary: Drees Homes (The Drees Company, Fort Mitchell, KY) is a family-owned private builder with no SEC-registered or Rule 144A debt, so its balance sheet, lot counts and bank lines are not public. Its president, Tim Terrell (a former CFO), describes a 'quasi-land-light' model that he says turns inventory nearly twice as fast as the industry average, and says being private lets Drees be flexible on deal structures. Drees's Centennial Strategy, set in 2024, targets about 4,000 closings a year by its 100th anniversary in 2028, up from about 2,300 in 2025. Its six pillars include being 'uniquely skilled at buying lots', reaching 300 closings in each division, and entering new markets. It entered San Antonio in January 2025 by buying Monticello Homes, opened a greenfield Columbus division in April 2026 and its first Mebane, NC community in May 2026. This roughly 70% growth plan is backed by family capital and undisclosed bank lines, with no named land banker, so Drees is a plausible prospect for lot-option capital in Texas, the Carolinas and Ohio.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, which the company calls 'quasi-land-light': it controls lots through a mix of structures and develops some of its own land, mainly in Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky. In its home markets it buys finished lots in third-party master-planned communities and buys sites outright, such as the Forest Commons school site in North Olmsted, OH, won in a competitive process. Its 'Elevate' build-on-your-lot program needs no land. No owned-versus-optioned target or lot count is published.

Builder Advisor Group was sell-side advisor, and the price was not disclosed.
ma.map_impact: Adds a San Antonio division, giving Drees all four big Texas metros. Monticello's Division President Mark Elphick stays as local leader, and founder Wayne Moravits stays at least a year to help with land acquisition and integration. Monticello communities keep their brand in the near term. Drees intends to grow the division to 300 or more closings a year, so expect more San Antonio lot buying.

profile.org_note: Betenbough Homes, LLC is wholly owned by Betenbough Companies, PBC, a Texas public benefit corporation that is 100% employee-owned through an ESOP and run by a CEO (Jeanna Roach) and a small executive board (Brad Nelson, Cal Zant, Kerry Ritchie). Inside the builder: President Cal Zant, then VP Operations Corey Lusk, then area directors, then general managers per region, with an in-house Land Development department in each of the four markets. Accounting sits in the shared-services affiliate Betenbough Business Services. There is no published CFO or head of land, so the land and finance decision-makers to approach are Cal Zant and Brad Nelson (the latter by inference).
profile.summary: A conventional for-sale, entry-level and move-up single-family builder working only in four West Texas markets (Lubbock, Midland, Odessa, Amarillo), where it says it is the number one builder; more than 20,000 homes delivered since 1992. It prices cost-plus, develops its own land through in-house land development teams and asks landowners to bring it tracts directly. It is unusual in ownership: 100% ESOP-owned through a faith-driven public benefit corporation with no outside equity, and with co-founder Rick Betenbough's death around the turn of 2023-24 and Ron Betenbough's on 28 August 2024, decisions now rest with a non-family CEO and executive board. A plausible but unproven land-banking customer: nothing public shows any off-balance-sheet lot financing today.

financing.summary: Betenbough Homes is a conventional for-sale builder, but it is financed unlike its Builder 100 peers: it is wholly owned by Betenbough Companies, PBC, which is 100% employee-owned through an ESOP and says it is exempt from corporate federal income tax, so there is no sponsor, no public equity and no SEC-registered debt. No lender, credit facility, land banker, lot-option partner or joint venture is named in any public source found; the company buys land directly (it runs a public 'Land Inquiry' page asking owners to offer tracts of any size) and develops it with in-house Land Development teams in all four markets. Several of its communities sit in city Public Improvement Districts, which cover upkeep of public improvements through assessments on the homeowner's tax bill. Its capital has gone into vertical integration (captive building supply 2021, title 2020, and a captive mortgage company that made its first closings in February 2026) and into large-scale charitable giving. Room for a land banker is real in principle (about 2,000 closings a year in 2024 per Builder, self-developed lots, no outside equity) but untested: nothing public shows it has ever used off-balance-sheet lot financing, and an ESOP-owned, purpose-driven company may prefer to own its land.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and self-develops, by all public signs. The company does not describe itself as land-light and publishes no owned/optioned split. It solicits raw land directly from owners and lists Land Development as an in-house department in Lubbock, Amarillo, Midland and Odessa; pricing is cost-plus (a fixed margin on hard costs). No stated lot-supply target.

capital_events.description: Olive Branch Home Loans, LLC, a captive mortgage lender wholly owned by Betenbough Companies, PBC (NMLS 2500551), was introduced as the group's newest business and was due to close its first loans in February 2026, starting in the builder's Northwest Lubbock region only. Before this the builder relied on outside preferred lenders (Cardinal Financial ran a 5.99% rate promotion with it in 2023).

The Cardinal Financial detail is from the company's 2025 Impact Report story 'Kiss the Waves'.

'Executive Services' (the founding and executive partners) acts as owner and investor and handles corporate strategy and access to capital and land; 'Operations Partners' run centralized functions (for land: the Operations Partner, Land PMO, externally a Vice President of Land); each market team has a 'Market Partner, Land' who runs land development and lot delivery. A Director of Corporate Land Acquisition sets land strategy with 'the Founding Partner'. Land development also runs through an affiliate, Dependable Development Inc. The company publishes no leadership page, so the people holding the land and finance posts are mostly not named in public.
profile.summary: Private, founder-owned semi-custom builder based in Monroe, NC (Charlotte area), building in five Carolinas markets: Charlotte, the Triad, Raleigh, Wilmington and Charleston. It calls itself the largest private builder in the Carolinas, with more than 20,000 homes delivered since its founding (2006 per the company), and trade press reported more than 2,200 annual starts and a lot pipeline above 19,000 lots in January 2026. It is a conventional for-sale builder that entitles and develops much of its own land, with side programs for build-on-your-lot and build-to-rent, and it has said publicly that it works with off-balance-sheet investors and developers for lots, which makes it a plausible land-banking customer.

financing.summary: True Homes is a private, founder-owned for-sale builder and discloses no financial statements, credit facilities or lot split. What is public: a lot pipeline above 19,000 lots against about 2,100 to 2,200 homes a year (roughly nine years of supply), a model built on buying, entitling and developing its own land (partly through an affiliate, Dependable Development Inc), and a 2025 job posting saying the corporate land team maintains relationships with off-balance-sheet investors and developers and with lenders. No land banker, lot-option partner or lender is named by the company, and no link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. A pipeline that long for a private builder, plus an acknowledged use of off-balance-sheet lot capital, makes it a plausible land-banking customer; the capital decision sits with the founding partners (Executive Services).
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning toward self-development. The company pitches landowners directly ('We Buy It Right, We Zone It Right, We Build It Right'), takes land through entitlement itself, and runs land development in-house through market land teams, a Land PMO and an affiliated developer. Its corporate land acquisition role covers both finished and to-be-developed homesites and manages off-balance-sheet investors and third-party developers. No owned versus optioned target is published.

financing.summary: CBH Homes is a founder-owned Idaho corporation (Corey Barton Homes, Inc.) with no public debt, no SEC filings and no announced lenders, land bankers or capital partners. Public records show it financing growth through owner-affiliated entities: Barton's Endurance Holdings LLC owns the 150-acre Caldwell HQ site, Open Door Rentals LLC (Barton-owned) held its first rentals, and sister companies supply HVAC, electrical, trusses and finishes. Its land pipeline leans on large master plans: Locale in SW Boise (~600 acres, ~2,500 homes at build-out; BoiseDev says CBH markets the homes but does not name the developer entity) and the proposed Radiance in Ada County (~1,200 acres, 6,800+ units), which Corey Barton is fronting. Radiance's land is largely owned by Dennis Baker-controlled entities, and the deal terms are not public. A 6,800-unit pipeline on land CBH does not yet own is the clearest opening for third-party lot or land-bank capital. No public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. The buyer-financing tool on its site (Home Loan Helper) is powered by Premier Mortgage Resources; that is a retail-mortgage partner, not builder finance.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, owner-controlled and self-developed; the company publishes no land-light or option target. It has built spec homes only since 2016, across 60+ communities in 13 southern Idaho cities. Large tracts are entitled through specific/area plans with Bailey Engineering as civil engineer (Locale, Radiance). History of aggressive land bidding: in 2021 a CBH-linked LLC won a state endowment-land auction near Caldwell for $35.2M (about 5x appraisal), then walked away and forfeited $600K in deposits and extension fees, citing high land costs (BoiseDev, 2021-09-28). Radiance (formerly East Hollow) would be its largest project ever: 3,782 single-family homes and 3,050 apartments, under Ada County jurisdiction. As of Oct 2026 no formal application had been filed.

The legal entity is a Texas limited partnership whose general partner is Bloomfield Properties, Inc. The 2026 state filing lists co-founder Donald J. Dykstra as chairman and Timothy M. Stewart as president; the other directors are Deborah Dykstra and four Sumitomo Forestry people working from Sumitomo Forestry America's Addison, TX office. Bloomfield buys land and develops its own lots; the only land-side signatory found in public records is vice president Clint Vincent. profile.summary: Dallas-Fort Worth-only builder founded in 2004, selling its Classic and Elements series in about 65 communities across 43 DFW cities; the company says it has built more than 20,000 homes and describes itself as a major land purchaser and developer. Sumitomo Forestry (Tokyo: 1911) bought 50% in 2013 and raised its stake to 65% in 2017, making Bloomfield a consolidated subsidiary held through Sumitomo Forestry America; the two minority holders named in 2017 (P. Ryan Properties, Inc. and TKJT, Inc.) were still listed as controlling parties, alongside the Dykstras and Tim Stewart, in a December 2024 state disclosure, and the founders still run the business. Since May 2026 it sits alongside DRB Group, Edge Homes, MainVue Homes and Tri Pointe Homes in Sumitomo Forestry's US homebuilding group, so parent capital is the visible funding source.

financing.summary: Bloomfield Homes, L.P. publishes no financial statements, no debt and no lot count: it is a consolidated subsidiary of Japan's Sumitomo Forestry (Tokyo: 1911), which bought 50% in June 2013 and went to 65% in May 2017 through Sumitomo Forestry America, with the founders' companies keeping the rest. Its capital therefore comes from the parent group and from whatever bank lines it holds privately; no land banker, lot-option financier or outside capital partner is named for Bloomfield in any source read, and it describes itself as a major land purchaser and developer. The parent reports lots only for its five pre-Tri Pointe US builders together: 73,971 lots at September 30, 2026, of which 50,471 are owned and 23,500 (32%) are under purchase contract, and it has told investors it wants its US builders to buy more land through option contracts to cut the financial burden. That push now has a balance-sheet reason behind it: after the $4.0B Tri Pointe purchase the parent's interest-bearing debt rose to JPY 1,659.7 billion, its equity ratio fell to 29.2%, net debt to equity is about 1.4 times, JPY 260 billion of acquisition funding still needs permanent financing before the SMBC bridge loan falls due on May 10, 2027, and management says a rating downgrade is possible. For a land banker the opening is a majority-owned, owner-developer builder in one market (Dallas-Fort Worth) whose parent wants its US land off the balance sheet, and whose sister companies already use the product (Tri Pointe has land banking arrangements; multifamily affiliate JPI signed with Millrose in 2026).
financing.land_strategy: Owns and develops most of its own land. In its own words Bloomfield has become 'a major land purchaser and developer' that designs its neighbourhoods with local governments; Sumitomo Forestry described its business in 2013 as home building and lot development. It also builds in master plans developed by others (Union Park by Hillwood is one confirmed case) and in communities carrying public improvement district or municipal management district assessments. No owned versus optioned target is published for Bloomfield; the parent's stated direction for all of its US builders is to 'promote land acquisition through option contracts' and lighten the balance sheet (August 2026 strategy briefing).

land_banking.counterparty: Sumitomo Forestry America, Inc. (subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd.)
land_banking.description: Majority owner and the visible source of capital. Sumitomo Forestry bought 50% of Bloomfield in June 2013 and a further 15% for $36.5M in May 2017, making Bloomfield a consolidated subsidiary at 65%. Tri Pointe's February 2026 merger communications describe Sumitomo Forestry's US builders, Bloomfield among them, as locally led brands that share the group's scale, capital support and long-term investment; in 2026 the parent is steering them toward option contracts for land. Terms of any parent loans, guarantees or capital contributions to Bloomfield are not published.

JPY 350.0 billion of the Tri Pointe funding has been made permanent and JPY 260.0 billion remains. Management expects about JPY 10 billion of valuation losses on US real estate for sale in the fourth quarter and plans to raise cash by selling strategic shareholdings and being more selective in investments.

profile.summary: US arm of Canada's family-owned Minto Group, building master-planned and 55+ communities in Florida and South Carolina and now entering Texas; the parent's CEO put 2024 at 2,385 homes delivered and $1.42 billion of revenue (February 2025 company release). It is a land-heavy master developer rather than a lot-option builder: its land head says Minto 'owns the land, develops the property and builds the homes', and in 2026 it closed outright on 3,170 acres in Waxahachie (13,270 homes planned) and 1,318 acres in Texas City (about 3,500 homes, Latitude Margaritaville Galveston Bay). The Latitude Margaritaville communities are built under license from Margaritaville Holdings, with The St. Joe Company as partner at Watersound.

financing.summary: Minto Communities USA is the private Florida homebuilding arm of The Minto Group (Ottawa; owned by the Greenberg family), so it files nothing and publishes no balance sheet, lot count, credit facility or rating; how the parent funds it is not public. The one window into its financing is the 50/50 Latitude Margaritaville Watersound joint venture (LMWS, LLC) with The St. Joe Company, whose SEC filings show a $45.0 million secured bank line (undrawn at 2026-09-30, matures January 2029) and land that St. Joe puts in with payment deferred until each home closes ($10,000 per home on the first 3,700 homes, $14,400 per home on the 3,557 acres added in September 2026). In 2026 Minto bought very large tracts on undisclosed terms: about 3,170 acres in Waxahachie, TX (13,270 planned homes; 2,812 acres bought from Walton Global) and 1,318 acres in Texas City, TX (about 3,500 homes), a new-state entry that adds roughly 17,000 planned lots plus 3,500 more through the St. Joe venture. No land banker, lot-option financier or public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found; Minto behaves as an owner-developer of master-planned communities, so the room for a land banker is in financing these multi-year Texas and Florida land positions, whose current funding is undisclosed.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and develops: Minto is a master-planned-community developer that buys large raw tracts outright and develops them over many years (Westlake FL, Latitude Margaritaville Daytona Beach and Hilton Head, and in 2026 Waxahachie and Texas City, TX). The only land-light structure in the public record is the St. Joe joint venture at Watersound, where the land partner contributes or sells land to a 50/50 venture and is paid per home as homes close. No stated owned/optioned target; the company does not describe itself as land-light.

land_banking.description: September 2026 expansion of the 50/50 Latitude Margaritaville Watersound venture: St. Joe sold 3,557 acres in its West Bay Creek sector plan to the JV for a contractual $50.4 million that is paid at an average of $14,400 per home only as each home closes (St. Joe booked it at a $31.4 million present value using an 8.0% imputed rate). It adds about 3,500 homes, taking the plan from 3,700 to about 7,200. This is seller-financed land with a pay-as-you-close profile, the closest thing to a land-bank structure in Minto's public record.
land_banking.source_title: The St. Joe Company 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Note 4 Joint Ventures
land_banking.note: St. Joe's notes do not name the partner; St. Joe's 2026-09-17 press release names Minto Communities USA as the JV partner (https://finviz.com/news/393367/the-st-joe-company-announces-plans-for-additional-3500-homes-in-the-latitude-margaritaville-watersound-community). Minto's own release puts the phase-two parcel at 3,565 acres with groundbreaking projected for mid-2027.

land_banking.description: Original land arrangement for the first 3,700 homes: St. Joe contributed the initial land when the JV was formed in 2019, at its historical cost plus agreed infrastructure ($8.4 million of $9.2 million completed) and is repaid at an average of about $10,000 per home as each home is sold; each partner initially put in assets valued at $3.1 million. In December 2025 the JV bought 34 more acres from St. Joe for a contractual $1.2 million, also payable as homes close.
land_banking.source_title: The St. Joe Company FY2025 10-K, Note 4 Joint Ventures
land_banking.note: 2,426 cumulative closings and 222 homes under contract at 2026-09-30 per the Q3 2026 10-Q. Verification 2026-11-19: date changed 2020 -> 2019; the 10-K says the JV was formed in 2019 and gives no separate 2020 land-contribution date.

land_banking.description: Walton Global, a real estate and land asset management company, sold Minto 2,812 acres inside the 3,169-acre Kemp Ranch master plan in Ellis County (Waxahachie), TX. Walton's release describes a sale; it gives no price and no phased takedown, option or continuing role, and does not say who held the other roughly 357 acres.
land_banking.source_title: Walton Global Announces Sale of 2,812-Acre Master-Planned Community Site Near Dallas-Fort Worth (2026-02-24)
land_banking.note: Recorded here because Walton is a land asset manager and the seller of Minto's largest tract; the public record shows an outright purchase, not a land-bank or option arrangement. Minto's own release (seen via Ground News and a Waxahachie Daily Light excerpt) gives 3,170 acres, 13,270 homes and a 2026-02-20 closing.

debt.instrument: LMWS, LLC $10.0 million secured revolving note from St. Joe (member loan)

debt.note: Dated 2020-06-25, matured 2025-06-25, fully paid and satisfied by 2025-12-31; no balance at 2024-12-31. Shows the land partner, not Minto, supplied the venture's early working-capital line. The cited JV statements name the lender only as "one of its members"; St. Joe identifies itself as the lender on the $10.0 million Latitude JV Note in its FY2025 10-K Note 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/745308/000110465926019676/R14.htm).

debt.instrument: LMWS, LLC (50/50 JV with St. Joe) $45.0 million Master Note / line of credit
debt.lenders_agent: Bank lender not named in St. Joe's filings or the JV's audited statements
debt.source_title: The St. Joe Company 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Note 17 Commitments and Contingencies
debt.note: principal_usd_m is the commitment; nothing was outstanding at 2026-09-30 or 2025-12-31 ($41.2 million was drawn at 2024-12-31). Two notes totalling $45 million dated 2022-12-16; maturity renewed in January 2026 from December 2025 to 2029-01-30, with an extension option subject to bank approval. Monthly interest, balloon at maturity. Secured by the JV's real and personal property; St. Joe and its partner (Minto) gave an unconditional completion guaranty for certain homes and improvements, not a repayment guaranty. JV-level debt, not a Minto corporate facility.

debt.instrument: Seminole Improvement District Series 2022 Revenue Bonds (special district serving Westlake, FL; district utility debt, not a Minto obligation)
debt.source_title: Seminole Improvement District FY2026 Adopted Budget (adopted 2025-08-04)
debt.note: The district's FY2026 budget carries an enterprise (water and sewer) debt-service fund for Series 2022 Revenue Bonds and a 2022 bond construction fund; principal and coupon were not legible in the budget text. No land-secured special-assessment (CDD-style) bond series appears in the budget: the non-ad-valorem assessment is described as funding operations, and the budget has a developer-contribution revenue line and a small obligation to repay the developer for culverts. The budget does not name Minto; the district's site ties it to Westlake.

joint_ventures.description: LMWS, LLC, a Delaware LLC formed 2019-06-20 and owned 50/50, builds and sells the 55+ Latitude Margaritaville Watersound community in Bay County, FL. A board of managers with equal votes runs it; one member provides day-to-day operating services at cost ($16.7 million of SG&A reimbursed in 2025). St. Joe accounts for it by the equity method ($75.5 million investment at 2026-09-30). JV balance sheet at 2026-09-30: $184.8 million of assets, $36.4 million cash, no debt, $149.6 million equity. Plan is about 7,200 homes after the September 2026 expansion; 2,426 closed, 222 under contract; 236 closings in the first nine months of 2026 against 411 a year earlier.
joint_ventures.source_title: The St. Joe Company 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, Note 4 Joint Ventures
joint_ventures.note: St. Joe's filings do not name Minto; the partner is named in St. Joe's 2026-09-17 press release (https://finviz.com/news/393367/the-st-joe-company-announces-plans-for-additional-3500-homes-in-the-latitude-margaritaville-watersound-community). Which member provides the operating services is not stated (presumably Minto, the homebuilder). JV revenue was $137.8 million and net income $27.3 million for the first nine months of 2026, down from $244.4 million and $52.0 million.

joint_ventures.description: Brand licence, not an equity joint venture: Minto develops and sells the Latitude Margaritaville communities under licence from Margaritaville. The selling entities are Minto's own (Minto Communities, LLC at Daytona Beach; Minto Latitude HH, LLC at Hilton Head) or the St. Joe JV (LMWS, LLC at Watersound). Texas (Galveston Bay) and South Florida are listed as coming soon.

joint_ventures.note: Corrects the common description of this as a JV. Licence or royalty terms are not public. Date is the Daytona Beach sales launch (November 2017). A Zonda release (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/latitude-margaritaville-a-piece-of-paradise-named-winner-of-the-2026-master-plan-of-the-year-award-302846501.html) names Naples, FL as an upcoming community and says other Texas markets are under evaluation.

profile.org_note: Founder-owned private builder with no regions: a small corporate team in Huntsville (founder/chairman Adam Davidson, CEO Brandon Jones) over market divisions, each run by a division president who, per a third-party org chart, reports straight to the CEO. Land is run in the divisions by VPs of land acquisition (named for Raleigh, Atlanta, Houston and Dallas); no company-wide head of land is public, and the founder and CEO are personally involved in land and builder deals. The CFO seat is unconfirmed (last named 2021); the Corporate Controller is the senior finance name with a 2026 record. The company publishes no leadership page. Legal name is from the Huntsville Chamber listing; the website footer reads 'Davidson Homes, Inc.', and a 2020 article names Davidson Holding Co. as parent.
profile.email_pattern: first initial + last name @davidsonhomes.com (one published example only: the media contact)
profile.summary: Privately held Huntsville, AL builder, No. 43 on the 2026 Builder 100 (up from 46 and 60), with about 105 active communities in six states (AL, TN, GA, NC, TX, AZ). It grows three ways: organically in existing divisions, by starting new markets with a land hire first (Dallas 2024, Charlotte 2025, Auburn 2026), and by buying builders for their lots (Kindred's San Antonio assets 2023, New Leaf Homes 2024, Evermore Homes 2025 with about 2,000 lots). Management describes a lot-light approach, including buying finished lots from other builders; it launched a mortgage joint venture with loanDepot in November 2026.

financing.summary: Davidson Homes is a founder-owned private builder (Huntsville, AL) with no SEC registrant, no public notes and no published financial statements, so its lenders, facility sizes, leverage and any outside equity are not public. What is public is how it gets land: it buys and develops much of its own land (its San Antonio division said in 2024 that nearly all of its communities were on the balance sheet), buys finished lots from other builders when entering a market (D.R. Horton and Pacesetter Homes in Dallas-Fort Worth in 2024), and adds lots by buying smaller builders (Kindred Homes' San Antonio assets in 2023, New Leaf Homes' San Antonio lots in 2024, and all of Evermore Homes, about 2,000 lots, in March 2025). The CEO describes the model as 'capital-lighter' and 'asset-light', but no land banker or lot-option financier has been named in any source opened in this run, and no public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. For a land banker that reads as an open account: a fast-growing private builder (rank 43 on the 2026 Builder 100, up from 60 in 2024, with press-reported goals of 3,000 to 4,000 closings a year) that is still carrying land itself and whose acquired builder, Evermore, sold because it ran short of capital to buy land.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owned. The company publishes no owned-versus-optioned split and no option target. In its own words the market-entry playbook is 'capital-lighter' (CEO Brandon Jones, March 2024) and the operating rhythm is 'asset-light, low overhead, high-velocity' (August 2023), and its Central Texas president said in 2023 that the aim was scale 'while not having to own too many lots'. In practice the sourced examples are balance-sheet land: San Antonio expected about a dozen open communities by end of 2024, 'almost all on our balance sheet', alongside some project options; Dallas-Fort Worth was opened in 2024 with finished lots bought from D.R. Horton and Pacesetter Homes; and builder acquisitions are used to buy lot pipelines.

profile.summary: Florida-only private builder (1,617 closings on the 2026 Builder 100; the company calls itself the 8th largest private builder in the US), best known for Valencia 55+ communities and luxury Palm Beach County communities. It buys and holds large tracts itself rather than optioning lots: agricultural-reserve assemblages, master-plan parcels (192 acres in Westlake for $80M in January 2026, 42 Avenir homesites for $28.1M in April 2026) and closed golf courses (Calusa, Falls, and Polo West in Wellington under contract for $62.5M in November 2026). The Ezratti family controls the company and no outside land banker or capital partner is named in public sources.

financing.summary: GL Homes is a private, family-controlled Florida builder (Ezratti family; The Real Deal's Sept. 2026 Forbes round-up put family wealth at $1.9B) that publishes no financial statements, has no SEC filings and no public or rated debt. It buys land outright and holds a long inventory: 4,871 acres at Indian Trails Grove entitled for 3,897 homes, the 4,000-acre Riverland master plan in Port St. Lucie, about 312 acres in Westlake bought for $109M, plus four closed golf courses. Public records reported by press show project-level acquisition mortgages from banks (Wells Fargo, City National Bank of Florida), mortgages to its own related entities, seller financing and per-home deferred payments to land sellers, rather than third-party land banks. The only land-bank-style capital on record is the 2010-2011 Mountain Real Estate Capital joint venture ($75M, 6,500 home sites), a downturn-era recapitalisation. Room for a land banker is narrow on core owned land, but 2026 spending is heavy (about $122M closed, $62.5M under contract and a further $40M Westlake tract due in 2027), and GL already buys finished-lot pods in other developers' master plans (Avenir, Arden, Westlake), which is the natural opening.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most and self-develops. President Misha Ezratti said in Sept. 2026 that GL holds an inventory of land, which lets it be selective, and in Nov. 2026 that it sticks to master-planned communities and agricultural land buyouts and goes after available land 'very hard'. Since Florida's Infill Redevelopment Act (2026) it has put a handful of qualifying sites (closed golf courses) under contract. It also buys finished-lot pods from master developers (Avenir, Arden, Westlake). No stated owned/optioned target; no public use of lot-option land banking.

land_banking.description: June 2010 equity joint venture of $75M to buy one new project and recapitalise six existing GL partnerships, covering 8,300+ acres and 6,500 home sites in West Palm Beach, Tampa, Naples and Fort Myers over 8 to 10 years (est. sellout $1.8B).

profile.org_note: Kolter Homes (founded as Kolter Signature Homes LLC; Kolter Homes office at 4807 PGA Boulevard, Palm Beach Gardens) is the homebuilding affiliate of The Kolter Group LLC, a private real estate firm led by CEO Bobby Julien from 105 NE 1st Street, Delray Beach. The group runs five divisions plus a services arm: Kolter Urban (condominiums; President Bob Vail), Kolter Homes (President Robert Smithwick), Kolter Multifamily (President Jeff Quinlivan), Kolter Hospitality (President Scott Webb), Kolter Land (President Jim Harvey; Tampa) and Kolter Financial Services (K Title, CTC Mortgage; President Guido Virgili). Kolter Homes itself is organised as a president, two EVPs (Finance, Operations) and three division presidents (Southeast Florida, Mid-Southeast US, Carolinas). Land and capital decisions sit largely outside the builder: land sourcing and lot development run through Kolter Land, which since November 2024 operates as Brookfield Kolter Land Partners with Brookfield Residential as part owner, and capital-provider relationships, treasury and project debt sit at group level (COO Howard Erbstein, CFO Bill Johnson, Director - Capital Markets Malcolm Joy). Inside Kolter Homes, EVP Finance Chris Schmitz is on the acquisition team and EVP Operations Derek Fenech oversees land development.
profile.email_pattern: flast@kolterhomes.com (Kolter Homes); flast@kolter.com (Kolter Group, Kolter Land, Kolter Financial Services)
profile.summary: Private Southeast builder of amenity-heavy master-planned and 55+ communities (Cresswind brand) in Florida, Georgia, the Carolinas and, newly, coastal Alabama. It is one arm of The Kolter Group, which describes more than $30 billion of expected project value across homes, condos, multifamily, hotels and land. A land banker should note that its sister company Kolter Land is itself a finished-lot supplier to other builders and took Brookfield Residential in as an owner in November 2024, and that capital relationships are run by the group's COO and CFO rather than by the builder.

financing.summary: Kolter Homes is the homebuilding arm of The Kolter Group, a private Delray Beach investment firm; it publishes no balance sheet, lot count, credit facility or rating. What is public shows three ways it gets lots without a land banker: (1) its sister company Kolter Land, in which Brookfield Residential bought an undisclosed ownership position in November 2024 (now trading as Brookfield Kolter Land Partners), develops master plans and delivers lots to Kolter Homes and to other builders; (2) bulk finished-homesite purchases from master developers, most visibly more than $117M paid to Landstar at Avenir since 2023, including 222 sites in August 2026; and (3) outright land buys held in 'KH' entities, such as about $75M for 446 acres in Wellington in 2025. Development money comes from EB-5 loans raised through EB5AN with a Kolter parent guaranty ($80M offering for Cresswind at Spring Haven), community development district bonds, and project-level partners and lenders at the group level (Brookfield, Carlyle, Rockpoint, BH Group, Apollo, BDT & MSD, PNC, U.S. Bank). No public tie to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found, so the opening for a land banker is the homesite takedowns Kolter now pays for in cash in bulk, and the new markets (Alabama and Texas) where it has no affiliate lot pipeline yet.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning to owning and self-developing: not land-light in the public-builder sense and no stated option target. Kolter Homes builds mostly large amenitised communities (14 Cresswind 55+ communities among 28 listed in FL, GA, NC, SC and AL as of November 2026). Lots come from the affiliated lot developer Kolter Land / Brookfield Kolter Land Partners (for example 1,300 Cresswind homes at Twin Lakes, GA and Cresswind at Hammock Oaks, FL), from bulk finished-homesite purchases inside third-party master plans (Avenir, Westlake), and from raw land bought and entitled directly (446-acre Artistry Lakes, Wellington, rezoned for 579 homes in March 2026). CEO Bobby Julien said in September 2026 that good South Florida land deals are rare and that Kolter is expanding into Alabama and Texas.

profile.legal_name: Eastwood Homes (operating entities include Eastwood Construction LLC and Eastwood Construction Partners LLC)
profile.org_note: Family-owned and flat: founder Joe Stewart (now an advisor), President Clark Stewart (runs the company), CFO Kevin Hutchins, then division presidents by metro (11 divisions after the May 2026 Peachtree deal, about 450 employees). No regional layer is visible. Capital and deal decisions sit with the President and CFO; the CFO's conference bio credits him with securing financing and handling corporate and land acquisitions. Job-posting snippets point to a corporate VP of Land Development and a Chief Operating Officer, and to land acquisition managers inside divisions reporting to the division president; neither corporate role is named publicly.
profile.summary: Privately held, family-owned Charlotte builder founded 1977: about 1,500 closings a year in 140+ communities across NC, SC, VA and GA, plus a build-on-your-lot line; HousingWire ranks it the No. 11 private builder. Growing by acquisition: Napolitano Homes (Hampton Roads, March 2025) and Peachtree Building Group (Atlanta, May 2026, about 1,000 land, pipeline and work-in-progress assets). A conventional for-sale builder that funds itself with bank debt and family equity; its CFO speaks publicly on land-long versus land-light models and on bank versus private capital, which makes him the natural first call.

financing.summary: Eastwood is a private, family-owned, conventional for-sale builder that publishes no financials, lot counts or facility terms. What is visible points to a bank-and-balance-sheet model: a public-records aggregator shows Fifth Third Bank as by far its largest recorded lender, the CFO talks about staying 'relevant to banking partners', and the seller of Napolitano Homes said Eastwood has the financial strength to carry land that a 200-home builder could not. No land banker, lot-option fund or outside equity partner is named anywhere public, and no link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. It is a plausible land-banking prospect: about 1,500 closings growing toward roughly 1,800 through two acquisitions in 14 months, a new block of about 1,000 Atlanta assets to carry, and a CFO who is on conference panels about land-long versus land-light models and bank versus private capital.
financing.land_strategy: Not stated in the company's own words. Indicators are mixed: Eastwood develops some of its own communities (an affiliate named Eastwood Development Corp appears in public records) and also buys lots from developers (it entered Richmond by buying lots in master plans, and in Atlanta keeps Cotter Properties as a development partner after buying Peachtree Building Group). Third parties describe it as able to hold land on its own balance sheet; no land-light target has been published.

ma.counterparty: Peachtree Building Group (metro Atlanta; principals Doug Cotter and Scott Schmidt)
ma.description: Eastwood announced the acquisition of Atlanta builder Peachtree Building Group, which it calls its 11th division. Trade press reports about 1,000 land, pipeline and WIP assets came with it and that Eastwood's Atlanta volume goes from roughly 120 closings a year to 350-400. Terms undisclosed. JTW Advisors (buy side), Zelman & Associates (introduced the seller), Williams Parker (Eastwood counsel).
ma.map_impact: Adds an Atlanta operation several times the size of Eastwood's existing one and lifts company volume from 1,506 closings (2025) toward roughly 1,800 on a combined basis (estimate: a Builder search snippet gives Peachtree 307 closings in 2025). Atlanta leadership after the deal is not public; the Peachtree principals are exiting owners, with Doug Cotter's Cotter Properties staying on as land development partner. Headcount about 450.
ma.source_title: Eastwood Homes press release: Expands Further into Metro Atlanta Through Acquisition of Peachtree Building Group
ma.note: The release announces the acquisition without a separate closing date; citybiz (2026-05-26) reports it as completed. Asset count, closings uplift and adviser detail are from HousingWire (2026-05-26 and 2026-05-27), i.e. Reported.

ma.counterparty: Napolitano Homes (Virginia Beach / Hampton Roads, VA)
ma.description: Eastwood completed the acquisition of family-owned Napolitano Homes, creating its 10th division and second in Virginia. Napolitano built up to about 200 homes a year; Eastwood's CFO expected about 125 added closings in 2025. The Napolitano brand was kept. Zelman & Associates was exclusive sell-side adviser. Terms undisclosed.
ma.map_impact: Added the Hampton Roads market and its division leadership (Vince Napolitano stayed in charge). The seller said Eastwood's balance sheet lets the division carry land it could not carry alone, so Hampton Roads land spend now runs through Charlotte.
ma.source_title: Eastwood Homes press release: Announces the Acquisition of Napolitano Homes
ma.note: Volume figures and the land-carrying remark are from The Builder's Daily (2025-03-31), i.e. Reported. Eastwood's earlier deal, Fortress Builders in Columbia, SC (2017), is outside the window.

industry_deals.description: Eastwood Homes acquired Peachtree Building Group, announced 2026-05-26; the release says Eastwood 'announced the acquisition' and Zelman, the seller's adviser, calls it a completed May sale. Price not disclosed. Peachtree is a private south-Atlanta builder; per Zelman the deal lifts Eastwood's Atlanta production from about 120 closings a year to about 350-400, and the seller's principals stay on as development partners. Most Peachtree operations stay with Eastwood, which now has 11 divisions; its second purchase in about 18 months after Napolitano Homes (Virginia, 2025). JTW Advisors advised Eastwood, Zelman Partners advised Peachtree.
industry_deals.map_impact: No top-100 row disappears: Peachtree is outside the top 100. Rank 46 Eastwood Homes roughly triples its Atlanta volume and should move up a few places on closings.
industry_deals.source_title: Metro Atlanta CEO (staff report reproducing the company release): Eastwood Homes Expands Further into Metro Atlanta Through Acquisition of Peachtree Building Group (2026-05-27)

profile.org_note: Three operating segments: Canada, U.S. Housing and U.S. Land, with the U.S. reported as West and Central and East. U.S. land is led nationally by Brad Chelton (President, U.S. Land) and U.S. homebuilding by Greg Shaia (President, U.S. Housing); combined land-and-housing regional presidents run Northern California, Southern California (with Arizona), Arizona and DC Metro, while Bill Meyer runs Southeast land and the Kolter partnership (Jim Harvey) supplies Southeast lots. Capital allocation sits with EVP and Chief Investment Officer Warren Krug and the Investment Committee (COO Shane Pearson is a member), supported by a central Investments team under EVP Carl Perrone; CFO Thomas Lui oversees treasury, capital markets and investor relations.
profile.summary: Land developer first, homebuilder second: about 127,000 managed lots (58,931 Brookfield share) at 30 Sept 2026 across 25 North American markets, 2,377 home closings and $1.8B revenue over the last twelve months. Wholly owned by Brookfield Corporation, which funds it alongside unsecured notes; it sells finished lots to other builders, runs land JVs and managed-only land for capital partners, and itself offers land-banking services, so it is as much a competitor or co-investor to a land banker as a customer.

financing.summary: Brookfield Residential is a land developer first: at 30 Sep 2026 it controlled 58,931 lots on a Brookfield-share basis (127,242 managed lots), and it pays for land with Brookfield Corporation equity, four unsecured 144A note series ($1.63B), a $675M unsecured revolver (drawn $586M, only $15M free at Q3 2026) and project loans. It is moving its land book off balance sheet by selling stakes to capital partners: 80% of five master-planned communities in Jan 2025 (NASH invested in five MPCs, announced Mar 2025), the Kolter Land partnership in the Southeast, and the Trez Capital JV. It now puts 5-50% equity into new land deals and also manages land with no equity. Its own land-banking counterparty is affiliate Brookfield Wealth Solutions (lot financing arrangements plus a 2025 land option agreement), and it invests in landbanking vehicles (Homebuilder Finance) and markets land banking to other builders. That makes it more a competitor or co-investor for Domain than a borrower. The opening for a third-party land banker is small but real: the $600M 6.25% notes mature in Sep 2027, Moody's moved the outlook to negative in Oct 2026, and the revolver is almost fully drawn.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving to land-light. The company describes an asset-light managed-land model: it sources a capital partner for each new land deal and invests 5-50% equity, keeps its existing wholly owned land, and may manage land with no equity. Growth is to come mainly from JVs and managed-only assets, which earn development management fees and secure finished lots for its own homebuilding. Target leverage is 40-50%, matched to active land and housing inventory.

lots.source_title: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
lots.note: Brookfield Residential share. Owned = 35,611 lots owned directly (Canada 23,423; U.S. 12,188) + 11,907 lots held through 47 unconsolidated entities. Optioned = 11,413 lots of 'inventory not owned' (consolidated land under financing arrangements and lots under option), of which 11,253 are in Northern California, 57 in Southern California and 103 in Texas. pct_optioned computed here (11,413 / 58,931). Managed lots at 100% (incl. JV partners' and managed-only interests): 127,242. Dec 31 2025: 58,155 controlled (34,213 owned, 12,432 JV, 11,510 not owned). Years supply not disclosed. Note that inventory-not-owned book value is only $19.3M, so most of these lots appear to be optioned or financed rather than balance-sheet land.

land_banking.description: BWS is a Brookfield Corporation affiliate. It holds land under financing arrangements that Brookfield Residential buys back as lots, and from 2025 a land option agreement under which Brookfield Residential pays option maintenance fees and deposits for the right to buy lots. At 30 Sep 2026 the related liability was $17.2M, inventory not owned was $19.3M, deposits were $12.7M on the financing arrangements and $24.5M on the option agreements, and capitalized option fees were $6.5M. In the first nine months of 2026 it paid $49.2M for lots and $16.1M for land bought from BWS.
land_banking.source_title: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
land_banking.note: In the 2025 Annual Report, 2025 lot takedowns from BWS were $83.1M (2024: $60.3M) and the liability fell from $117.3M (Dec 2024) to $53.7M (Dec 2025); the land option agreement with BWS was entered in 2025. amount_usd_m is the outstanding liability at Q3 2026, not the program size, which is not disclosed. profile.summary: Houston-based entry-level and move-up builder founded in 2004, majority owned by Japan's Daiwa House since September 2021 (an 80% stake at the time, per trade press; 89.11% as of December 2025, per Daiwa House). Daiwa House reported 1,465 homes delivered, USD 645 million of sales and 268 employees for FY2024. It builds in four Texas metros plus Arizona (2023), Nashville (2024 acquisition) and Huntsville (October 2025 acquisition), and describes itself as a lot developer as well as a builder. Growth is funded by the parent, which reorganised ownership under CRC Holdings LLC in December 2025 to make financing easier.

financing.summary: CastleRock Communities LLC is a second-tier subsidiary of Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd. (Tokyo: 1925): Daiwa House USA Holdings Inc. bought 80.0% from the three founders in September 2021 for about US$402 million and, since a 1 December 2025 reorganisation, holds 89.11% of a new Delaware holding company, CRC Holdings LLC, which Daiwa says was set up to facilitate financing for CastleRock; CEO Robert L. (Lance) Wright holds 9.01% and land head Kirk Breitenwischer 1.88%. CastleRock files nothing publicly, so its own bank lines, lot count and any lot-option or land-bank arrangements are not disclosed, and no land banker is named in any source opened in this run. Before Daiwa, the business ran on US$155 million of partner subordinated loans (converted to equity in 2021); today growth is funded by parent equity (CRC Holdings capital stock US$528.6 million) and the parent's yen balance sheet (R&I AA-, JCR AA, funding cost in Japan about 1.3% to 1.4%). Daiwa's three US builders together held 75,017 lots including controlled lots at the end of 2025, about 9.6 years of their combined 7,776 deliveries, and Daiwa does not say how much of that is owned. The opening for a land banker is at parent level: Daiwa's interest-bearing liabilities rose to JPY 3,717.7 billion at 30 September 2026 (debt-equity 1.25x against a former discipline target of about 0.6x), largely from buying real estate for sale including US single-family land, and management said in November 2026 it is considering reducing leverage rather than adding to it.
financing.land_strategy: Not stated in owned-versus-optioned terms. Daiwa describes CastleRock as doing both residential land development and home sales (it self-develops and also sells residential land), and the company's own leadership page says its land head buys both raw land for development and existing (finished) lots. Daiwa's group framing for the US single-family business is growth through M&A plus strategic land acquisition; it reports group land holdings 'including controlled lots' (75,017 at end of 2025) without an owned/controlled split, and publishes no land-light target. Trade press (The Builder's Daily, July 2026) reports a Daiwa aim of about 100,000 controlled US lots under its next plan; that target was not found in Daiwa's own documents opened here. Group tone is land-heavy: Stanley Martin's Steve Alloy, executive chairman of Daiwa House USA Holdings, told the same publication in November 2025 that the industry's land-light model does not fit how his company operates. No equivalent statement from CastleRock was found.

Yakim, a 2021 seller, is no longer a holder. When and how the stake rose (purchase of Yakim interest, capital injections, or both) is not disclosed.

profile.org_note: Legend Homes is the for-sale homebuilding company (the 'Retail' entity, with the Princeton Classic Homes brand) inside family-owned Camillo Companies, alongside SimplyHome (build-to-rent owner and operator, formerly Camillo Properties), Academy Development (land acquisition and lot development for both) and LCI Services (maintenance). Group CEO Dan Miller sits over a Legend president (Lee Darnold) with three division presidents (Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio) created in early 2026. Land decisions sit outside the builder, at Academy Development under president Sean Mulroony; finance sits at group level with CFO Jomar Ereso and Chief Investment Officer Dror Goldberg. The founder's daughters, Lara Camillo Moynihan and Lauren Camillo Sullivan, are the board members the company lists.
profile.summary: Texas-only entry-level builder (Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio), more than 22,000 homes sold since 1991, and one arm of the Camillo family's vertically integrated group. It is a conventional for-sale builder, but it shares its land pipeline with the build-to-rent affiliate SimplyHome (more than 10,800 rental homes built), and some communities are split between the two. A search-result snippet of Builder's firm profile (page not opened, so unconfirmed) shows 1,457 closings in 2025, down from 2,049 in 2024, with 165 single-family build-to-rent units, so a small part of reported volume may be rentals built for the affiliate. Lots come mainly from affiliate Academy Development, and the group describes itself as one of the largest private landowners in Texas, so this is a land-heavy, self-developing builder rather than a land-light one; a plausible land-banking customer only if the new, finance-led management (CEO from August 2025, CFO from April 2026) chooses to take land off the family balance sheet.

financing.summary: Legend Homes is a conventional for-sale builder, but it is financed and supplied with land as one arm of the Camillo family's private, vertically integrated group, and nothing about its own debt or liquidity is public. Affiliate Academy Development buys, entitles and develops most of its lots (more than 25,000 lots developed since 1989), and the group calls itself one of the largest private landowners in Texas, so the model is own-and-develop, the opposite of land-light; Legend also takes sections in third-party master plans such as Signorelli's Bluestem. The same land pipeline feeds the build-to-rent affiliate SimplyHome (more than 10,800 rental homes built), and the only named lender anywhere in the group is Churchill Real Estate, which provided SimplyHome a $255 million bridge facility arranged by JLL in 2023. No land banker, lot-option financier or outside equity partner has been named publicly. It is a plausible land-banking customer rather than a current one: the land sits on a family balance sheet, the 1,457 closings in the 2026 Builder 100 are well under half the 3,351 closings/units the company cited for 2022, and since August 2025 the group has been run by a finance and capital-markets CEO (ex-Highland Homes, ex-TPG Capital) with a new CFO (April 2026), a Chief Investment Officer and a newly promoted land president whose remit includes 'strategic partnerships'.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and self-develops. The company's framing is an 'integrated approach': affiliate Academy Development acquires and develops land for both Legend Homes (for sale) and SimplyHome (for rent), and the group describes itself as one of the largest private landowners in Texas. No land-light or option target is stated. Legend supplements affiliate lots with sections bought in third-party developers' communities.

land_banking.description: The group's in-house land company. It acquires, entitles and develops communities and delivers finished lots to Legend Homes and to the rental affiliate SimplyHome; it reports more than 25,000 lots and more than 100 communities developed since 1989 in Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio and Bryan-College Station. This is the role a land banker or third-party developer would otherwise fill.

land_banking.note: Terms between the affiliates (lot pricing, takedown schedules, who holds title) are not public. The 25,000 figure is lots developed over the company's life, not lots held today. The 100-plus communities figure is from https://www.camillocompanies.com/our-companies (opened 2026-11-19), not the Mulroony release, which states only the 25,000 lots.

profile.summary: NOT a conventional for-sale homebuilder. Hancock Builders (formerly Hancock Communities, founded 1976) is a private Phoenix general contractor and fee developer that builds single-family build-to-rent communities for third-party developers and investors (TerraLane/IHP Capital Partners, Cavan Companies, Blueprint Capital, Van Tuyl/Vlux, WestStone, Montgomery Street Partners, UrbanStreet); all 1,374 of its 2025 Builder 100 'closings' are rental units delivered to those owners. All work is in Arizona: 25 rental communities delivered since 2017 and 10 under construction as of September 2025. It is a weak land-banking prospect because the land sits on its clients' balance sheets, not its own, although founder Greg Hancock sources that land and the company says it plans to expand into for-sale and commercial contracting and to work with developers outside Arizona.

financing.summary: Edge Homes is a consolidated subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry (Japan), not a stand-alone private borrower, and publishes no financing of its own: no credit facility, lender, land banker or lot count is public at the Edge level. Funding context is the parent, which carried JPY 1,659.7 billion of interest-bearing debt at 30 September 2026 after buying Tri Pointe Homes with bank bridge financing, and which says about JPY 260 billion of that bridge still has to be moved to permanent financing. Sumitomo Forestry states that its U.S. builders are using option contracts to cut the financial burden of land: across the U.S. group 39,261 of 106,415 lots (about 37%) were under option at September 2026, and 23,500 of 73,971 (about 32%) for the five pre-Tri Pointe builders that include Edge. For a land banker this is a plausible but parent-gated customer: Edge runs its own acquisition and entitlement team and buys land outright on entitlement-contingent contracts, while the parent has both a stated push toward optioned lots and leverage that rose sharply with the Tri Pointe deal (net D/E about 1.4x at September 2026).
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, leaning owned. Edge sources and entitles its own land (VP of Land Acquisition plus VP of Land Entitlement) and contracts to buy sites conditional on rezoning: Taylorsville's 2026 ordinances for the 16.5-acre, 316-unit Solstice at 54th only take effect once Edge Homes Utah, LLC closes on the property. The parent's stated U.S. policy is to restrain spec starts and acquire more land through option contracts to reduce financial burden; no Edge-specific owned/optioned target is published.

profile.org_note: Founder-owned group run from 500 Stonehenge Parkway, Dublin, OH. Two arms share one executive team: a company-owned homebuilder (six markets, each a state affiliate that holds every community in its own single-member project LLC) and a franchisor, Epcon Communities Franchising, LLC, that licenses the product to 60+ independent builders. Land and capital decisions sit with CEO Joel Rhoades, CFO/Treasurer David Blackmore, an operations executive (Brooks Longfellow) and the two founder co-chairmen, all of whom are officers of every project LLC; no VP or Director of Land is named publicly and current market leaders are confirmed only for Raleigh (2023 and older names for Columbus, Atlanta and Nashville are tagged Inferred in the people list).

profile.summary: Private, founder-owned builder of single-storey courtyard homes for 55+ buyers, and a homebuilding franchisor (its franchising site calls it the largest US homebuilding franchise by closed units). The Builder 100 figure (1,269 closings, about $825M) is the whole system: per CEO Joel Rhoades in May 2026, the company-owned arm closed just under 600 homes last year in six markets (Columbus, Charlotte, Raleigh, Indianapolis, Atlanta, Nashville) and 60+ franchise builders in 20+ states closed a little over 600. For a land banker the addressable customer is the roughly 600-home corporate arm (average 2024 settlement price about $721K), which buys and develops its own land through single-purpose project LLCs; franchisees are separate small builders that finance their own land.

financing.summary: Epcon is a private, founder-owned company with no public debt, ratings or disclosed bank facilities, so most of its financing is not public. What is public: each company-owned community sits in its own single-member project LLC, the corporate arm buys and develops its own land in-house, and Epcon project LLCs have been filing SEC Form D notices since at least 2016; the nine notices opened for 2024 and 2025 are all small private debt placements ($250K to $2.7M each, one investor each, two placed by a small Ohio broker-dealer, Lincoln Douglas Investments). That pattern points to project-by-project private capital on top of undisclosed bank loans, not a programmatic land bank; no land banker, lot-option partner or link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. It is a plausible but small land-banking customer: only the roughly 600-home company-owned arm (six markets, about 18 active communities at the end of 2024, average price about $721K) is one counterparty, while the other half of the 1,269 ranked closings belongs to 60+ independent franchise builders who, per the franchise disclosure document, mostly buy raw ground and fund it with local bank or family-office acquisition and development loans that Epcon does not provide.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and develops (not land-light, as far as public sources show). The affiliates buy raw land and develop lots themselves through single-member project LLCs; a May 2025 Columbus job advert for a Land Development Project Manager describes in-house lot delivery. No owned/optioned split or target is published. The franchise disclosure document says most franchisees also buy raw ground rather than finished lots.

profile.summary: Conventional for-sale homebuilder and the largest privately owned builder in the Pacific Northwest by its own description: more than 28,000 homes since 1989, selling entry-level and workforce-priced homes in secondary and rural markets across Oregon, Washington, Idaho and Montana. Owned by the Watson family and run from a new Redmond, Oregon support centre opened in 2025. It sources and develops much of its own land, has bought lot positions from other builders, and publishes no lot counts, lenders or capital partners, so it is a plausible but untested land-banking prospect.

financing.summary: Conventional for-sale homebuilder, privately held by the Watson family, with no SEC filings, no rated or public debt and no published lot counts, lenders or credit facilities; how it funds land is not publicly disclosed. The public record points to a self-funded, self-developing land model: in-house land acquisition and land development staff in each region, a 'Sell Land to Hayden Homes' intake on its website, bulk purchases of other builders' lot positions (Copper Basin in 2015, RYN Built Homes in 2021) and public-private land deals with cities (Parkside Place in Bend). No land banker, lot-option financier or institutional capital partner is named anywhere, and no public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. That makes it a plausible land-banking customer that appears to be unserved: the company itself said in October 2026 that finished-lot costs can exceed what its entry-level prices support, and a Vice President of Land Acquisition seat was recruited around late 2025 to lead regional land teams and find new markets. One unconfirmed lead: a search-result summary of a Builder article lists Hayden Homes among strategic builder investors in Avila Real Estate Capital's first homebuilder debt fund (closed July 2025).
financing.land_strategy: Not framed publicly as land-light or land-heavy, and no owned-versus-optioned target is stated. Evidence suggests it buys and develops most of its own land in secondary and rural Northwest markets (regional land acquisition, forward planning and land development teams; direct land purchases from owners), supplemented by buying finished or pipeline lots from other builders and developers and by city partnerships that bring land inside urban growth boundaries in exchange for affordability commitments.

profile.org_note: Founder-owned holding company (Brian Bahr, Founder and Chairman) with three operating companies: Challenger Homes (Colorado for-sale builder, CEO Brandon Loveridge), National Builder Group (NBG, a network of owner-operator builders in which each operator holds 20% and NBG arranges all lot and construction financing; President and CEO Jim Rosewater) and Goodwin Knight (multifamily and rental cottages, also led by Loveridge). Land is decided in two places: Challenger Homes in Colorado Springs (land heads not named on any company page) and, for NBG, each local owner-operator finds finished lots and NBG headquarters approves and funds them. All Pro Capital, a separate Bahr-founded investment firm, raises investor debt that funds NBG.
profile.summary: Conventional private for-sale homebuilder, founder-owned, started in 2000 by Brian and Heather Bahr and now a group of three businesses: Challenger Homes (entry-level and move-up homes in about 11 Colorado communities), National Builder Group (16 owner-operator builders listed across 11 states, finished lots only, 475+ homes sold in 2025 per its affiliate lender) and Goodwin Knight (rental cottages and apartments, 859 units under development). It became fully founder-controlled again in February 2024 when Green Brick Partners sold back its minority stake for about $64 million. A plausible land-banking customer: growth is funded by bank lines and by roughly 10% investor debt raised through an affiliate, with no named land banker.

financing.summary: Private and founder-owned, so there is no public balance sheet, lot count or rating. What is public: the group funds homes and land with bank financing (more than $100 million, lenders not named) and with investor debt raised by its affiliate All Pro Capital, whose current fund (All Pro Funding V) lends to National Builder Group at Prime + 3% (10% today, 7% floor, 10% cap) against deeds of trust at no more than 75% of value, with a corporate guarantee from The Challenger Group, Inc., maturing 31 December 2031. In February 2024 the controlling owner bought back Green Brick Partners' minority stake for about $64 million, removing its one institutional equity partner. No land banker or lot-option partner is named anywhere; National Builder Group buys only finished lots a few at a time, so the room for a land banker is mainly Challenger Homes' Colorado community pipeline and any larger finished-lot takedowns the owner-operators cannot stage, where land-bank pricing would compete with roughly 10% affiliate money that carries a parent guarantee.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed and not quantified. National Builder Group is explicitly finished-lot only: each owner-operator starts with 2 finished lots and adds at least 2 a month, finds the lots locally, and headquarters approves and arranges 100% of lot and construction financing on a non-recourse basis. Challenger Homes sells in about 11 Colorado communities, several inside third-party master plans (Sterling Ranch, Wolf Ranch, Meridian Ranch); whether those lots are bought finished, optioned or self-developed is not disclosed. The affiliate debt fund says its loans fund new homes and land development. No stated owned-versus-optioned target.

profile.org_note: Until the 2026-05-04 sale, UHG reported three segments (GSH South Carolina incl. Augusta GA; Rosewood move-up homes; Other = Raleigh NC plus the Homeowners Mortgage JV) run through Midlands, Coastal and Upstate SC, Augusta and Raleigh divisions, and every new land deal was approved by a Land Investment Committee of the CEO/President, Co-COOs and CFO, with division leadership presenting deals. profile.summary: Columbia/Chapin, SC entry-level builder (Great Southern Homes brand, founded 2004 by Michael Nieri, ~11,000 homes built) that closed 1,192 homes in 2025 across the Midlands, Upstate and Coastal SC, Augusta GA and Raleigh NC. It ran a very land-light model: at 2025-12-31, 96% of 7,225 lots were controlled by option contracts with third-party developers, Nieri-related developers and land banks. Stanley Martin Homes (Daiwa House Group) bought it for about $221M enterprise value in cash, closing 2026-05-04; it is being folded into Stanley Martin's Carolinas divisions, so land-bank conversations now run through Stanley Martin, not a stand-alone UHG team.
