land_banking.note: lots = 307 single-family + 74 townhome lots. Schell was the rezoning applicant in 2021; the terms on which HHHunt develops and delivers the lots (purchase, option, fee development) are not public. HHHunt is a developer-builder, not a land banker.

land_banking.description: Historical: in Dec 2012 the Charlotte-based investor formed a joint venture with Ocean Atlantic to buy a lender's note on Breakwater, a 185-lot community in Lewes, so that Ocean Atlantic could finish development; Schell Brothers was to sell and build homes on the remaining lots. Terms were not disclosed.
land_banking.source_title: Ocean Atlantic, real estate investor team up to develop Lewes community (Delaware Business Now)
land_banking.note: Fourteen years old and included as precedent only: it shows the Schell family group has taken institutional land capital at the affiliate level. No current MREC relationship was found.

capital_events.description: The only lender named in press coverage: TowneBank financed the renovation (over $500,000) of the 13,500 sq ft building at 1919 Huguenot Road, Chesterfield, which Schell Brothers bought for $850,000 as its Richmond division office.

joint_ventures.description: Westford Glen, Henrico County, VA: Schell Brothers assembled about 76 acres (nine parcels, under contract) and brought in Midlothian-based Main Street Homes as co-developer. Rezoning sought for up to 330 townhomes and 40 detached homes plus 3 commercial acres; Main Street's president put the cost at about $175M at buildout, with construction roughly two years out and a four-year buildout. County staff had not yet backed the rezoning in Nov 2025. The two builders also work together on Dogwood Creek in Chesterfield.

financing.summary: Olthof Homes is a private family company with no public debt, no SEC filings and no announced capital partner, so almost nothing about its financing is public. What town records show is a builder that buys and develops its own land: parcels are held in affiliated LLCs registered at the home office (Cedar Lake Development, LLC; Integrity Development LLC), it closes on land after entitlement, runs its own land development, and posts performance and maintenance letters of credit with towns (issuing banks not named). No land banker, lot-option financier or joint venture has been named publicly, and it has no public link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon. It is a plausible but small land-banking prospect: about 530 closings a year, five new communities opened in 2026, and a stated aim to reach the top 50, all funded so far from an owned-land model.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and self-develops, in practice: the company acts as land developer in many of its communities, holds land in affiliated single-purpose LLCs at its St. John address, and invites landowners to sell to it directly through a published land contact. profile.org_note: Family-owned, three generations: Park Square Enterprises, LLC is the parent of Park Square Homes, Kimaya (commercial, multifamily and build-to-rent development), PSH Mortgage (JV with FBC Mortgage) and Park Square Homes Title. Co-CEOs Suresh Gupta and son Vishaal Gupta run it; Keith Hurand was named President and COO in July 2024 (not reconfirmed in 2026). Finance sits with CFO Monika Goyal (shared with Kimaya); land acquisition and development are run by a small in-house team at manager level (no current VP of Land is publicly named, and the company has advertised the VP of Land seat).
profile.summary: Orlando-based, family-owned Florida-only builder founded in 1984, ranked No. 100 on the 2026 Builder 100 with 522 closings and $251M revenue in 2025, down from 996 closings and $311M in 2024. It builds entry-level single-family homes and townhomes across Central Florida, Tampa Bay and Southwest Florida, plus 6-15 bedroom vacation and short-term-rental resort homes near the Orlando parks, and its sister company Kimaya develops build-to-rent and multifamily (Park Square Homes acted as general contractor on Kimaya's award-winning Ocoee Village build-to-rent townhomes). It buys both raw land it develops itself and finished lots from developers, which makes it a plausible, if small, lot-option customer.

financing.summary: Park Square Homes is a private, family-owned Florida builder (parent Park Square Enterprises, LLC) with no SEC filings, no rated or public debt and no published financial statements, so its bank lines and land financing are not public. Volume fell from 996 closings ($311M) in 2024 to 522 closings ($251M) in 2025 per Builder's 2026 firm profile, which is why it slipped from No. 70 to No. 100. It sources land both ways: it buys raw or partly entitled parcels and develops them itself (Sutton Lakes in Winter Garden, ~200 homes, groundbreaking planned 2026; 25 acres at Babcock Ranch for 242 townhomes, 2023; Phase 1 of Walton Global's Canopy master plan in Hernando County, 76.55 acres / up to 227 lots, 2024), and it takes finished lots under contract from developers (Keewin's Cypress Park Estates in Haines City, alongside D.R. Horton, Lennar and Dream Finders; Newland homesites for Tampa communities). No land banker, lot-option financier or outside equity partner is publicly linked to the homebuilder. The family's commercial arm Kimaya raises project equity from family offices, RIAs, fund managers and institutions for build-to-rent and multifamily, so the family is used to outside capital. For a land banker: a mid-size self-developing builder with falling volume (and a VP of Land opening seen only in search snippets) is a plausible lot-option customer, but the size of any facility is unknown.

people.prior_role: Executive Vice President (2021-2026) over homebuilding in 15 eastern states; Regional President, Mid-Atlantic (2019); Group President, Metro Washington D.C. (2016); Division President, Houston (2012)
people.source_title: Toll Brothers IR: Senior Management page
people.note: CEO and director effective 2026-03-30 (8-K filed 2026-03-31, Item 5.02; appointment approved 2026-01-05). Joined 2004 through the executive training program as an Assistant Project Manager. Came up through division and regional operations in Texas and the Mid-Atlantic. On the May 2026 earnings call he said about 20% of FY2026 revenue comes from land-banked communities and about 30% of optioned lots are land-banked, and that 20% to 30% 'feels about right' going forward; his prepared remarks put seller financing, joint ventures and traditional options ahead of land banking, which Toll uses 'when it makes sense'.

Business Report land-record items name him as DSLD's signatory on lot takedowns (Zachary, Nov 2024; Reserve at Conway, Jan 2025) and call him 'one of DSLD's partners' who represented both buyer and seller when DSLD bought 71 and 83 lots from Livingston Parc LLC (Apr and Nov 2025: https://www.businessreport.com/dsld-acquires-83-more-lots-in-denham-springs-development/). In the Nov 2025 caption he refers to 'bankers and bondholders' asking how big DSLD plans to get, which implies bank lines and some form of bond debt. Business filings cited by Business Report list him and Lee Foster as directors of Pavo Capital Inc., a Baton Rouge lot-holding company (https://www.businessreport.com/this-company-just-bought-over-30-lots-in-the-highlandia-community/, Apr 2025). CFO since at least April 2014 (Business Report). No treasurer or separate capital-markets officer is published, so he appears to cover those functions. Email is built from the company pattern and is not confirmed.

people.name: Lee Foster

competitors.name: Domain Real Estate Partners
competitors.summary: What a competitor or builder can see about Domain without asking. Domain's own site gives scale ($6.7B+ current gross asset value, about $18.2B committed since 2015, 825 projects, 29 states, 91 MSAs as of 2026-10-31), its three products and its team. DW Partners' Form ADV (May 2026: $2.27B regulatory AUM) and the Domain funds' Form D filings show the vehicles and investor counts (Solaris $565M from 41 investors, Metric $333M from 3, Evergreen $205M from 9). The PGIM partnership (over $4B across seven deals by May 2026) and the CIO's podcast remarks (low-double-digit pricing, insurance private placements) are public. Lennar named Domain among its land bankers on its March 2026 call, and Commercial Observer tied DW Partners to a $164.5M Lennar land-bank site in Sunrise, FL (Jan 2026). Most notable for the team: a May 2024 Domain one-pager marked not for general distribution is downloadable without login from insuranceaum.com, showing median rate (13%), median term, monthly net returns 2016-2024, fee model, leverage cost and client names. Millrose's 10-K names DW Partners as a competitor; EDGAR full-text search finds Domain named in only one builder filing (Hovnanian, FY2015).

facts.fact: Domain's homepage 'Our Platform' block states 29 active states, 91 active MSAs, $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value and about $18.2B gross capital committed since inception, footnoted as portfolio statistics as of October 31, 2026.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage, Our Platform

facts.fact: Growth visible from Domain's own published figures: strategy assets $1.77bn (Apr 30, 2024, one-pager) to $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value (Oct 31, 2026, website), roughly 3.8x in 30 months (6.7 / 1.77; calculated; the two metrics are labelled differently so the comparison is approximate). Counterparties grew from 23 to 33 and MSAs from 52 to 91 over the same period.
facts.source_title: Domain website homepage (Oct 31, 2026) compared with Domain one-pager (Apr 30, 2024)

facts.fact: On the InsuranceAUM podcast published November 6, 2025, Bob Clark said Domain owned a little over 100,000 residential lots on behalf of builder partners, had a little over $4.7 billion invested, and had done a bit over 600 deals (the 600th closed the week before recording). He did not say whether the $4.7 billion was current or cumulative. For comparison, the April 2024 one-pager showed about 60,000 lots.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: The GSP podcast show notes (Oct 2026) say the episode covers how Domain prices deals on the builder relationship rather than deal by deal, that banks are generally not Domain's competition, that insurance capital is moving into senior land debt, and that new land bankers entering in 2026 have compressed spreads. No numeric pricing is given in the notes.
facts.source_title: George Smith Partners, The Landscape Podcast show notes

facts.fact: On the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast, Bob Clark said Domain's fund was 'annualizing' at 14% to 15% and contrasted that with a dividend yield of about 9% at Millrose; he described Domain's investments as roughly four-year amortizing positions. The transcript does not say whether the 14% to 15% is gross or net.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 with Bob Clark, transcript, Nov 6, 2025

facts.fact: A Domain one-pager (data as of April 30, 2024; prepared by DW Partners) is openly downloadable from InsuranceAUM.com and shows the then-active portfolio: $1.77bn strategy assets, $5bn total budgeted project costs, about 60,000 total lots across 52 MSAs, 159 land banks, 6 mortgage loans, 1 joint venture, 23 homebuilders and land developers, a 13% median interest rate and a 41-month median term. The document's own disclaimer says it is not intended for general distribution, yet it is reachable without login. Tagged Inferred only because the data is more than 24 months old (primary document, opened); it is the only public document found that states a rate and a term.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024 (hosted on InsuranceAUM.com)

facts.fact: The same May 2024 one-pager publishes monthly net performance for 2016 through March 2024, with calendar-year net returns between 10.60% (2017) and 15.70% (2018) and 13.63% for 2023. Its footnote discloses the model fee load used (0.50% management fee, 0.50% servicing fee, 10% performance fee over an 8% hurdle with 50/50 catch-up) and that third-party leverage has been applied since December 2017 at rates ranging from 4.75% to SOFR + 4.00%. Tagged Inferred only because the document is more than 24 months old.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024, Historical Net Performance and footnotes

facts.fact: What builder SEC filings reveal about Domain's terms: almost nothing. EDGAR full-text search for the exact phrase 'Domain Real Estate Partners' (2015 to Nov 19, 2026) returns a single document, Hovnanian's 10-K for fiscal 2015. A search for 'DW Partners' in 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K filings since 2019 returns no homebuilder filing (hits are FS-managed credit funds, Millrose, and unrelated energy and SPAC issuers). No public builder discloses a Domain-specific option fee, deposit or yield. (Negative finding derived from the search results.)
facts.source_title: SEC EDGAR full-text search results, queried 2026-11-19

facts.fact: Structure as described by Bob Clark on the October 28, 2024 InsuranceAUM podcast: Domain closes on the land and takes title, advances funds to complete finished lots, and treats the arrangement as non-recourse project finance; the builder does the development work, guarantees timing and cost, and carries entitlement risk. Pricing was described as 'low double digits'; most deals run about four years and amortize, for an effective duration of about two to two and a half years. Deposit percentages and option-fee mechanics were not disclosed. Tagged Inferred only because the source is about 25 months old; the four-year amortizing profile was repeated in November 2025.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 251 with Bob Clark, Oct 28, 2024

facts.fact: Domain's Builders page says it partners with well-capitalized public and private homebuilders and land developers nationwide and seeks long-term relationships with proven operators. No builder is named on the page, and no pricing or terms are published anywhere on the site.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Builders page

facts.fact: DW Partners' own Firm page lists 'Domain Homebuilder Finance' as one of four strategies (with RMBS, CMBS and CRE Lending), active since 2015, with two products: land banking (off-balance-sheet financing tied to builder sales pace) and first-mortgage loans for land acquisition and infrastructure development. DW's homepage describes DW as an employee-owned alternative asset manager founded in 2009 that invests in bonds and loans collateralized by real estate.
facts.source_title: DW Partners website, Firm page (copyright 2026)

facts.fact: Domain's homepage describes the firm as a capital partner to the U.S. homebuilding industry since 2015, providing capital for residential land acquisition, development and construction. Headline statistics shown: founded 2015; 825 projects financed since inception; $6.7B+ current investment gross asset value; 33 active homebuilder and land developer partners.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage (statistics footnoted as of October 31, 2026)

facts.fact: Domain publishes three strategies. Land Banking: it acquires fully entitled land and funds 100% of horizontal development into finished lots; it says it primarily partners with Top 60 U.S. homebuilders, 'predominantly the Top 25'. A&D Lending: senior-secured, non-recourse first-mortgage loans to land developers delivering finished lots to national and regional builders, typically under pre-sale commitments. Vertical Financing: financing to Top 200 U.S. homebuilders for vertical home construction.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, homepage, Our Investment Strategies

facts.fact: DW Partners' Form ADV (other-than-annual amendment dated 2026-05-01) lists 'Domain Real Estate Partners, LLC' as an other business name of DW Partners, LP, and its Schedule D note states that Domain Real Estate Partners, LLC is an entity within DW's operational structure that executes DW's residential homebuilder finance strategy, and that the individuals who use the Domain name are DW employees under DW's supervisory and compliance program. In legal terms the public record shows Domain as a DW strategy / business name rather than a separately registered adviser.
facts.source_title: DW Partners, LP Form ADV Part 1A (CRD 155459), Schedule D Section 1.B and Miscellaneous, filed 2026-05-01

facts.fact: The May 2024 one-pager gives the strategy inception as August 2015, describes land banks as off-balance-sheet financing delivering finished lots on a 'just in time' basis matched to estimated sales pace, and says deals are directly sourced from builders and developers and underwritten and managed by an in-house team. It names clients: public builders Lennar, Pulte and Toll Brothers; private builders Clayton Homes, Ashton Woods and David Weekley; land developers Eisenhower Property Group and Glenmont Development. Tagged Inferred only because the document is more than 24 months old.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners one-pager, May 2024, Investment Strategy and Partnerships

facts.fact: Domain's Investors page offers only a login link to a Juniper Square investor portal (data room, fund documents, reporting) and an investor-relations email address; no fund names, sizes or investor names are published. The site footer says any offer is made only to qualified investors by private placement memorandum.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Investors page

facts.fact: Public gap between two published scale figures: the Domain website shows $6.7B+ 'current investment gross asset value' (Oct 31, 2026) while DW's Form ADV shows $2.27B of regulatory AUM (May 2026) and about $1.19B of gross assets in Domain-named funds. Domain's own May 2024 one-pager footnote explains its 'strategy assets' as a combination of assets advised by DW and assets serviced by Domain Servicing, LLC, and PGIM has separately announced funding of more than $4B of land banking through Domain. A reader can therefore see that most of the deployed capital sits outside DW-advised funds (difference 6.7 - 2.27 = about $4.4B; inference from the cited figures, not a company statement).
facts.source_title: Domain website homepage statistics, compared with DW Form ADV 2026-05-01 and Domain one-pager May 2024

facts.fact: Domain Solaris Fund, LP (Delaware LP organized 2023, c/o DW Partners) Form D/A signed 2026-08-12: first sale 2023-08-01, indefinite offering, $564,780,000 sold to 41 investors, $1,000,000 minimum, Rule 506(b) and Section 3(c)(7), no sales compensation. General partner: DW General Partner, LLC. Signed by Houdin Honarvar as authorized signatory of the GP.
facts.source_title: Domain Solaris Fund, LP Form D/A filed 2026-08-12

facts.fact: FS Credit Opportunities Corp. (NYSE: FSCO) reports a first-lien senior secured loan to 'Domain Timberlake Note Issuer, LLC' (industry: Real Estate Management & Development) at Term SOFR + 6.50% with a 1.0% floor, maturing 12/20/2029: $29.0M principal at Dec 31, 2023, $20.3M at Dec 31, 2025 and $20.3M (fair value $20.1M) at June 30, 2026. The FSCO filings do not name DW Partners or Domain Real Estate Partners; the link to Domain is inferred from the entity name and from Bob Clark's statement that a Domain subsidiary issued a rated note in 2023. No document opened in this run states the affiliation, so treat the attribution as unconfirmed.

facts.fact: Domain's own Press page summarises the PGIM press release of May 26, 2026: PGIM and Domain have surpassed $4 billion of U.S. residential land-banking transactions across seven deals since their partnership began, using asset-based, non-bank capital, with Domain sourcing, underwriting, closing and managing each deal.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Press page (PGIM release, May 26, 2026)

facts.fact: Bisnow (May 26, 2026) reported that PGIM, Prudential Financial's asset manager, completed more than $4 billion of land-banking deals through its partnership with Domain Real Estate Partners LLC, that the partnership began in 2025 ('last year'), and that seven residential land bank transactions had been financed. No builders, deal sizes or pricing were disclosed.

facts.fact: Alternative Credit Investor (May 26, 2026) reported the PGIM-Domain partnership targets national housebuilders, sits inside PGIM's private asset-based finance platform, and that Domain had more than $6bn deployed across its portfolio at that time. facts.source_title: Alternative Credit Investor, 'PGIM and Domain hit $4bn in US land-banking deals', May 26, 2026

facts.fact: PGIM's own press release (Newark, May 26, 2026) says PGIM has surpassed $4 billion in funding for new U.S. land banking projects through its partnership with Domain, across seven completed residential land bank transactions, aimed at national homebuilders. Its 'About Domain' text says Domain has financed over 720 projects totaling about $16 billion of project costs since 2015 with more than $6 billion currently deployed; asterisked figures are footnoted as of March 31, 2026. Bob Clark is quoted as founder and CIO of Domain. The release names no builder, no deal size, no pricing and no start date.
facts.source_title: PGIM press release, 'PGIM and Domain Real Estate Partners Surpass $4 Billion in U.S. Land Banking Transactions', May 26, 2026

facts.fact: DW Partners, LP reported regulatory assets under management of $2,273,017,018 across 21 accounts, all discretionary, in its Form ADV dated 2026-05-01. Sum of the four gross asset values = $1,186.6M (calculated: 654.7 + 331.9 + 172.1 + 27.9). Auditor shown for each is Ernst & Young; custodian State Street Bank and Trust.

facts.fact: Domain Evergreen Fund, LP (Delaware LP organized 2025) Form D/A signed 2026-03-13: first sale 2025-03-03, indefinite offering, $205,086,306 sold to 9 investors, $5,000,000 minimum, Rule 506(b), no sales compensation. facts.fact: Insurance-capital note programme as described by Bob Clark on the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast: a first private placement to insurance investors closed at the end of 2024; a second followed in Q1 2025; in Q3 2025 Domain closed its first 'traditional' offering from its main finance company, a $200 million private placement of five-year and seven-year fixed-rate notes sold entirely to insurance capital; three transactions were done and two more were due to close in November 2025. facts.fact: The disclaimer on the November 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast page states that Kroll assigned an investment-grade rating to Domain's operating company in May 2025, that the rating was solicited and that Domain paid for it. facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 334 page, disclaimer

facts.fact: On the October 28, 2024 InsuranceAUM podcast Bob Clark said a 2023 portfolio financing for a very large builder was done as a note rated A- (the page attributes the A- to Egan-Jones Ratings Company for a Domain subsidiary, with no compensation paid for it), and that Domain was preparing a five-year, non-call-three private placement for one builder programme. He put the land and land development financing market at roughly $150 to $160 billion. Tagged Inferred because the source is about 25 months old.
facts.source_title: InsuranceAUM.com podcast episode 251 with Bob Clark, Oct 28, 2024

facts.fact: Domain Real Estate Fund II, LP (Delaware LP organized 2023) filed a single Form D on 2023-05-04: $5,000,000 offered and sold to 1 investor, first sale 2023-05-01, offering not intended to last more than a year. Older than 24 months with no later amendment.
facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Fund II, LP Form D filed 2023-05-04

facts.source_title: Domain Real Estate Partners website, Press page; DW Partners Press page checked the same day

facts.fact: InsuranceAUM.com lists Domain Real Estate Partners as a Platinum Partner with a public profile: founded 2015, 825 projects financed with over $18bn of project costs, products described as structured lot purchase options (land banking), non-recourse loans and project-level equity investments, and '$3BN' assets under management footnoted as of 10/31/2026. facts.fact: George Smith Partners' Landscape podcast page for 'The Land Banker's View of the Housing Market' (dated October 27, 2026 on Domain's Press page) describes Domain as one of the largest land bankers and land lenders in the country, with roughly $6.7 billion 'in the ground' and more than $17 billion funded across 750+ projects, all in for-sale residential. Guest: Bob Clark, listed as Founding Partner, DW Partners and CIO, Domain Real Estate Partners.

facts.fact: On Lennar's Q1 fiscal 2026 earnings call (March 13, 2026) Executive Chairman Stuart Miller named Domain in a list of Lennar's land banking relationships (with Millrose, Angelo Gordon, Hearthstone, Apollo and others) that he said continue to function well; Lennar said 86% of its homesites in the quarter were delivered through land bank relationships, up from 52% a year earlier, and that it controlled about 486,000 homesites versus about 11,000 owned. Domain repeats this mention on its own Press page. The Motley Fool transcript garbles 'Millrose' and 'Hearthstone'; Domain's Press page gives the clean list.

'Domain' is not mentioned.

facts.fact: Credit record as stated publicly: on the November 6, 2025 InsuranceAUM podcast Bob Clark said Domain had nothing on its credit watch list and no defaults in the portfolio; on the October 28, 2024 episode he said the strategy had no credit losses over its life. He also said in November 2025 that the firm had just passed 40 people.

facts.fact: Hovnanian's fiscal 2015 10-K (filed Dec 18, 2015) says it had recently announced a land banking arrangement with Domain Real Estate Partners for up to $125.0 million, under which it sells existing land parcels and holds an option to buy back finished lots subject to a cost of carry, and that such land banking transactions are accounted for as financings rather than sales because of the repurchase options. competitors.name: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management
competitors.summary: Kennedy Lewis Investment Management manages Millrose and runs a separate private land-banking business with its own capital (Fund III, Fund IV and Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co, 'KLRES'), built from 2021 around a team that came from Domain. It signs builder commitments (New Home/Landsea, Dream Finders/Beazer, Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI) and then allocates them, so far mostly to Millrose; the August 2026 amendment to Millrose's management agreement loosened the rules on how deals are split with its private vehicles. Private-fund pricing and book size are not public; Millrose's non-Lennar yield (about 10.8%) is the best public proxy.

facts.fact: Proxy for Kennedy Lewis pricing via its public vehicle: Millrose's weighted average yield on non-Lennar agreements was about 10.8% in Q3 2026 (10.6% in Q2), guided to about 11% in Q4; the Lennar master program is cited at 8.5%; the Dream Finders preferred carries a 12% dividend.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: The New Home commitment letter names the fee stack (Initial Option Fee, Monthly Option Fee, Termination Fee, Asset Management Fee and a Minimum Project Return) but puts every number in a separate fee letter that was not filed. Kennedy Lewis's rates to builders in its private funds are not public.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Template terms from Kennedy Lewis's 2025-05-12 commitment letter for a $700 million land bank to The New Home Company ('Project Lakeland'): up to $600 million funded at closing plus up to $100 million for horizontal development; Kennedy Lewis buys the properties, grants homesite options and pays development cost up to a guaranteed contract sum under construction agreements; no option term over 72 months; builder may stretch a takedown schedule by up to 20% before closing and take three quarterly deferrals per project.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Same letter, risk protections: properties are grouped into pools of at least four projects; a builder walk-away on one option lets Kennedy Lewis terminate the rest of that pool (cross-termination), while builder's total payment obligation per pool is capped at $20 million; aggregate takedown price must be at least 105.25% of the closing commitment amount; builder pays diligence costs and expenses even if the deal does not close; funding was conditional on at least $650 million of sponsor equity.
facts.source_title: KLIM land bank commitment letter to The New Home Company, 2025-05-12 (Landsea Schedule TO Ex. (b)(1))

facts.fact: Scale with Lennar before and around Millrose: Hunterbrook reports that Lennar and Kennedy Lewis began a land-banking partnership in 2021 and that Millrose's investor presentation cites '$4.5B+' of land-banking transactions between the two since 2022. Kennedy Lewis has not published a total for dollars, lots or number of builders in its private strategy.
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook Media, 2026-10-02

facts.fact: Hunterbrook, quoting the Millrose prospectus, reports that Lennar picked Kennedy Lewis as Millrose's manager without a competitive selection process and that Kennedy Lewis served as Lennar's unpaid strategic adviser on the spin-off's structure and contracts; it dates the Richman-Lennar relationship back about two decades (he covered Lennar as a Goldman Sachs high-yield analyst).
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook Media, 2026-10-02

facts.fact: Millrose's FY2025 10-K states that Kennedy Lewis acted as Lennar's strategic advisor while the Lennar agreements were prepared and that it had no prior experience managing a public company.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: The FY2025 10-K places the asset-servicing arm's staff in Scottsdale, Arizona and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (Kennedy Lewis HQ New York; other offices Miami and Geneva). The part of that filing read in this run did not name the servicer's leader.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: Millrose's FY2024 10-K lists Kennedy Lewis itself among the key competitors in the land-banking market and warns that Kennedy Lewis manages land-banking entities that compete with Millrose for opportunities and resources. The glossary names two: Fund III (Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners Master Fund III LP and parallel vehicles) and KLRES (Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company LP).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: Platform: Kennedy Lewis runs an in-house land-banking servicer / asset-management division that monitors horizontal development pace and community sales, handles capital disbursements, homesite sales and monthly option-payment collection, and supports diligence. The FY2024 10-K says it is led by David Valiaveedan and staffed by people who worked at Lennar, Hovnanian, Beazer, Toll Brothers, Woodbridge Builders and the land-banking platforms of DW Partners and Blackstone Credit; the Manager's underwriting team has more than 30 diligence professionals.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: In August 2024 Kennedy Lewis added 12 people from Gibraltar Real Estate Capital (a residential development capital provider) and folded them into KL Servicers, its unit for asset monitoring, servicing and diligence on land-banking investments. Gibraltar co-founders Roger Brush and Michael Lapat joined as managing directors; they had executed about $3.5 billion of transactions across 25 states. The firm was put at $16 billion AUM in the article.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch, 2024-08-14

facts.fact: Kennedy Lewis describes the product as 'homebuilder finance': structured capital for US homebuilders to buy land and complete horizontal development capital-efficiently and relieve balance-sheet pressure. Its flagship opportunistic credit fund (Fund III) carries exposure to the strategy alongside its other credit verticals.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2023-11-07 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: Kennedy Lewis built its homebuilder-finance / land-banking strategy by hiring David Valiaveedan and Brieanne Nikrandt as Managing Directors on 2021-06-28 'to lead the firm's homebuilder financing strategy'. Both came from DW Partners, where they had led residential investments since 2015; Valiaveedan formed and led DW's Domain Real Estate Partners and was earlier VP Finance & Treasurer of Hovnanian. Kennedy Lewis had about $7 billion of AUM at the time.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2021-06-28 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: EDGAR shows only two filings for KLRES (Form D 2023-10-10 and D/A 2024-10-11) as of 2026-11-19: no 2025 or 2026 amendment. Inferred (from the absence of the annual amendment an ongoing offering requires): the KLRES offering probably stopped taking new money before October 2025; final size not disclosed.
facts.source_title: SEC EDGAR submissions listing, CIK 1995205

facts.fact: On the Q3 2026 call management said the fee is 1.25% of gross tangible assets excluding the new single-family-rental portfolio: Kennedy Lewis proposed leaving SFR homes out of the fee base while the product is unproven, and acknowledged that the $250 million buyback shrinks its own fee base.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: A third-party Form ADV aggregator lists KLRES at $886.8 million gross asset value, 103 beneficial owners, $10 million minimum investment, adviser Kennedy Lewis Management LP, auditor Deloitte, administrator HedgeServ, custodian JPMorgan (page shows data through Oct 2026; exact Form ADV date not shown).
facts.source_title: PrivateFundData.com profile of Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company LP

facts.fact: Millrose management fee expense was $30.264 million for Q3 2026 (Q3 2025: $25.895 million) and $88.325 million for the nine months to 2026-09-30 (2025: $59.959 million). Inferred run-rate: about $121 million a year (Q3 x 4).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations

facts.fact: Across five Fund IV vehicles filed 2026-09-21 (Domestic $1.46bn, Co-Inv Domestic $319.1m, Offshore $248.3m, USTE $146.1m, Co-Inv USTE $23.0m) about $2.19 billion had been sold, per a trade summary of the Form Ds. Fund IV is the successor to Fund III and may allocate to land banking.
facts.source_title: Angellinx market insights, 2026-09-22

facts.fact: Fund IV: KLCP Domestic Fund IV LP Form D/A signed 2026-09-21 shows a $4.5 billion total offering, $1,456.4 million sold to 40 investors, first sale 2024-12-31; placement agents PJT Partners, Rockefeller Capital Management and Cleopatra Consulting UK. This is the main domestic vehicle only.
facts.source_title: Form D/A, KLCP Domestic Fund IV LP (filed 2026-09-21)

facts.fact: 2026-08-27 amendment to the management agreement: property-level operating costs of single-family rental homes became a Millrose-paid 'Reimbursable Expense' (the Manager still bears other operating expenses), and the investment guidelines were restated to cover homesites for single-family detached/attached homes including homes held as rentals under an approved SFR strategy. Signed for both sides by Robert Nitkin.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Lennar and the Manager: no Lennar equity stake in the Manager is disclosed. Lennar instead holds contractual consent rights under the Founder's Rights Agreement over any successor manager or management agreement, over replacement of the key men (Chene and Richman), and over transfers of Manager membership interests to homebuilders. After its Oct-Nov 2025 exchange offer Lennar held only a de minimis amount of Millrose stock.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Ownership: the 2026 proxy lists no Kennedy Lewis entity among 5% holders of Millrose. Darren Richman beneficially owned 265,000 Class A shares (under 1%) as of 2026-03-23. Certain Millrose officers have ownership and financial interests in Kennedy Lewis.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Latest firm AUM in a primary source: 'in excess of $33.0 billion' as of 2025-12-31, including Millrose at its gross assets (AUM method varies by fund and counts commitments).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 / Item 1A

facts.fact: Millrose paid the Kennedy Lewis manager about $87.8 million of management fee for 2025.
facts.source_title: Millrose DEF 14A filed 2026-04-02

facts.fact: Earlier firm AUM points: over $25 billion including Millrose as of 2025-03-25 (funded and unfunded commitments), per the Millrose FY2024 10-K. Other releases cited in this file give about $7bn (June 2021), about $14bn (Nov 2023), $16bn (Aug 2024, trade press) and about $30bn (July 2025, Taylor Morrison release).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024 (filed 2025-03), Item 1 Business / Our Manager

facts.fact: Fee from Millrose: 1.25% a year of Tangible Assets (0.3125% a quarter, paid in advance), payable regardless of performance; the Manager pays Millrose's ordinary operating costs and officer compensation out of the fee. Initial term three years from 2025-02-07 with one-year renewals; termination fee is 3.0x average annual fee if 3-year average ROE is at least 7%, otherwise 2.5x (accelerated) or 1.5x (at expiry).
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

facts.fact: The management agreement treats an assignment to a homebuilder or homesite developer, or certain changes of control involving David K. Chene or Darren L. Richman, as an assignment of the agreement (i.e. needing consent).
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

facts.fact: KLRES Form D/A (signed 2024-10-10): $724.7 million sold ($724,737,665) to 79 investors, offering still indefinite, PJT Partners LP named as placement agent, signed by Anthony Pasqua as authorized signatory.
facts.source_title: Form D/A, Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP (filed 2024-10-11)

facts.fact: Petershill (Goldman Sachs Asset Management) made a strategic investment in Kennedy Lewis, referenced by Alternatives Watch in Aug 2024 as 'recent'; Richman tied the Gibraltar team hire to growth after that investment. Stake size not found. The exact announcement date (2024-04-02) was seen only in a search-result headline, not opened.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch, 2024-08-14

facts.fact: Fund III: Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners Master Fund III LP and parallel / co-investment vehicles closed at $4.1 billion on 2023-11-07 against a $3 billion target, about 50% deployed at close; investors are pensions, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, foundations and endowments. Fund III is a named 'Priority Account' for land banking under the Millrose allocation policy.
facts.source_title: Kennedy Lewis press release 2023-11-07 (PR Newswire)

facts.fact: Dedicated land vehicle: Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP ('KLRES', Delaware LP formed 2023, GP Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company GP LLC). Original Form D (signed 2023-10-04): first sale 2023-10-02, $410.0 million sold to 3 investors, offering size indefinite, exemptions 506(b) and 3(c)(1)/3(c)(7).
facts.source_title: Form D, Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Co LP (filed 2023-10-10)

facts.fact: Positioning of private capital against Millrose: on the Q3 2026 call management said no Kennedy Lewis-managed vehicle outside Millrose took part in the roughly $1.1 billion Dream Finders / Beazer financing, and Richman pointed to Kennedy Lewis's access to 'hundreds of blue chip LPs'. Millrose then had 22 counterparties.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (2026-10-27), Webull copy

facts.fact: Restated allocation policy (2026-08-27): Priority Accounts are now any Kennedy Lewis-managed entity allocating capital to land banking (Fund III and KLRES and their affiliated/successor vehicles are named). The terms 'Overflow Funds' and '$1B Allocation' no longer appear. The ban on raising outside land-banking capital now applies only 'as long as Millrose has Available Capital'; Fund IV and KLRES (and successors) may raise without board consent; new successor funds and new land-banking-focused vehicles count as Priority Accounts in the rotation. Reading the two versions side by side is this agent's comparison: confirm in the exhibit.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Under both versions Millrose's 'Available Capital' excludes capital subject to Lennar's Capital Priority Right, the rotation ends when the private accounts' investment periods end (then everything goes to Millrose if it has capital), and the Manager reports rotation and follow-on allocations to the Millrose board each quarter.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Millrose Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27, 8-K Ex. 10.2 (restated Exhibit C Allocation Policy)

facts.fact: Counterparty change: Taylor Morrison, Kennedy Lewis's largest disclosed non-Lennar builder relationship ($3 billion Yardly facility plus a for-sale land bank), was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on 2026-07-24 for $72.50 a share in cash and has delisted. The 8-K does not mention the Kennedy Lewis facilities.
facts.source_title: Taylor Morrison 8-K filed 2026-07-24 (merger closing)

facts.fact: In the Landsea deal the commitment was signed by Kennedy Lewis Investment Management, LLC 'and/or its affiliates' (Darren Richman, authorized signatory) with no fund named; the funding was then placed in Millrose, which provided more than $500 million. This is the 'manager commits, then allocates' pattern a rival will meet.
facts.source_title: Cox, Castle & Nicholson deal announcement, 2025-07-21

facts.fact: Original allocation policy (2025-02-07): 'Priority Accounts' were Fund III (incl. KLIM Delta HQ3 LP and Kennedy Lewis Capital Partners (EU) SPV LP) and KLRES. Deals directed to Millrose by Lennar or a builder went 100% to Millrose; follow-ons on existing Kennedy Lewis land banks could go 100% to the private funds; all other deals suitable for both alternated on a rotation starting with Millrose. 'Overflow Funds' got deals only if neither Millrose nor a Priority Account had capital. A builder could opt out in writing ('Non-Millrose Deal').
facts.source_title: Millrose Management Agreement with Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors, 8-K Ex. 10.1 (2025-02-07), incl. Exhibit C Allocation Policy

competitors.name: Millrose Properties, Inc. (NYSE: MRP)
competitors.manager_or_parent: Externally managed by Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC (Kennedy Lewis Investment Management)
competitors.summary: Millrose (NYSE: MRP) is the only land banker that must publish its book. Spun out of Lennar on 2025-02-07 and run for a 1.25%-of-assets fee by Kennedy Lewis, it had $9.25B invested at 2026-09-30 across 156,729 homesites, 834 communities, 30 states and 22 builder counterparties. Lennar is 63.5% of capital at a fixed 8.5% under filed master agreements; the other 21 builders pay a floating 10.8% (floors about 10%, deposits about 10%, 95-96% of capital in cross-termination pools), but only five non-Lennar names are public: New Home Co (Landsea take-private, about $700M), Dream Finders (Beazer takeover, about $1.07B incl. a $488M 12% preferred), Taylor Morrison's Yardly, JPI (multifamily) and Rausch Coleman's seller-side holdback. It has reported no builder walk-aways, forfeitures or renegotiations since inception. Its constraint is capital: debt-to-capitalization 36% against a 33% target after $1.0B of 6.50%/6.75% notes and a new unsecured bank facility, and it will not issue equity below book ($35.24), so growth now comes from takedown recycling, a $250M buyback signals the stock is cheap, and the August 2026 amendments opened rentals. Lennar's founder rights (most-favoured rate, capital priority, pool caps of $50M/$25M at risk per pool) shape what Millrose can offer everyone else.

facts.fact: Rate for future Lennar deals: Risk Spread (Bloomberg US Composite BBB BVAL Yield Curve 3-year index) + a 4.00% spread + a Rating Adjustment, with a 7% minimum and 10% maximum. It is struck on a monthly calculation date (first business day of the month) and then stays fixed for that project's life.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Schedule 1

facts.fact: Rating Adjustment in the Lennar formula: zero while Lennar Corporation is rated Baa1-Baa3 / BBB+ to BBB- (two of three agencies); minus 0.5% on an upgrade to A3 / A-, and a further minus 0.25% per notch above that; plus 1.0% on a downgrade to Ba1 (Moody's) or BB (S&P, Fitch) as the agreement words it, and a further plus 0.25% per notch below. Lennar was rated Baa2/BBB at the spin.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Schedule 1

facts.fact: Monthly option payment = Invested Capital x Applicable Rate / 360, calculated daily. Invested Capital is what Millrose has paid for acquisition and improvements, less takedown prices and other builder payments received (the 5% up-front option payment reduces it). Due within 10 days of Millrose's monthly statement; non-refundable and not credited against takedown prices.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 1.7

facts.fact: Founder's Rights floor on other customers' pricing: for 18 months from 2025-02-07, Millrose may issue equity to another customer in exchange for future property assets only if that customer's option rate is at least the lower of 9.5% and Lennar's Applicable Rate plus 1%.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.04

facts.fact: Most-favoured-rate clause: if any Millrose affiliate agrees a lower option rate with a third party, Lennar may match that lower rate on all its new future property assets acquired or initiated within 180 days after the event; Millrose must notify Lennar promptly and reimburse the difference if it fails to. Deals for Lennar-related ventures do not get this matching right.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.04

facts.fact: Default interest under the Lennar Master Option Agreement accrues at the property's Applicable Rate plus 5% (or the legal maximum if lower).
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 17.5

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): management said no customer has terminated, threatened to terminate or asked to renegotiate, including on the roughly $800M of land that cycled in Q3. facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Millrose states that no counterparty has exercised its option to terminate since inception (Q3 2026 deck, as of 2026-09-30); the Q1 and Q2 2026 releases likewise report zero option terminations. No impairments were reported in 2026; the only credit item was a $0.9M credit-loss benefit in Q2 2026 on development loans.
