facts.fact: Builder deposit roll-forward, nine months to 2026-09-30: opening $927.0M, additions $199.4M, applied on takedowns $(123.2)M, closing $1,003.2M. No options were terminated, forfeited or expired unexercised in Q3 or the nine months, so no forfeited-deposit income was recognized.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 2 (Builder deposits; Preferred instruments; Development guarantee holdback)

facts.fact: Dream Finders preferred terms as disclosed by Millrose: perpetual, no maturity or mandatory redemption; 12.0% cumulative dividend paid quarterly in arrears; Dream Finders may redeem from the third anniversary of issuance; Millrose may convert into Dream Finders common stock from the sixth anniversary; holder redemption/conversion rights on specified events. Carried at cost (ASC 321 measurement alternative).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 2 (Builder deposits; Preferred instruments; Development guarantee holdback)

facts.fact: The $100M development guarantee holdback owed to Rausch Coleman Companies becomes payable within ten business days of the later of 2027-02-10 (two years after the acquisition) or completion of development on 50% of the guaranteed assets, reduced by any development cost overruns.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 2 (Builder deposits; Preferred instruments; Development guarantee holdback)

facts.fact: Homesites under option roll-forward, nine months to 2026-09-30: opening $8,872.7M, investments $3,349.7M (about $1.4B land acquisitions and $1.9B development costs), takedowns $(2,320.0)M, closing $9,902.4M. Millrose reports no delinquencies or defaults by any counterparty since inception and treats expected credit loss on the option book as immaterial, citing non-refundable deposits, contractual termination fees and cross-collateralization.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 4 Homesites Under Option Contracts

facts.fact: Purchase-money mortgage structure: in 2025 Millrose bought two land parcels for $33M with non-recourse property-level mortgages that a counterparty fully indemnifies and services (pays all interest); Millrose intends to sign an option agreement with that counterparty at maturity ($4M due Q4 2026, $29M in 2027).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 11 Debt

facts.fact: On 2026-08-27 Millrose and Lennar amended the Founder's Rights Agreement: a new defined term 'BTR Properties' (completed single-family homes held as rentals); 'Excluded Capital' restated as the first $2B of debt and equity from any source plus all capital raised solely to fund BTR Properties; and Lennar's secured-financing collateral consent right restated so that Lennar-program properties cannot be pledged alongside other customers' optioned properties without Lennar's consent, while separate secured financing of BTR Properties is allowed.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Founder's Rights Agreement dated 2026-08-27 (8-K Ex. 10.1)

facts.fact: The Management Agreement was amended on 2026-08-27: the investment guidelines now expressly allow single-family homes held and operated as rentals under an approved rental strategy; property-level operating costs of rental homes and the cost of holding land after a counterparty fails to exercise its option are reimbursable by Millrose; and the manager's investment allocation policy (Exhibit C) was replaced in full: opportunities directed to Millrose go 100% to Millrose when it has capacity, shared opportunities rotate between Millrose and Kennedy Lewis accounts, with quarterly reporting to the board and limits on Kennedy Lewis fundraising for land banking.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27 (Millrose 8-K Ex. 10.2, filed 2026-09-01)

facts.fact: The Founder's Rights Agreement with Lennar was amended on 2026-08-27: 'Excluded Capital' (capital outside Lennar's priority right) is the first $2B of debt and equity from any source plus all capital raised solely to fund rental-home ('BTR Properties') purchases; Lennar's consent is required before a Lennar-program property is pledged in a secured financing that also pledges another customer's property. Signed for Millrose by COO Robert Nitkin and for the Lennar entities by Diane Bessette and Katherine Lee Martin.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Founder's Rights Agreement dated 2026-08-27 (Millrose 8-K Ex. 10.1, filed 2026-09-01)

facts.fact: Risk controls described around Q2 2026 results: large deposits plus cross-termination pooling (walking from one property can trigger penalties or forfeitures across the pool), a focus on entitled land in supply-constrained markets, and in the softer market a tilt to stronger builders, less development complexity and more margin of safety (Richman, per HousingWire).
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily, 'Millrose Q2 2026 results build on new partnerships, growth mojo' (2026-08-07)

facts.fact: Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04): Richman said deposits are about 10% today versus roughly 20 to 25% historically, framing the lower level as offset by other credit enhancement (pooling); Millrose underwrites to a 20%+ builder gross margin assuming flat home prices. He noted several public builders had booked walk-away charges on parcels elsewhere, and that Millrose's fallback plans if a builder walked are re-optioning to another (possibly larger) builder or selling to a merchant builder. (Machine transcript; wording approximate.)
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-08-04 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Under the Lennar Master Program Agreement, Lennar's payment obligations are capped at $50M per pool for spin-off assets and $25M per pool for other admitted properties (the 10-K does not spell out which payments the cap covers). A Lennar party can cure a default by electing a bulk purchase of the affected property, which cancels cross-termination rights already exercised.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Option deposits are non-refundable, fully earned at signing, set as a percentage of the land purchase price in each agreement, and credited against the takedown price; the percentage is not disclosed for Lennar or anyone else. Takedown price is land acquisition cost plus the pre-agreed development budget funded by Millrose; the builder bears overruns above the agreed maximum and must finish land development even if it walks.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Investment guidelines in the management agreement: no more than 40% of the real estate portfolio's value in one state; limited discretionary entitlement risk; a construction agreement with cost-overrun guarantees and an option agreement with a defined takedown schedule at closing; single-family detached or attached product only; an environmental assessment no older than 180 days. No single-counterparty or single-metro limit is stated.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Lennar's continuing rights: a 'Capital Priority Right' reserving part of Millrose's available capital for future Lennar-designated acquisitions and development (amount not stated), approval over any financing that would take debt-to-equity above 1:1, and a consent right over mixing Lennar-related assets into a shared collateral pool. Millrose's own leverage ceiling is 33% debt-to-capitalization.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Q4 2025 call (2026-02-26): 96% of the portfolio by investment balance is in cross-termination pools; COO Robert Nitkin said pooling does not stop a builder walking but raises the cost. Q1 2026 call put the pooled share at about 95% of $8.7B invested capital. Management also cited about $9B of forward-flow relationships across roughly 10 counterparties.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript, 2026-02-26 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: Cross-termination pooling: at 2025-12-31, 96% of Millrose's portfolio investment balance was in pooling arrangements. If a counterparty lets its option lapse on one pooled property it forfeits the option deposits for the whole pool and Millrose may terminate the options on the other pooled properties and sell them free of the option. Pools are built to mix geographies, communities and product types.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Deposit levels implied by disclosed deals (all calculated): spin-off assets $584.8M of deposits on $5,556M of land contributed (about 10.5%); Rausch $90.3M on $1,049M of land (about 8.6%); New Home / Landsea $28.3M on $522.8M (about 5.4%). At 2025-12-31 Lennar-related option deposit liabilities were $726.7M against $6.9B of homesites (about 10.5%).
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 5 Related Party Transactions

facts.fact: Builder deposit liability roll-forward for 2025: $584.8M from the spin-off, $90.3M from Rausch, $417.0M of additions, less $165.1M credited on takedowns, ending at $927.0M at 2025-12-31.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 2 Significant Accounting Policies

facts.fact: Deposits netted in the invested-capital reconciliation at 2025-12-31 were $482.7M ($201.9M Lennar Master Program, $280.8M Other Agreements) versus $927.0M of builder deposits on the balance sheet; the release does not explain the difference. On that basis Other Agreements deposits equal about 12.0% of the $2,341.9M of Other Agreements homesites (calculated).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 / FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Weighted-average remaining life at 2025-12-31: 3.3 years Lennar Master Program, 2.0 years Other Agreements, 3.0 years total; weighted-average maturity (months to the final scheduled homesite sale per community, weighted by investment balance): 64, 35 and 57 months.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Accounting and credit: option contracts are treated as sales-type leases under ASC 842 because exercise is considered reasonably certain; option fee income is recognized on an effective-yield basis. Millrose reported no delinquencies, defaults or option terminations in 2025 and judged credit loss on the option assets immaterial; the only allowance is $1.0M on development loans.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 4 Homesites Under Option Contracts

facts.fact: Future land development funding commitments at 2025-12-31: $5.8B under Lennar option contracts and $1.6B under other counterparties' option contracts.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 9 Commitments and Contingencies

facts.fact: Expected undiscounted option fee cash flows on contracts in place at 2025-12-31: $792.0M (2026), $726.1M (2027), $524.7M (2028), $331.8M (2029), $224.4M (2030) and $516.5M thereafter.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 4 Homesites Under Option Contracts

facts.fact: At 2025-09-30 the invested-capital reconciliation netted $392.3M of builder deposits: $171.0M under the Master Program Agreement and $221.3M under Other Agreements.
facts.source_title: Millrose preliminary Q3 2025 results press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2025-10-09)

facts.fact: Land development commitments at 2025-09-30: $5.9B under Lennar option contracts and $1.4B under other customers' option contracts.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2025, Note 8 Commitments and Contingencies

facts.fact: At 2025-06-30 all Lennar assets were pooled and 55 communities outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement were pooled for cross-termination, per the Q2 deck's pooling slide (the Q1 deck had said no third-party assets were pooled).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2025 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2025-07-31)

facts.fact: Land development commitments at 2025-06-30: $5.7B under Lennar option contracts and $0.6B under other customers' option contracts.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q2 2025, Note 8 Commitments and Contingencies

facts.fact: Takedown price has no premium or escalator: per the 10-K it is the property's acquisition price plus the pre-set horizontal development budget, allocated per homesite in the takedown schedule of each Project Addendum. Millrose's return is the option fee alone. The seed book shows it: about $6.6 billion of value plus about $4 billion of development to fund against $10.9 billion of scheduled takedown prices.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1 (Lennar Agreements) and Item 2

facts.fact: Number of pools: the January 2025 prospectus described the seed assets as pooled into 21 pools averaging 41 properties each; the FY2024 10-K (March 2025) says the Transferred and Supplemental Transferred Assets are pooled into 30 pools averaging 29 properties each. The 10-K is the newer figure.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1 and Item 2

facts.fact: Put-back right: Millrose can sell a property back to Lennar at Millrose's total capital investment if there was a material misrepresentation on title, environmental matters or permits and approvals.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1 (Lennar Agreements)

facts.fact: Land development commitments at 2025-03-31 were $5.3B in total (no Lennar / other split given).
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q1 2025, Commitments and Contingencies note

facts.fact: Walk-away cost for Lennar on a property: it forfeits the 5% up-front payment, owes the unpaid part of the 5% Additional Deposit as a termination fee, must complete the horizontal work in the pool, and loses its options on the other properties in that pool if Millrose cross-terminates.
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, February 2025 (8-K 2025-02-24, Exhibit 99.1), slide 29 (Master Option Agreement)

facts.fact: Deposits under the Lennar Master Option Agreement: (1) an up-front 'Option Payment' (called the Initial Deposit in the 10-K) of 5% of projected total land acquisition and development costs, fully earned when paid; (2) an 'Additional Deposit' of up to 5% of the takedown price of homesites still under option, which Millrose can call as a prepayment on 20 business days' notice when it needs ordinary-course cash flow (credited dollar-for-dollar to takedowns) or which falls due as an Option Termination Payment within 20 business days after Lennar terminates. The two forms of additional deposit together cannot exceed 5%.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.6 and 1.9

facts.fact: Lennar's failure to exercise an option or to make a monthly option payment is not a 'default' under the Master Option Agreement: the option simply ends. Millrose's remedies on a builder default are to terminate, keep the option consideration and claim direct damages; it cannot force Lennar to buy and cannot recover consequential or punitive damages.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.3 and 17

facts.fact: Cross-termination mechanics (form of Multiparty Cross Agreement): a Cross Termination Event occurs when the option on any pool property ends for a reason other than Millrose's default and Lennar has not bought all its homesites. Millrose then has 20 business days to elect to terminate the options on other properties in that pool, or the right is waived. Each pool's agreement operates independently of the others.
facts.source_title: Form of Multiparty Cross Agreement (8-K Exhibit 10.8), Section 3

facts.fact: Carve-outs from cross-termination: Lennar can cure a single-property default by a bulk purchase where the default cannot be cured by payment and is outside its control; a termination because Lennar bought every homesite does not count; and if Millrose asks Lennar to fee-build the terminated property the event is treated as cured. Where a property is terminated for Lennar's default, remedies are confined to that property.
facts.source_title: Form of Multiparty Cross Agreement (8-K Exhibit 10.8), Section 3(a)-(c)

facts.fact: Pool sizing rule: Lennar's 'Total Payment Obligation' per pool (all 5% option payments plus all additional deposits made or owed for properties in the pool) may never exceed $50 million for pools of seed properties or $25 million for pools of future properties. Lennar proposes the pools, Millrose's approval cannot be unreasonably withheld, 'primary consideration' goes to diversity by geography, community and home type, and pools must be structured to stay off Lennar's balance sheet.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(a)

facts.fact: Inferred from the pool caps: with up to 10% of cost at stake per property (5% up front plus up to 5% additional), a $50 million cap implies a seed pool of roughly $500 million of takedown value and a $25 million cap a future pool of roughly $250 million. That is the most Lennar loses by abandoning an entire pool. Calculation: cap / 10%.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(a)

facts.fact: Takedown flexibility for Lennar: up to four quarterly extensions of a takedown on five business days' notice with no extension fee stated (it must be caught up by the final takedown); it may accelerate takedowns up to 50% of a pool's homesites, and a bulk purchase above 50% requires buying every homesite in the pool.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 1.4

facts.fact: Pause periods in the option agreement: up to two pauses of up to six months each per property, triggered by a seasonally adjusted home-price decline of 10% or more in the MSA on the Burns index (measured from the deal's effective date) or a pandemic / public health emergency; two more six-month pauses with Millrose's approval, not to be unreasonably withheld, if the condition persists. During a pause takedown and construction deadlines extend, no closings happen and the fee runs at the Pause Rate, 50% of the Applicable Rate.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Section 1.4(e)

facts.fact: Lennar can also call pauses at its sole discretion under the Founder's Rights Agreement (still capped at two per community in total, six months each, at half rate), but while any Lennar property is in such a pause Lennar loses its most-favoured-rate right on new deals.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.07

facts.fact: Carry costs sit with the builder: Lennar pays real estate taxes, assessments, HOA dues, utilities, maintenance and insurance on optioned property through the option termination date, plus closing costs and transfer taxes at takedown.
facts.source_title: Master Option Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.6), Sections 1.8, 6 and 8

facts.fact: After a termination Lennar has no right of first offer or refusal on the retained land. It has 90 days to buy homesites where it has started vertical construction, otherwise it must remove the construction on request. Millrose may within 20 days ask Lennar to act as fee builder on the land, which Lennar must do only where it is active in that market, for a management fee of 20% of reimbursable costs plus overhead and sales fees, paid by Millrose.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Section 2(d) and Exhibit E (form of Fee Builder Agreement)

facts.fact: Program has no end date and no volume commitment from Lennar: the acquisition period runs until both sides agree in writing to stop admitting properties; Lennar need not offer deals and grants no exclusivity, first look or right of first refusal. The obligation runs the other way: while Lennar has capital reserved, Millrose must on Lennar's request acquire every proposed project that meets the Program Criteria, signing documents within 15 business days.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Sections 2(b), 4(a), 4(c), 4(e)

facts.fact: Program Criteria (the Lennar buy-box): all material discretionary approvals obtained (entitled land only); primary use single-family detached or attached homesites; no building moratorium; a Phase I environmental report dated within 180 days of closing; a full takedown schedule; Lennar responsible for finished-homesite costs above the contract sum; and Millrose need not buy if more than 40% of total committed capital would sit in a single state.
facts.source_title: Master Program Agreement, Millrose / Lennar entities, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.5), Exhibit F

facts.fact: Development funding: Millrose funds horizontal development up to the budgeted contract sum under the Master Construction Agreement; Lennar performs the work as contractor and is solely responsible for cost overruns unless an independent consultant determines otherwise; home construction is outside the funded work. Lennar Corporation backs this with an unlimited parent Payment and Performance Guaranty covering the program, option and construction agreements.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01

facts.fact: Founder's Rights Agreement (2025-02-07; Millrose with U.S. Home, Lennar Homes Holding and CalAtlantic) gives Lennar eight rights: management succession consent, equity price protection, capital priority, enforcement, rate adjustment, the debt-to-equity limit, secured-financing collateral consent, and pause designation. Millrose may not grant these rights to anyone else without Lennar's consent. Most last until Lennar-contributed cash and capital assets fall below 10% of Millrose's total GAAP assets for six consecutive months.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Articles II-III

facts.fact: Capital Priority Right: from 2026-03-01 and every three months after, Lennar may reserve Millrose capital for its own deals for the next three-month period; what it does not reserve is lost ('use it or lose it'), though lost amounts not committed to third parties are restored at the next date. The reservable pool is Lennar's initial capital (the value of the contributed assets, about $5.2 billion of land book value plus cash per the recitals) and recycled capital, plus 25% of new non-revolver debt and 25% of new equity that Millrose raises beyond the first $2 billion, capped at $10 billion less the initial capital. If Millrose cannot fund a committed Lennar deal it owes Lennar's damages including replacement financing cost.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.03

facts.fact: Enforcement Rights: if Millrose fails to convey a homesite within 10 days after notice, Lennar gets specific performance without bond, pre-agreed confession of judgment and attorney-in-fact powers, and may stop monthly option payments across all programs until cured. If Millrose disputes in good faith on a pooling-violation claim Lennar keeps paying, and the loser of the dispute pays the other three times the monthly option payments made during the dispute period.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Article IV

facts.fact: Equity price protection: if within 18 months of 2025-02-07 another customer receives Millrose equity for future property assets worth more than $500 million at a per-share price below Lennar's effective price, Millrose must issue extra Class A shares at no cost so that the original spin shares are re-priced to the lower level (the new customer does not participate).
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Section 3.02

facts.fact: Lennar consent is required to replace the manager (not to be unreasonably withheld; 10 business days to object) and to approve successors to the named key men, David K. Chene and Darren L. Richman. Lennar's consent, in its sole discretion, is also needed before any Lennar-optioned property is pledged in a financing alongside property optioned to another customer.
facts.source_title: Founder's Rights Agreement, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.2), Sections 3.01 and 3.06

facts.fact: Recognition, Subordination and Non-Disturbance Agreement (2025-02-07): Lennar subordinates its option rights to Millrose's intercompany mortgages and pledge; Millrose must give 10 business days' notice before foreclosing and Lennar may buy the note for the amount owed.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01

facts.fact: HOPP'R ('Homesite Option Purchase Platform') is Lennar's, not Millrose's: Lennar-Millrose HOPP'R, LLC sublicenses the rights to Millrose Holdings on a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, non-transferable basis for internal use, perpetual subject to limited termination conditions. Lennar may license the same platform to other land banks.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2025-02-07 (spin-off completion), Item 1.01 (Sublicense Agreement)

facts.fact: Management Agreement (2025-02-07): the manager is Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Kennedy Lewis Investment Management. Fee is 1.25% per annum of Tangible Assets (0.3125% a quarter), paid quarterly in advance on 1 January, April, July and October, and payable regardless of performance. Through about the first 12 months the base is total assets including cash, less intangibles and non-revenue-generating assets; after that cash is excluded.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 1 and 10

facts.fact: There is no incentive fee, carried interest or equity grant to the manager in the Management Agreement. Out of the 1.25% the manager pays all company operating expenses, including officers and directors' cash fees up to $1.25 million a year (growing 3% a year). Millrose reimburses only offering costs, extraordinary litigation and M&A costs, and the cost of owning and maintaining land where a builder failed to exercise its option.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 1 and 11

facts.fact: Manager term and exit: three-year initial term to 2028-02-07, then automatic one-year renewals. Millrose can end it without cause only on 180 days' notice, with a two-thirds vote of independent directors during the initial term (majority at a term end), on grounds of materially detrimental performance or an excessive fee. Termination for cause (uncured material breach, insolvency, fraud or gross negligence, dissolution) takes a majority of independent directors, 30 days' notice and no fee.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Sections 14-15

facts.fact: Manager termination fee: 3.0x the average annual management fee if average annual return on equity over the prior three years is 7% or more; otherwise 2.5x if terminated before the initial term ends and 1.5x at or after expiry. The average uses the two years before termination (annualised if shorter).
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Section 1 (Termination Fee)

facts.fact: The prospectus estimated the first-year management fee at about $77 million on $6.2 billion of assets ($5.2 billion land, $500 million Lennar cash, $500 million option-deposit cash).
facts.source_title: Millrose Properties prospectus (Form S-11, 424B1), filed 2025-01-17, Our Post-Spin-Off Relationship with KL

facts.fact: Millrose's own list of homebuilder M&A deals it has financed: Rausch Coleman / Lennar (2025-02-10; 25,000 homesites; $900M land assets), Landsea / New Home Co take-private (2025-05-12; 4,186 homesites; $700M land assets), Beazer / Dream Finders (2026-10-20; $580M land assets plus $488M preferred).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 Earnings Presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27), slide 13

facts.fact: Delivery against target: Q2 2026 exit AFFO run rate reported at $0.80 per share (top of the $0.78 to $0.80 range); year-end 2026 run-rate guidance then raised to $0.82 to $0.84 on 2026-10-27. Non-Lennar invested capital grew $1.0B in nine months (from $2,367.6M to $3,371.2M, calculated), and is about 42% of the asset base pro forma for the Dream Finders closing.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): the SFR pilot was underwritten at about a 5% going-in cap rate and 10 to 12% levered IRR, is about 1% of assets, and is described as a first step toward a possible rent-to-own product; Richman said Lennar did not push Millrose into it and the deal was arm's length. He said no Kennedy Lewis vehicle outside Millrose took part in the Dream Finders financing. Lennar's book was described as about $6B of assets with roughly $4B of build-out cost still to fund.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (Webull / Motley Fool)

facts.fact: Only five non-Lennar counterparties are publicly identifiable: New Home Co (now Risewell Homes), Taylor Morrison (for-sale program and Yardly build-to-rent), Dream Finders Homes, Beazer Homes (now part of Dream Finders) and JPI (multifamily). On the Q2 2025 call the CEO said he names only clients who have disclosed the relationship themselves. The other roughly 16 are undisclosed.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2025 earnings call transcript (Investing.com) (count of named builders compiled by this agent from the sources in builder_relationships)

facts.fact: Pipeline as of the Q3 2026 call: no numeric 2027 deployment target given. Nitkin said the pipeline remains active, land prices have been 'sticky', and builders including top-15 builders that are not yet clients are approaching Millrose for land positions. Takedown proceeds are to be used first to bring debt-to-capitalization back from about 36% to the 33% target, with room to lever up again for further M&A financing.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Product scope widened in 2026 beyond for-sale lot options: build-to-rent (Yardly), multifamily land (JPI, July 2026), preferred equity in a builder (Dream Finders, September-October 2026) and a single-family rental pilot (1,233 completed Lennar homes in 18 states for about $333M, $120M of equity plus $213M of limited-recourse debt at SOFR+120 bps; a further build-to-rent community contract of about $150M gross had not closed at 2026-10-27). Richman called multifamily opportunistic and said Millrose would be very selective there.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27); multifamily comment from HousingWire 2026-08-07

facts.fact: Dream Finders Homes' acquisition of Beazer Homes closed 2026-10-20 with about $1.1B of Millrose capital: about $580M (net of option deposits) of land-banking capital on about 7,000 homesites (over half finished, about 2.5-year weighted-average life) plus about $488M (net of original issue discount) of Dream Finders preferred equity paying a 12% dividend ($171M funded 2026-09-14, $317M at closing). Pro forma, about 42% of Millrose's asset base sits outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Dream Finders / Beazer economics (closed 2026-10-20, $1,068M total): land banking $580M net of Dream Finders deposits on about 7,000 lots (more than 50% finished, about 2.5-year weighted-average life) earning option fees plus an $8.0M commitment fee; preferred instrument $488M net of OID ($500M balance) earning 12% plus a $5.25M commitment fee, funded $171M on 2026-09-14 and $317M on 2026-10-20. Millrose describes the preferred as fixed-income in profile, like its development loans.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 Earnings Presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27), slide 12

facts.fact: Dream Finders preferred funding: agreement dated 2026-09-14; first closing $170.6M net of a $4.4M OID ($175.0M stated value); second closing 2026-10-20 of $316.9M net of OID, fulfilling a $350.0M remaining commitment. Deferred commitment fee of $1.7M at 2026-09-30.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 6 Preferred Instruments

facts.fact: Single-family rental pilot detail: 1,233 newly built homes bought from Lennar for about $333M gross (about $270K per home), mainly TX (386 homes, $82M), FL (142, $41M), SC (129, $35M), OK (115, $26M), NC (114, $39M); net exposure about $120M after $213M asset-level limited-recourse debt at SOFR+120bps (about 5.12%); property manager Evergreen Residential. A further roughly $150M of community build-to-rent purchase contracts is signed (about $100M expected asset financing, $50M net). SFR assets are excluded from the Kennedy Lewis management fee base. Management is evaluating 'path-to-homeownership' lease structures.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 Earnings Presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27), slides 15-17

facts.fact: At 2026-09-30 Millrose had agreements to buy a further 620 single-family rental homes from Lennar for about $150.3M (about $50.0M net after expected asset-level financing); if it does not close on some or all of them it may forfeit deposits. It carried $10.8M of SFR property deposits in other assets.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 12 Commitments and Contingencies

facts.fact: Counterparty count by quarter, as stated by management: 11 at 2025-06-30 (6 in the top 25 of the Zonda Builder 100), 12 at 2025-09-30, 15 at 2025-12-31 (9 of the top 25 US builders), 17 at 2026-03-31, 19 at 2026-06-30, 22 at 2026-09-30 (three added in Q3 2026). Counts include Lennar. Sources: Q2 2025, Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 call transcripts, Q1 2026 press release, Q2 and Q3 2026 decks; this row cites the latest.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: M&A financing is now a named product line. Millrose's 2026-08-07 release called Dream Finders/Beazer the third time it has provided land banking capital for a builder acquisition (the release does not list the earlier two; the Q3 2026 deck's transaction list points to Lennar/Rausch Coleman in February 2025 and New Home/Landsea in mid-2025). Richman said he sees significant opportunity as consolidation continues; on the Q1 2026 call he described M&A support as 'a tool in the tool belt'.
facts.source_title: Millrose press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-08-07

facts.fact: Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04): Richman said a new residential product suite was in development (commercial ruled out) and that the 33% leverage target, set before Millrose had operating history, was under review; the Taylor Morrison / Yardly arrangement included vertical construction financing, unlike JPI.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-08-04 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: 2026-07-30: Millrose closed the first acquisition under a new land-banking facility 'established by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management' to fund Class A multifamily land acquisition and development in JPI's target markets. Millrose acquires and funds development of the sites; JPI pays option fees and takes sites down as its pipeline matures. JPI (Sumitomo Forestry subsidiary) reports 54 active communities, 18,785 homes, $6.9B value. Facility size not disclosed.
facts.source_title: Millrose / JPI press release, 2026-07-30 (company IR PDF)

facts.fact: On 2026-05-11 Millrose announced its intent to provide land-banking capital for Dream Finders Homes' proposed acquisition of Beazer Homes, buying Beazer-owned homesites at closing; it held a Goldman Sachs 'highly confident' letter for up to $500M of financing for the deal. It said the deal would temporarily take debt-to-capitalization above its policy target, to be restored through equity issued above book value or organic deleveraging from takedown proceeds, and repeated that it will not issue equity below book value.
facts.source_title: Millrose press release: land banking capital support for Dream Finders / Beazer (2026-05-11)

facts.fact: Q1 2026: Millrose reached 17 homebuilders (16 outside Lennar) and said one of the two added in the quarter is a top-10 national homebuilder (the call specified publicly traded). It has never named that builder. Management said new relationships start small and grow, and that this one did not cause the quarter's yield dip.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-05-06)

facts.fact: Underwriting as described by management: (1) cross-termination pooling covered about 97% of the portfolio at mid-2025, 96% at year-end 2025 and about 95% at Q1 2026; (2) no MSA above 6% of the portfolio (Q2 2025); (3) builders' price, pace and margin assumptions are tested against Millrose's own lot-pricing dataset across 30 states, then legal and development diligence; (4) an internal monthly MSA risk-rating model; (5) deposit percentages are not disclosed and the CEO declines to give contract-level terms.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool, 2026-05-06); pooling percentages also from the Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 transcripts

facts.fact: Who Millrose says it will and will not finance: management repeatedly separates builders using land banking for capital efficiency (wanted) from those using it for risk mitigation (declined). On the Q3 2025 call it said it passed on a 'substantial amount' of deals that quarter because its data did not support the builders' underwriting, and would rather pass than take more risk for a little more spread. On the Q1 2026 call it said it gives declined builders anonymized feedback comparing their lot pricing with its comps.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2025 earnings call transcript (Investing.com); feedback practice from the Q1 2026 transcript

facts.fact: View of rivals: management never names a competitor. On the Q3 2025 call Richman called Millrose the 'only national public platform' dedicated to homesite capital and said builders value certainty of capital over cost. On the Q1 2026 call management said newer land-banking entrants are finding a tougher market harder, that private land-banking alternatives cannot match Millrose's capital certainty and transparency, and that scale, data and track record widen its moat.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool, 2026-05-06)

facts.fact: The only non-Lennar builders named in Millrose's calendar-2025 periodic filings and decks are The New Home Company (Landsea acquisition financing) and Taylor Morrison (Yardly build-to-rent, through Kennedy Lewis). The Q3 and Q4 releases and decks and the Feb 2026 investor deck name no counterparty other than Lennar; the FY2025 10-K names New Home only. This is a reading across the documents listed in sources_consulted, not a statement by Millrose.
facts.source_title: Millrose FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-03-02), Item 1 Business

facts.fact: Full-year 2025 target for funding outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement was set at at least $1.0B (2025-03-17), raised to $1.5B (2025-05-14) and to $2.2B (2025-10-23); actual 2025 funding under Other Agreements was $2,622.5M. Year-end quarterly run-rate guidance moved from $0.67-$0.69 EPS (March) to $0.69-$0.71 (May), $0.70-$0.73 AFFO (July) and $0.74-$0.76 AFFO (October); the actual year-end run rate was about $0.77. Compiled from the March 17, Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4 releases, each cited separately in this file.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 / FY2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Feb 2026 decks frame 2026 growth as similar in volume to 2025's roughly $2.4B of net new deployment outside Lennar: an illustrative $2B of net new capital at 11% yields would lift annualized AFFO from $3.00 to about $3.30 per share (about +10%), assuming 5.7% interest on $1.3B of new debt and new equity issued at book value. Millrose labels this illustrative, not guidance.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: 2026 targets set on 2026-02-26: up to $2B of net new capital deployment in 2026 (about $1B by mid-year from existing debt capacity), a further $2B of invested capital outside the Lennar agreement, Q2 2026 exit AFFO run rate of $0.78 to $0.80 per share (about 10% year-on-year AFFO per share growth), maximum debt-to-capitalization of 33%, and no equity issuance below book value. The 2025 stretch target of $2.2B non-Lennar invested capital was beaten at about $2.4B.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4/FY2025 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: 2026 guidance given on the Q4 2025 call (2026-02-26): base case of about $2.0B of invested-capital growth outside Lennar, taking total invested capital to about $10.5B with more than 40% from non-Lennar partners; about $1.0B by mid-year funded from existing debt capacity; guidance excludes M&A. Reaffirmed in the Q1 2026 release. By Q3 2026 the non-Lennar share was 36% and 42% pro forma for Dream Finders/Beazer. No explicit long-run target mix has been stated.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Forward-flow backlog (Q4 2025 call, 2026-02-26): management said forward-flow agreements total about $9.0B across roughly 10 counterparties and that about $3.0B of the land portfolio will cycle off in the next year and must be replaced; COO Robert Nitkin said that even with no new counterparties they were confident of deploying about $1.0B by mid-year.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: In the Q1 2025 release (2025-05-14) Millrose raised its full-year 2025 target for new transaction funding outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement to $1.5B from $1.0B, and raised its year-end quarterly earnings run-rate guidance to $0.69-$0.71 per share. It said it had executed programmatic (forward-flow) commitments with five other homebuilders, none named.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2025-05-14)

facts.fact: On 2025-05-12 Millrose announced a $700M commitment to New Home Company (owned by Apollo-affiliated funds) to support its acquisition of Landsea Homes, expected to close in Q3 2025 alongside the acquisition.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2025-05-14)

facts.fact: Between 2025-04-01 and 2025-05-09 Millrose deployed about $130M outside the Lennar Master Program at yields above 11%, bringing the total since the spin to about $480M.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2025 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2025-05-14)

facts.fact: Non-Lennar business must be ring-fenced: other customers are served through separate 'Other Subsidiaries', not Millrose Holdings or the entities serving Lennar; their deals are individually negotiated by the manager, may not carry the Lennar operating principles and may resemble traditional land banking. Deals with Lennar-related ventures mirror the Lennar agreements but carry no Lennar parent guaranty.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1

facts.fact: Millrose's own investment guidelines: no more than 40% of portfolio value in one state; every deal needs an option agreement with a defined takedown schedule and a construction agreement; no liens or moratoriums; environmental report within 180 days. HOPP'R phase lengths are given as 6-60 months for land acquisition and development and 4-14 months to first home.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1

facts.fact: Competitors Millrose names in its 10-K: Kennedy Lewis itself, Angelo, Gordon & Co. (now part of TPG), DW Partners, LP and Brookfield Properties.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-K for FY2024, filed 2025-03-31, Item 1 (Competition)

facts.fact: REIT and distribution policy: Millrose elects REIT status from the taxable year ending 2025-12-31 and must distribute at least 90% of REIT taxable income; management said it is committed to paying out 100% of earnings. First dividend $0.38 a share ($65 million) declared 2025-03-17 for the stub period from the spin to 2025-03-31, pro-rated from a normalised $0.65 a quarter. Millrose Holdings is a taxable REIT subsidiary.
facts.source_title: Millrose press release 2025-03-17 (8-K Exhibit 99.1)

facts.fact: Early non-Lennar pace: about $250M closed outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement between the Feb 7 spin and 2025-03-17 at yields above 11%, with at least $100M more expected within 30 days and a first full-year target of at least $1B. Initial guidance was Q2 2025 EPS of $0.65-$0.68 and a year-end quarterly run rate of $0.67-$0.69.
facts.source_title: Millrose press release on inaugural dividend and outlook (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2025-03-17)

facts.fact: Stated model is 'recycled capital': deposits and takedown proceeds are redeployed into new land and development. Three growth lanes in the February 2025 deck: Lennar forward flow, 'strategic homebuilders' and third-party builders, aimed at the top 10 builders and the remaining public and private builders, with non-Lennar deals focused on high-migration, low-tax 'Smile States'. Millrose sized the market at over $170 billion a year (1.22 million starts x $140,000 land and development cost per homesite).
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, February 2025 (8-K 2025-02-24, Exhibit 99.1), slides 20-22

facts.fact: Margin-of-safety pitch in the February 2025 deck: with an illustrative 20% builder margin plus deposits and cost levers, home prices would have to fall about 30% before a builder is better off walking; 39% of the seed book turns in under a year.
facts.source_title: Millrose investor presentation, February 2025 (8-K 2025-02-24, Exhibit 99.1), slides 16 and 24

facts.fact: Deal allocation between Millrose and Kennedy Lewis's own funds: customers Millrose directs go 100% to Millrose; follow-ons to existing Kennedy Lewis investments can go 100% to Kennedy Lewis 'Priority Accounts' (Capital Partners Master Fund III and Kennedy Lewis Residential Property Income Company, 'KLRES'); other deals suitable for both alternate, starting with Millrose, until those funds' investment periods end, after which they go to Millrose first.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Exhibit C (Allocation Policy), Sections 2-4

facts.fact: Limits on Kennedy Lewis competing with Millrose: without Millrose board approval Kennedy Lewis may not raise other capital to provide land banking, except 'Overflow Funds' (used only when neither Millrose nor a Priority Account has capital) and up to $1 billion of land banking from its Fund IV.
facts.source_title: Management Agreement, Millrose / Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, 2025-02-07 (8-K Exhibit 10.1), Exhibit C, Section 5

facts.fact: Concentration admitted in the risk factors: Lennar is the largest counterparty, may let options lapse, has no duty to bring new business, can use rival land banks, can pull its rate down to whatever a non-Lennar builder gets, can halve its fee during pauses for up to two years with Millrose's agreement, and its Capital Priority Right limits capital left for others. Pooling protection is not guaranteed for other customers.
facts.source_title: Millrose Properties prospectus (Form S-11, 424B1), filed 2025-01-17, Risk Factors

facts.fact: Millrose has raised no primary equity since the spin: shares outstanding were 166,003,497 at every quarter end from 2025-03-31 to 2026-03-31 (so the Lennar exchange offer was purely secondary) and 166,047,927 at 2026-11-03 (154,228,116 Class A + 11,819,811 Class B) after 44,430 director RSU shares vested on 2026-04-03. No preferred stock is outstanding (50M authorized). Authorized common: 275M Class A, 175M Class B.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Stockholders' Equity note and 10-Q cover page

facts.fact: Q3 2026 call (2026-10-27): an analyst (Goldman Sachs) estimated about 40% debt-to-capitalization pro forma for Dream Finders, which management did not dispute; Richman said takedown proceeds will repay debt back toward the unchanged 33% target (no timeline) and that M&A portfolios turn faster (about 2 years versus 3). Buybacks will not be debt-funded: while the stock trades below book, about 90% of earnings is distributed and about 10% goes to repurchases, with the dividend not reduced, plus unused Lennar 'priority capital'.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript, 2026-10-27 (stockanalysis.com)

facts.fact: The 33% maximum has not been restated since the Q1 2026 release (my reading of four documents, so tagged Inferred): the Q2 2026 release and presentation (30% actual) and the Q3 2026 release and presentation (36% actual) give no leverage target, maximum or range. Reported debt-to-capitalization crossed the former 33% ceiling in Q3 2026. Absence checked in the two releases and two presentations only; call transcripts were not read.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Management's stated funding logic for bank debt (CEO, 2026-03-27 release): floating-rate borrowings are matched against floating-rate homesite option contracts; the facility was moved from secured to fully unsecured. The Q3 2026 presentation shows 'newly issued bonds' at 6.50% to 6.75% as the debt cost for the core land-banking business and about 5.12% for asset-level rental-home debt.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Capital posture after Dream Finders (Q3 2026 call): debt-to-capitalization about 36% against a 33% target; a $250M buyback authorized in October 2026, to be funded from retained earnings (about 90% of earnings paid out, about 10% to buybacks while the stock is below the $35.24 book value) and not from borrowing; no equity issuance below book. The management fee was $30.3M for Q3 2026, at 1.25% of gross tangible assets; Kennedy Lewis proposed excluding the rental homes from the fee base.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Buyback: on 2026-10-26 the board authorized a share repurchase program (no earlier authorization appears in the filings read) of up to $250M of Class A stock (about 4% of book equity), open-market or negotiated, no obligation. It was authorized in the same month leverage was pushed above the former 33% ceiling. No repurchases had occurred through 2026-09-30.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2026-10-27, Item 8.01

facts.fact: Pro forma debt after the 2026-10-06 notes (my calculation, not a company figure): senior notes outstanding rise to $3.0B across four series (2029, 2030, 2031, 2032). If the roughly $897M funded to Dream Finders on 2026-10-20 ($580M homesites + $316.9M preferred) was entirely debt-funded, corporate debt would be about $4.0B and debt-to-capitalization about 41% ((3,127.5 + 897) / (3,127.5 + 897 + 5,850.9)). The company has not published a post-closing leverage figure; the revolver balance after the offering is not disclosed.
facts.source_title: Calculated from Millrose Q3 2026 10-Q Subsequent Events and balance sheet

facts.fact: Distance to Fitch's downgrade trigger (my calculation; Fitch's own adjustments may differ): gross debt / equity was about 0.54x at 2026-09-30 on corporate debt (3,164.9 / 5,850.9), or 0.58x including the SFR facility, already above the 0.5x management target Fitch cited in 2025. Adding the full $1.0B of Oct 2026 notes with none of it used to repay debt would give about 0.71x; assuming only the roughly $897M Dream Finders funding was net new debt gives about 0.69x (0.73x with SFR), close to the 0.75x 'sustained' downgrade trigger. No 2026 Fitch, Moody's or S&P action was located (search budget ran out).
facts.source_title: Calculated from Fitch 2025-08-12 sensitivities and Millrose Q3 2026 10-Q

facts.fact: 2026-10-06: closed $1.0B senior unsecured notes at par, $500M 6.500% due 2029-10-15 and $500M 6.750% due 2031-10-15 (Citibank trustee). The 2031 notes carried a special mandatory redemption if the Dream Finders / Beazer merger did not close by 2027-05-13 (it closed 2026-10-20). Proceeds, with the $500M term loan, were for general corporate purposes including buying homesites from the combined Dream Finders / Beazer and repaying the revolver ($850M drawn at 2026-09-21).
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2026-10-06 (senior notes closing, Items 1.01/2.03)

facts.fact: Bond covenants are light: all four note indentures restrict only liens, sale-leasebacks and mergers / sales of substantially all assets, with a 101% change-of-control put; no debt-incurrence, leverage or builder-concentration covenant is described.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2026-10-06; 8-Ks filed 2025-08-08 and 2025-09-12

facts.fact: After the Oct 2026 notes the fixed-rate bond book is $3.0B at a weighted coupon of about 6.43% ((1,250 x 6.375% + 750 x 6.250% + 500 x 6.500% + 500 x 6.750%) / 3,000), up from 6.33% on the first $2.0B; the two new tranches alone add about $66M of annual interest. My calculation from the coupons in the indenture 8-Ks.
facts.source_title: Calculated from Millrose 8-Ks filed 2025-08-08, 2025-09-12 and 2026-10-06

facts.fact: Debt at 2026-09-30 (principal): revolver $635.0M, delayed-draw term loan $496.9M, 6.375% notes due 2030 $1,250M, 6.250% notes due 2032 $750M, purchase-money mortgages $33M (total $3,164.9M), plus the separate SFR secured facility $213.1M. Credit facility margins after the 2026-08-05 amendment are SOFR + 1.75% / 2.00% / 2.25% by leverage. In compliance with all covenants.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 11 Debt

facts.fact: 2026-09-30: subsidiaries entered a limited-recourse secured revolver with Goldman Sachs Bank USA to finance single-family rental homes: up to $235M committed (expandable to $1.0B at lenders' option), one-month Term SOFR + 1.20% with a 0.50% floor, maturing 2028-09-29 plus a one-year extension; $213.1M drawn against a 1,233-home pilot costing about $333M (about 64% loan-to-cost, my calculation). By margin this is the cheapest debt in the stack (my observation) and it sits outside the 'corporate debt' leverage figure.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Debt note

facts.fact: Debt at 2026-09-30 (principal): revolver $635.0M, delayed-draw term loan $496.9M, 6.375% notes due 2030 $1,250.0M, 6.250% notes due 2032 $750.0M, purchase money mortgages $33.0M; total $3,164.9M, or $3,127.5M net of $37.4M issuance costs, up from $2,143.0M gross at 2025-12-31. Separately, SFR secured facility $213.1M. Fixed-rate notes were 63% of the $3,164.9M and floating bank debt 36% (my calculation), versus 95% fixed at 2025-12-31.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Debt note

facts.fact: Reported debt-to-capitalization (total debt / (total debt + equity)) and debt by quarter end: 2025-03-31 about 5% ($350M); 2025-06-30 about 15% ($1.0B); 2025-09-30 about 25% ($2.0B); 2025-12-31 26% ($2.1B); 2026-03-31 about 29% ($2.4B); 2026-06-30 about 30% ($2.5B); 2026-09-30 36% ($3.1B corporate debt, excluding the $213M SFR facility). Each figure is from that quarter's earnings release; all seven were opened.
facts.source_title: Millrose quarterly earnings press releases Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 (latest cited)

facts.fact: Liquidity (cash plus undrawn bank capacity) by quarter end: $1.1B (2025-03-31), $1.4B (2025-06-30), $1.6B (2025-09-30), $1.3B (2025-12-31), $1.5B (2026-03-31), $1.4B (2026-06-30), $0.8B (2026-09-30: $65M cash plus about $0.8B remaining revolver/term-loan capacity). Cash itself is kept thin: $64.5M at 2026-09-30 against $10.6B of assets.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Covenant headroom at 2026-09-30 (my calculation): bank Leverage Ratio about 0.35x on corporate debt alone ((3,164.9 - 39.5 cash above $25M) / (3,125.4 + 5,850.9)) or about 0.36x including the $213M SFR facility, against a 0.45x cap; tangible net worth $5.85B against a $4.39B floor (about $1.46B of cushion). That places the bank debt in the middle pricing tier (SOFR + 2.00%). If the Dream Finders funding was all debt-financed the ratio would be about 0.41x, i.e. the top pricing tier (SOFR + 2.25%) and within 4 points of the cap.
facts.source_title: Calculated from A&R Credit Agreement definitions and Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet

facts.fact: Weighted average cost of debt is not stated in any release, presentation or debt note read. My estimate at 2026-09-30: about 6.2% on $3,131.9M of interest-bearing corporate debt = (1,250.0 x 6.375% + 750.0 x 6.250% + 1,131.9 of revolver and term loan x 5.92%) / 3,131.9, where 5.92% = 3.92% term SOFR (the 9/30/2026 rate the company's own presentation uses) + 2.00% middle-tier margin (leverage ratio about 0.35x), ignoring any SOFR credit adjustment, undrawn fees and fee amortization; the $33M purchase money mortgages are excluded because the counterparty pays their interest. Including the $213.1M SFR facility at 5.12% the blend is about 6.1%. Cross-check: Q3 2026 interest expense of $47.1M annualized over average net debt of about $2.8B is about 6.7% all-in including fee amortization.
facts.source_title: Calculated from Millrose Q3 2026 10-Q Debt note, Amendment No. 1 pricing grid and Q3 2026 presentation SOFR assumption

facts.fact: Interest cost run-rate: interest expense was $2.5M (Q1 2025), $10.3M (Q2 2025), $43.7M (Q3 2025, including the $11.9M write-off), $35.2M (Q4 2025), $39.2M (Q1 2026), $40.0M (Q2 2026) and $47.1M (Q3 2026); FY2025 $91.8M; nine months 2026 $126.3M. Q3 2026 split: senior notes $33.2M, revolver $10.7M, term loan $3.2M.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Debt note; quarterly earnings releases

facts.fact: Book value per share: $35.40 at 2025-03-31 (stated) and $35.24 at 2026-09-30 (stated in the Q3 2026 presentation; equity $5,850.9M / 166,047,927 shares). In between, by my division of reported equity by shares: $35.39 (2025-06-30), $35.29 (2025-09-30), $35.28 (2025-12-31), $35.26 (2026-03-31), $35.24 (2026-06-30). Book value is flat to slightly down because all AFFO is paid out; total equity has stayed at about $5.85B to $5.88B since the spin while debt went from zero to $3.1B.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27); quarterly releases for intermediate equity figures

facts.fact: Dividend policy and record: Millrose targets paying out 100% of AFFO. Declared per share: $0.38 (2025-03-17, stub from Feb 7; equal to $0.65 for a full quarter), $0.69 (2025-06-16), $0.73 (2025-09-22), $0.75 (2025-12-22), $0.76 (2026-03-23), $0.77 (2026-06-23), $0.79 (2026-09-23, $131.2M, paid 2026-10-15). Q3 2026 AFFO was $0.80 per share, so the dividend consumed essentially all of it; the company shows an 8.9% annualized dividend yield on book equity.
facts.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Stockholders' Equity note; dividend 8-Ks and earnings releases

facts.fact: New-issue pricing trend: Millrose paid 6.375% for 5-year money in Aug 2025 and 6.250% for 7-year money in Sep 2025, but 6.500% for 3-year and 6.750% for 5-year money in Sep 2026. On like-for-like 5-year tenor the coupon rose 37.5 bps in 13 months (6.375% to 6.750%) while leverage went from about 15% to 36% debt-to-capitalization. Coupon comparison is my calculation from the four pricing 8-Ks; no benchmark-spread data was read.
facts.source_title: Millrose 8-K filed 2026-09-23 (pricing of 2029 and 2031 notes), compared with 2025 pricing 8-Ks

facts.fact: 2026-08-05: Amendment No. 1 cut the credit facility loan margin by 0.25% per annum. 2026-09-21: accordion exercised, adding Flagstar Bank and $50M to take revolver commitments to $1.385B.

facts.fact: Financial covenants in the 2026 unsecured credit agreement (Section 7.27), tested quarterly: (a) maximum Leverage Ratio 0.45x, defined as net debt / (net debt + tangible net worth), with an election to run up to 0.50x for the quarter of a 'Material Acquisition' and the four following quarters (two elections maximum, not consecutive); (b) minimum interest coverage 1.50x (EBITDA / interest incurred, trailing four quarters); (c) minimum tangible net worth of $4,392.2M plus 50% of net equity issuance proceeds after 2025-12-31 (plus 50% of net income only if Millrose ceases to be a REIT). Millrose must also keep REIT status. Amendment No. 1 did not change these.
facts.source_title: Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated 2026-03-25 (8-K Ex. 10.1)

facts.fact: Borrowing base under the unsecured facility: advance rates of 75% on single-family lots under contract, 70% on lots not under contract (65% after 18 months), 65% on land under development, 50% on land held for future development, 60% / 40% on commercial or clubhouse lots under / not under contract, 50% on mortgage loans made, 100% of unrestricted cash above $25M. Sub-limits: land held for future development (and loans on it) capped at 40% of the base; mortgage loans 5%; commercial/clubhouse lots 5%.

facts.fact: Builder concentration in the credit agreement: no cap on exposure to a single builder or customer was found in the covenant or borrowing-base sections read. The only counterparty-specific terms seen are a 'Material Counterparty' definition (a counterparty whose properties exceeded 40% of consolidated assets at closing, in practice Lennar) with a covenant (Section 7.23) barring amendments to that counterparty's program agreements that are materially adverse to lenders. Other baskets: investments in 'Permitted Business' investees limited to the greater of $600M and 10% of tangible net worth; secured/non-recourse debt liens limited to the greater of $200M and 3% of tangible net worth; cross-default threshold $90M; change of manager from Kennedy Lewis without an acceptable replacement in 90 days is an event of default.
facts.source_title: Amended and Restated Credit Agreement dated 2026-03-25 (8-K Ex. 10.1)

builder_relationships.builder_name: Rausch Coleman Companies, LLC (seller; lots optioned to Lennar)
builder_relationships.description: Land seller in the 2025-02-10 Rausch Coleman / Lennar deal (25,000 homesites, $900M land assets per Millrose's Q3 2026 deck). Millrose still holds a $100M development guarantee holdback payable to Rausch no earlier than 2027-02-10, reduced by any development cost overruns.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose 10-Q for Q3 2026 (filed 2026-11-04), Note 2 (Development guarantee holdback)

builder_relationships.description: On 2025-02-10 Millrose bought RCH Holdings (parent of Rausch Coleman Companies), about 25,000 homesites, for about $859M cash net of $90.3M of Lennar-funded option deposits and a $100M development holdback, and optioned the homesites back to Lennar, enabling Lennar's acquisition of the builder.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 3 Spin-Off and Other Significant Business Transactions

builder_relationships.description: Not a direct option counterparty: Millrose bought about 7,000 Beazer-owned homesites ($580M net of deposits) when Dream Finders Homes acquired Beazer on 2026-10-20 and optioned them to Dream Finders.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 Earnings Presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27), slide 12

builder_relationships.description: Builder-side view of the Beazer financing. Commitment letters dated 2026-08-06 were with Kennedy Lewis Investment Management (not Millrose): an $800M land bank facility and a $450M convertible preferred investment, alongside a $900M bank bridge (BofA / Goldman). At closing on 2026-10-20 Dream Finders received $572.1M of land-bank proceeds from Millrose and/or affiliates, used to redeem Beazer's $350M 7.25% notes due 2029 and repay Beazer's credit facility. Beazer was bought for $33.50 per share, about $878.4M.
builder_relationships.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 8-K (Beazer closing), filed 2026-10-20

builder_relationships.builder_name: Dream Finders Homes (Series B Convertible Preferred)
builder_relationships.description: Terms of the preferred Millrose bought: 12.00% cumulative dividend, deferrable, stepping up 0.50% after year 6 and every six months after to a 15% cap; perpetual; callable by the company after year 3 at 102%, year 4 at 101%, then par; holder conversion only after year 6 at a 20% discount to the 90-day average price (25% discount on covenant breach); 2.5% original issue discount; board observer right and a right of first refusal on new preferred. Dream Finders sold $675M in total ($225M on 2026-09-14, $450M on 2026-10-20) to unnamed institutional purchasers. Millrose says it holds a $500M balance ($171M and $317M funded net of discount), so about $175M went to other purchasers (calculated: 675 minus 500; not identified).
builder_relationships.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 8-K (Series B preferred first closing), filed 2026-09-15

builder_relationships.builder_name: New Home Co (now Risewell Homes) / Landsea Homes
builder_relationships.description: New Home's 2025-05-12 announcement of its $11.30-per-share, roughly $1.2B enterprise value take-private of Landsea said Millrose was providing committed land banking capital alongside $650M of new Apollo equity; no Millrose dollar figure was given there. On Millrose's Q2 2025 call management said it closed an approximately $500M homesite portfolio (net cash funding) with cross-termination provisions like its other contracts. Millrose's own deck states 4,186 homesites and $700M of land assets; the gap between about $500M net funding and $700M is not explained publicly (likely deposits and future development funding; inferred). The deal closed 2025-06-25 per HousingWire.
builder_relationships.source_title: New Home Co / Landsea Homes joint press release (Landsea 8-K Ex. 99.1), 2025-05-12; funding figure from the Q2 2025 call transcript (Reported)

builder_relationships.builder_name: The New Home Company (listed as Risewell Homes in the builder spine)
builder_relationships.description: Up to $700M land-banking commitment announced 2025-05-12 to back New Home's acquisition of Landsea Homes. Closed 2025-06-25: Millrose paid $494.5M cash for $522.8M of land (4,186 homesites), net of $28.3M of option deposits, and optioned the homesites to New Home.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, Note 3 Spin-Off and Other Significant Business Transactions

builder_relationships.description: Millrose bought 1,233 completed homes from Lennar across 18 states for an aggregate cost of about $333M (about $270K to $280K per home), financed with $213M of limited-recourse secured debt at SOFR+120 bps and about $120M of equity. Underwritten at roughly a 5% going-in cap rate, about 8% unlevered and 10-12% levered IRR; about 10% of homes rented as of 2026-10-26; leasing managed by Evergreen Residential. Management says no further purchases since quarter-end and that rent-to-own is still being designed.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27); underwriting detail from the Q3 2026 call transcript (Reported)

builder_relationships.builder_name: Unnamed 'Borrower A' (development loan; listed among Lennar related-party balances)
builder_relationships.description: Secured residential development loan across multiple US markets at 12% paid-in-kind interest; carrying amount $287.7M at 2025-12-31, maturity 2026-01-31 extended on 2026-01-29 to 2026-07-31. The Q3 2025 10-Q lists $302.7M of development loan receivables among balances with Lennar, so this borrower appears to be Lennar-related (identity not disclosed).
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, schedule of development loans secured by residential properties

builder_relationships.description: Secured residential development loan across multiple US markets at 12% paid-in-kind interest; carrying amount $35.6M at 2025-12-31, maturity 2029-09-30. Borrower not named.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose FY2025 10-K, schedule of development loans secured by residential properties

builder_relationships.description: $3B land and construction financing facility for Taylor Morrison's Yardly build-to-rent platform announced 2025-07-23 by Taylor Morrison and Kennedy Lewis (Millrose's manager), with a right of first refusal on Yardly funding over a 2.5-year exclusivity term; The Q2 deck says initial Millrose closings were scheduled through Q3 2025 and that about $200M had been deployed outside the Lennar agreement as of Jul 31, 2025; the Q2 earnings release adds that the majority of the facility is expected to be allocated to Millrose. Amount funded by Millrose on Yardly alone is not disclosed.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q2 2025 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2025-07-31)

builder_relationships.description: Added as a new counterparty in Q1 2026 (taking the count to 17); Millrose did not name it or size the relationship.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-05-06)

builder_relationships.builder_name: JPI (subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry Co., Ltd.)
builder_relationships.description: Multifamily land-banking facility established by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management; Millrose closed the inaugural acquisition on 2026-07-30 (its first multifamily counterparty). Horizontal-only (land and site development), rental product, deposit plus option fee on the investment balance; yields described on the Q2 call as consistent with other agreements. Size and site count not disclosed.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose / JPI press release, 2026-07-30 (company IR PDF)

builder_relationships.builder_name: Beazer Homes USA (acquired by Dream Finders Homes 2026-10-20)
builder_relationships.description: Beazer was already a land-banking client before the merger: in Millrose's 2026-08-07 release CEO Richman called both Dream Finders and Beazer valued clients and said his team had partnered with Beazer across multiple market cycles. Size of the pre-merger Beazer and Dream Finders positions is not disclosed. Post-merger, Millrose land-banks about 7,000 former Beazer/Dream Finders homesites for about $580M.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-08-07

builder_relationships.description: Taylor Morrison's 2025-07-23 release says it already had a land banking agreement with Kennedy Lewis supporting its for-sale operations, making Yardly the second financing vehicle between them. Whether those for-sale lots sit in Millrose or in Kennedy Lewis funds is not stated; Millrose's CEO named Taylor Morrison as a Millrose client on the Q2 2025 call. Taylor Morrison was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on 2026-07-24.
builder_relationships.source_title: Taylor Morrison press release, 2025-07-23

builder_relationships.builder_name: JPI (multifamily developer; subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry)
builder_relationships.description: Announced 2026-07-30: Millrose closed the first acquisition under a new land banking facility set up by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management for Class A multifamily sites in JPI's target markets. Millrose buys the sites and funds development; JPI pays option fees and takes sites down as projects mature. Millrose's first multifamily counterparty. Facility size, first-site location and dollars are not disclosed. JPI's CFO/CIO Mollie Fadule called it an off-balance-sheet capital solution. Per HousingWire, management said it mirrors the Yardly structure.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose / JPI press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-07-30

Builder-by-builder searches for other public builders' filings mentioning Millrose could not be completed: the shared web-search budget for this session ran out after about a dozen searches, and SEC full-text search is blocked from this machine. Who bought the other roughly $175M of Dream Finders Series B preferred (possibly Kennedy Lewis funds): purchasers are unnamed in Dream Finders' 8-Ks. The Dream Finders 10-Q for Q3 2026 was only partly readable (tool truncation) so its subsequent-events note was not checked.

Full Q2 2026 call transcript was not opened (only the Q2 deck, a HousingWire article and a third-party summary). Benzinga's Q3 2026 transcript, BusinessWire originals, Akin Gump's deal release, risewellhomes.com and Millrose's q4cdn-hosted PDFs were blocked or rate-limited; wire copies and SEC exhibits were used instead.

No Chief Investment Officer, head of capital markets or named investor-relations officer is published for Millrose; no phone numbers or personal emails are published. Kennedy Lewis's wider residential/land-banking deal team (below Richman and Nitkin) was not found in the sources opened.
Stephen/Steven Hensley's exact title is inconsistent across transcript vendors and is not confirmed on the company site.
5% holders and insider share counts: the proxy's ownership tables are images and could not be read; Stuart Miller's roughly 43% voting power is from Hunterbrook only.
