deals.description: Dream Finders completed its all-cash purchase of Beazer on 2026-10-20 at $33.50 per share, about $2.2B enterprise value; Beazer was delisted from the NYSE. Dream Finders expects $100M+ of annual run-rate cost synergies, will move Beazer communities onto Dream Finders floor plans and aims to bring leverage back to current levels within 18-24 months. The combined company builds in 26 of the top 50 MSAs. Millrose provided about $1.07B of land-bank and preferred-equity financing (see the Millrose profile).
deals.map_impact: Rank 21 Beazer Homes merges into rank 14 Dream Finders Homes; the Beazer row disappears and the combined company calls itself the 6th largest US builder (by 2025 revenue; HousingWire counts 13,035 combined 2025 closings). Adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware and more Maryland/DC to Dream Finders. Patrick Zalupski stays CEO and co-chairman; Rick Beckwitt (ex-Lennar and D.R. Horton) joined the Dream Finders board as co-chairman in July 2026 during the bid. The closing release names no continuing role for Beazer CEO Allan Merrill or other Beazer executives.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes Completes Acquisition of Beazer Homes (Business Wire release, 2026-10-20, as carried by Finviz)

deals.description: Century acquired substantially all the assets of HistoryMaker; the 2026-10-08 release says it 'has acquired' them, so the deal was announced and closed together. Price, lots and community counts not disclosed. HistoryMaker (founded 1949, Grapevine TX) builds only in Dallas-Fort Worth; the deal triples Century's DFW community count. Century's DFW operations and HistoryMaker combine into one division based in Grapevine with HistoryMaker division leadership joining; Century keeps a land development relationship with HistoryMaker's sister company Jabez Development. Vestra Advisors advised HistoryMaker.
deals.map_impact: Rank 77 HistoryMaker Homes is absorbed into rank 10 Century Communities; the HistoryMaker row disappears. HistoryMaker's division leaders run Century's combined DFW division; owner and CEO Nelson Mitchell sold, and Jabez Development continues as a land developer for Century.
deals.source_title: Century Communities Triples Dallas-Fort Worth Footprint with Acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes (PR Newswire release, 2026-10-08, as carried by Finviz)

deals.description: Berkshire Hathaway has been buying Lennar shares on the open market; this is not an acquisition, and the date shown is the date of the report. ResiClub reports from Berkshire's SEC filings that Berkshire raised its Lennar holding by 94% in Q3 2026 and by about 260% since the start of 2026, to around 11% of Lennar; an earlier ResiClub piece (2026-08-20) put the holding at 13.1M Class A shares plus Class B, worth just over $1.2B, with a small new D.R. Horton position of 3,600 shares. No bid for Lennar has been reported.
deals.map_impact: No row merges. The owner of the new Taylor Morrison / Clayton platform (ranks 6 and 12) is now also a roughly 11% shareholder of rank 2 Lennar, which matters for anyone reading Lennar's and Millrose's ownership and for speculation about further Berkshire housing moves.
deals.source_title: ResiClub: Warren Buffett's successor makes third big housing market bet this year, now owning around 11% of Lennar (2026-10-05)

deals.target: Innovative Construction Group (ICG), a PulteGroup subsidiary
deals.description: Builders FirstSource agreed to buy ICG, PulteGroup's off-site framing business (wall panels, roof and floor trusses, installation; plants of about 400,000 sq ft in Florida and about 200,000 sq ft in South Carolina), for an undisclosed price, announced 2026-08-03. This is a division sale by a top-3 builder, not a homebuilder purchase. Pulte bought ICG in 2020 for about $104M and said in January 2026 it would divest it; Pulte expects to keep buying off-site components without owning the factories. Closing date not confirmed in the sources opened (Vestra Advisors, Pulte's adviser, lists the deal under August 2026).
deals.map_impact: No ranking change. Rank 3 PulteGroup (seller, builder_id pultegroup) exits factory ownership and frees capital for homebuilding; relevant as a sign of a large builder going more asset-light.
deals.source_title: HousingWire: Why Builders FirstSource bought ICG; and why Pulte sold it (2026-08-03)

deals.description: Stanley Martin bought employee-owned Florida builder Holiday Builders (Melbourne FL): it agreed the deal on 2026-07-16 and the seller's adviser says it closed 2026-07-29 (other reports say it became official 2026-07-30). Price not disclosed. Holiday closed about 1,050 homes in 2025 and brings 40+ communities and about 10,600 controlled Florida lots (Palm Coast, Palm Bay, Panama City, Orlando area, North Port, Cape Coral). Holiday becomes a wholly owned subsidiary. Zelman Partners advised Holiday.
deals.map_impact: Rank 62 Holiday Builders is now owned by rank 18 Stanley Martin (Daiwa House); the Holiday row merges into Stanley Martin. With UHG, Stanley Martin's 2025 pro-forma closings are about 7,560 (5,320 + 1,192 + 1,050, a sum of the figures in the cited articles), and Daiwa House's US builders total about 10,000.
deals.source_title: HousingWire (sponsored, Zelman): Holiday Builders Sale Shows What Buyers Want in Homebuilder M&A (2026-07-29)

deals.description: Berkshire Hathaway completed its purchase of Taylor Morrison on 2026-07-24 for $72.50 per share in cash, about $6.8B equity value and $8.5B enterprise value. Sheryl Palmer stays CEO and oversees integrating Taylor Morrison (including Esplanade, Yardly build-to-rent and Taylor Morrison Home Funding) with Berkshire's site-built builders in Clayton Properties Group (15 regional builders). Combined 2025 closings were nearly 23,000 across 21 states, 52 markets and 700+ communities.
deals.map_impact: Rank 6 Taylor Morrison is no longer public and now shares an owner with rank 12 Clayton Properties Group. Berkshire says Taylor Morrison will lead a unified site-built operation, and Taylor Morrison's CMO told ResiClub (2026-08-20) that all of Clayton's site-built builders will roll up under Taylor Morrison while manufactured/modular stays with Clayton Homes; so the two rows effectively become one Berkshire platform of about 23,000 closings, the 4th largest US builder (level with NVR). Sheryl Palmer leads it. acquirer_builder_id is null because Berkshire itself is not a ranked builder; its ranked subsidiary is clayton-properties-group.
deals.source_title: Taylor Morrison newsroom: Berkshire Hathaway Completes Acquisition of Taylor Morrison (2026-07-24)

deals.acquirer: Mungo Homes (Clayton Home Building Group / Berkshire Hathaway)
deals.description: Mungo Homes acquired McGuinn Homes, announced 2026-07-02; the release says Mungo 'announced the acquisition' and gives no separate closing date. Price not disclosed. McGuinn builds in Aiken, Columbia, Greenville, Hilton Head and Sumter SC and Augusta and Savannah GA, has about 75 employees and was projected to close nearly 800 homes in 2026 (ResiClub puts 2025 closings at 993 and says build-to-rent has at times been the bulk of its business). Whelan Advisory advised McGuinn.
deals.map_impact: Rank 65 McGuinn Homes is absorbed into Mungo Homes, a Clayton Properties Group (rank 12) builder, so the McGuinn row disappears into Clayton and, after the Taylor Morrison roll-up, into the Berkshire site-built platform. Adds Augusta GA and Aiken SC and build-to-rent relationships. Founder Wade McGuinn sold; HousingWire reports McGuinn will become part of the Mungo platform rather than stay stand-alone.
deals.source_title: Mungo Homes: Mungo Homes Acquires McGuinn Homes, Expands Southeast Presence (2026-07-02)

deals.description: Eastwood Homes acquired Peachtree Building Group, announced 2026-05-26; the release says Eastwood 'announced the acquisition' and Zelman, the seller's adviser, calls it a completed May sale. Price not disclosed. Peachtree is a private south-Atlanta builder; per Zelman the deal lifts Eastwood's Atlanta production from about 120 closings a year to about 350-400, and the seller's principals stay on as development partners. Most Peachtree operations stay with Eastwood, which now has 11 divisions; its second purchase in about 18 months after Napolitano Homes (Virginia, 2025). JTW Advisors advised Eastwood, Zelman Partners advised Peachtree.
deals.map_impact: No top-100 row disappears: Peachtree is outside the top 100. Rank 46 Eastwood Homes roughly triples its Atlanta volume and should move up a few places on closings.
deals.source_title: Metro Atlanta CEO (staff report reproducing the company release): Eastwood Homes Expands Further into Metro Atlanta Through Acquisition of Peachtree Building Group (2026-05-27)

deals.description: Sumitomo Forestry completed its all-cash purchase of NYSE-listed Tri Pointe Homes on 2026-05-14 (merger agreement dated 2026-02-13); Tri Pointe survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry and deregistered its shares (SEC filing). Per trade press the price was $47.00 per share, about $4.5B; Tri Pointe keeps its brand, Irvine home office and management under CEO Doug Bauer; it had 160+ active communities, and with Sumitomo's five existing US builders the group expects about 15,000 US homes a year across 18 states against a 23,000-a-year 2030 goal. In November 2026 Sumitomo cut its 2026 US closings forecast to 12,705 (from 14,160) and called Tri Pointe synergies with its other US builders its top priority.
deals.map_impact: Rank 19 Tri Pointe Homes is no longer a listed company; it becomes a sister of rank 15 DRB Group (builder_id drb-group) (Sumitomo Forestry's other top-100 builder) and Sumitomo's other US builders. The Tri Pointe row stays as a separate brand but its parent changes to Sumitomo Forestry; combined Sumitomo US volume is roughly top-five scale. Leadership stayed. Watch for consolidation between Tri Pointe and the other Sumitomo builders in 2027.
deals.source_title: Tri Pointe Homes Form S-8 POS filed 2026-05-14 (merger with Sumitomo Forestry completed May 14, 2026); price and operating details from HousingWire 2026-05-14 and Builder and Developer 2026-05-21

deals.description: Closed 2026-05-04 (announced 2026-02-23; merger agreement dated 2026-02-22). Stanley Martin acquired Nasdaq-listed United Homes Group by merger for $1.18 per share in cash, an enterprise value of about $221 million; the stock and warrants were delisted. The executive officers listed in the closing 8-K, including chief executive Jack Micenko and executive chairman Michael Nieri, ceased to be officers at closing.
deals.map_impact: United Homes Group (#56, 1,192 closings in the ranking) is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Stanley Martin (#18): the two rows share one owner, Daiwa House. United Homes' top leadership left at closing. Adds Greenville, Spartanburg, Clemson, Columbia and Myrtle Beach, South Carolina and Augusta, Georgia to Stanley Martin (per HousingWire).
deals.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2026-05-04 (completion of merger with Stanley Martin Homes)

deals.description: Toll Brothers bought substantially all the assets and operations of Buffington Homes, a private builder in Fayetteville AR: it signed on 2026-04-21 and its 10-Q says the deal closed in May 2026 (exact day not disclosed), was accounted for as an asset acquisition and was not material. Price not disclosed. Brought about 1,500 owned or controlled home sites across nine active or coming-soon communities, priced from the $400,000s to over $1M. All Buffington employees joined Toll; partners Clay Carlton and Mike Lamberth stay to focus on land acquisition and development. Builder Advisor Group advised Buffington.
deals.map_impact: No top-100 row changes: Buffington is not ranked. Rank 9 Toll Brothers enters northwest Arkansas (Fayetteville / Bentonville) with about 1,500 lots.
deals.source_title: Toll Brothers 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, Note 2 Acquisition (announcement terms from Toll release of 2026-04-21)

deals.description: Agreement signed and business transfer executed 2026-03-19 US time (2026-03-20 Japan time). Trumark bought the single-family homebuilding business of Sumner, Washington-based JK Monarch: land, homes and staff in the Seattle metro area. JK Monarch delivered 59 homes in 2024 on about $53 million of revenue and had about 600 lots secured at the end of February 2026. Price not disclosed; Daiwa House said the effect on its results is minimal.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (JK Monarch unranked). Trumark (#66) adds a Washington division, its first market outside California and Colorado; Daiwa House's three US builders (Stanley Martin, CastleRock, Trumark) now reach the Pacific Northwest.
deals.source_title: Daiwa House Industry press release: Trumark Companies to Acquire the Single-Family Housing Business of Monarch (2026-03-23)

deals.description: Announced 2026-03-10: Tokyo-based Hajime Construction, an Iida Group company, took a 51% stake and management control of Utah builder Wright Homes (founded 1994, Wasatch Front). Founder Derek Wright and his team stay as operators and minority owners and the brand continues. Price not stated in the source; a closing date was not confirmed.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (target unranked). Second US builder stake for Iida Group after Patrick Malloy Communities; one of four Japanese-buyer deals that opened 2026.
deals.source_title: HousingWire: Hajime Construction Buys 51% of Utah Builder Wright Homes (2026-03-12)

deals.description: Closed 2026-01-14 (announced 2026-01-16). Single-family rental owner Invitation Homes bought Atlanta-based ResiBuilt, a fee builder of build-to-rent communities, for $89 million plus up to $7.5 million of incentive payments. It came with 23 active building contracts and an option on about 1,500 lots; no land transferred. ResiBuilt has built more than 4,200 homes since 2018 in Georgia, Florida and the Carolinas. Former parent Resicap stays independent.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (neither party is a ranked for-sale builder). A rental landlord bringing a homebuilder in-house; relevant to build-to-rent lot demand in the Southeast.
deals.source_title: The Real Deal: Invitation Homes Buys ResiBuilt for $89M (2026-01-19)

deals.acquirer: None (company-run review of strategic alternatives, including a sale or merger)
deals.description: Review ended without a deal, disclosed 2025-10-19/20. On 2025-05-19 United Homes Group's board formed a special committee of independent directors to review strategic alternatives. In October 2025 the committee concluded the company should stay independent given market conditions; four independent directors then said they would resign after controlling stockholder and executive chairman Michael Nieri declined to step down from that role, and two other directors also resigned.
deals.map_impact: No map change at the time: United Homes Group (#56) stayed independent. It set up the February 2026 agreement to sell to Stanley Martin at $1.18 per share.
deals.source_title: United Homes Group 8-K filed 2025-10-20 (conclusion of strategic review; director resignations)

deals.description: Closed in October 2025 (exact day not disclosed; trade press reported it as done on 2025-10-10). D.R. Horton bought the homebuilding operations of Greenville, South Carolina-based SK Builders for about $80 million in cash: about 160 homes in inventory, 260 lots and a backlog of 110 sold homes, plus control of about 1,320 more lots through purchase contracts. The sellers kept their land development business (HousingWire).
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (SK Builders is not in the top 100). D.R. Horton (#1) deepens Greenville/Spartanburg; the sellers continue as a land developer.
deals.source_title: D.R. Horton 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 (SK Builders acquisition)

deals.description: Closed 2025-09-25 US time (announced 2025-09-17). Stanley Martin bought the assets and operations of Greensboro, North Carolina builder Windsor Homes: land, homes and staff in the Triad (Greensboro, Winston-Salem, High Point) and Wilmington. Windsor delivered 334 homes in 2024 on about $124 million of revenue and had about 2,100 lots secured. Price not disclosed; Daiwa House said the effect on its results is not significant.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (Windsor unranked). Stanley Martin (#18) adds the North Carolina Triad and Wilmington and about 2,100 lots; first of three Stanley Martin acquisitions in under a year (United Homes Group and Holiday Builders followed in 2026).
deals.source_title: Daiwa House Industry press release: Stanley Martin Homes Has Acquired the Homebuilding Business of Windsor Homes (2025-09-26)

deals.acquirer: The New Home Company (Apollo funds); now Risewell Homes
deals.description: Closed 2025-06-25. Apollo-backed New Home Co, through Lido Holdco, completed a cash tender offer and merger for Nasdaq-listed Landsea Homes at $11.30 per share; about 83.3% of shares were tendered and Landsea was delisted. Landsea's 8-K says the deal was funded with debt, land bank funding and equity (Millrose's own filings show it bought $522.8M of the land; see the Millrose profile). Matthew Zaist became president and CEO; Landsea's executive officers left and its board resigned.
deals.map_impact: Landsea Homes disappears as a separate builder and the combined company is the #27 row, now named Risewell Homes (about 4,000 closings a year across roughly 10 markets per HousingWire). Leadership is New Home's; Landsea's leadership left. Millrose is the land banker of record on this deal.
deals.source_title: Landsea Homes Corp. 8-K filed 2025-06-25 (completion of merger with Lido Holdco / New Home Co)

deals.description: Closed 2025-05-14: Scott Felder Homes, the Central Texas builder owned by Kansas City private equity firm Platform Ventures, bought Olivia Clarke Homes, a builder founded in 2020 with five Dallas-Fort Worth communities. Olivia Clarke keeps its name and founder Jennifer Johnson stays. Terms not disclosed; Builder Advisor Group was exclusive advisor.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map: neither party is ranked. Private-equity-backed platform adding Dallas-Fort Worth to Austin, San Antonio and Denver.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Platform's Scott Felder Buys Olivia Clarke In Strategic Stretch (2025-05-14)

deals.description: Closed 2025-05-02. Dream Finders bought Atlanta homebuilder Green River Builders, Inc.; cash consideration was $32.8 million as first reported in the Q2 2025 10-Q (purchase accounting was preliminary). Reported in the Southeast segment.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Second Atlanta acquisition in 2025 for Dream Finders (#14), after Liberty Communities.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 10-Q for Q2 2025, Business Acquisitions note

deals.acquirer: Iida Group Holdings (via Arnest One America)
deals.description: Iida's subsidiary Arnest One set up Arnest One America to subscribe for new shares giving it 60% of PMCO Holdings, the parent of Atlanta-area builder Patrick Malloy Communities, for about $55.1 million, with closing expected in late April 2025; the deal was announced in Iida's Tokyo filing dated 2025-04-07 (summarized 2025-04-14). PMCO had 2024 sales of $117 million and operating profit of $18.8 million. HousingWire (2025-08-04) put the investment at about $52 million and the implied whole-company value just under $90 million, and treated the deal as newly public in late July 2025; a closing date was not confirmed.
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map (target unranked). First US builder controlled by Iida Group, a new Japanese entrant alongside Sekisui House, Daiwa House and Sumitomo Forestry.
deals.source_title: FilingReader summary of Iida Group Holdings notice: subsidiary to acquire US housing firm (2025-04-14)

deals.description: Effective 2025-04-01 (announced 2025-03-28 by Sumitomo Forestry America): Dallas-based Brightland Homes was consolidated under Rockville, Maryland-based DRB Group. This is an internal combination of two Sumitomo Forestry builders, not a purchase from a third party. Per HousingWire (2025-04-16) the combined DRB spans 14 states and 19 divisions, expected about 9,000 closings in 2025, and is led by DRB chief executive Ronny Salameh.
deals.map_impact: Brightland Homes disappears as a separate ranked row; its volume is in DRB Group (#15, parent Sumitomo Forestry). DRB's leader stayed; Brightland's separate leadership did not continue at the top.
deals.source_title: Brightland Homes press page: Brightland Homes to Consolidate Under DRB Group (release dated 2025-03-28)

deals.description: Reported on 2025-03-10 as set to close that night (a separate closing confirmation was not found). Davidson Homes bought Columbus, Georgia-based Evermore Homes (formerly American Southern Homes), a roll-up of Grayhawk Homes (Georgia), Stoneridge Homes (Alabama) and Dorn Homes (Arizona) that sold after running into capital constraints. Terms not disclosed.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Davidson (#43) gets its first Arizona position plus more Southeast volume; Evermore's brands fold into Davidson.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Davidson Homes Seals Down Last Details To Acquire Evermore Homes (2025-03-10)

deals.description: Closed 2025-02-10 (previously announced). Lennar bought the homebuilding operations of Fayetteville, Arkansas-based Rausch Coleman, which delivered about 5,300 homes at an average price of about $230,000 in calendar 2024. Millrose Properties, just spun off from Lennar, bought Rausch Coleman's land and Lennar holds options on it. Lennar did not disclose a price; Construction Briefing (2025-05-13) cited a $900 million transaction value.
deals.map_impact: Rausch Coleman no longer exists as a separate ranked builder: its roughly 5,300 annual closings are inside Lennar (#2). Lennar gained new markets in Arkansas (including Bentonville/Fayetteville and Little Rock), Tulsa, Birmingham and Kansas City. First builder acquisition financed with Millrose land banking, the template later used for New Home Co / Landsea.
deals.source_title: Lennar press release: Lennar Completes Acquisition of Rausch Coleman Homes (2025-02-10)

deals.description: Reported 2025-02-07 as acquired: Canada-based Empire Communities bought Charlotte, North Carolina builder SouthCraft Builders, an attainable-price builder that keeps its operations and leadership under Empire. Terms not disclosed. Builder Advisor Group advised SouthCraft. Follows Empire's 2024 purchase of Covington Homes in Colorado.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Empire (#61, listed as Empire Homes) deepens Charlotte with a lower price point; SouthCraft's volume now counts inside Empire.
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Empire Building: SouthCraft Expands U.S. Footprint, Scale (2025-02-07)

deals.description: Closed 2025-02-04 per Construction Briefing: Defy Investments, a newly formed investment company under Rival Holdings, bought Indianapolis builder Davis Homes. Price undisclosed. The buyer described a buy-and-hold approach and plans to test construction technology (HousingWire interview, 2025-02-06).
deals.map_impact: No change to the top-100 map: neither party is ranked. Example of a financial (non-builder) buyer taking a private regional builder.
deals.source_title: Construction Briefing: What's driving the consolidation of US homebuilders? (2025-05-13)

deals.description: Announced as completed on 2025-01-31: privately held Drees Homes bought San Antonio-based Monticello Homes, a roughly 30-year-old builder. Price and closings not disclosed in the source. Founder Wayne Moravits stays as a consultant for at least a year.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges. Drees (#37) adds San Antonio and now builds in all four big Texas markets (Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin, San Antonio).
deals.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Drees Forays Into San Antonio With Monticello Homes Purchase (2025-01-31)

deals.description: Closed 2025-01-23. Dream Finders bought the majority of the homebuilding business of Georgia-based Liberty Communities, LLC (certain assets and assumed liabilities) for $112.7 million in cash; the former owner also received a redeemable noncontrolling interest in DFH Liberty, LLC valued at $8.1 million, with rights to a share of future earnings above a threshold. Trade press (The Real Deal, 2025-02-03) adds that the purchase included Liberty's offsite manufacturing and component import businesses.
deals.map_impact: No rank row merges (Liberty is not in the top 100). Dream Finders (#14) entered Atlanta and enlarged Greenville, South Carolina; Liberty's volume is inside the Dream Finders row.
deals.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 10-Q for Q2 2025, Business Acquisitions note

articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: closes $2.2B Beazer purchase with $572M Millrose land-bank facility
articles.summary: Dream Finders closed its all-cash Beazer purchase Oct. 20, 2026 ($33.50 a share, about $2.2B enterprise value), funded by a $572.1M Millrose land bank facility and $675M of preferred; Millrose says it bought about $488M (net of discount).
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose put land banking and preferred equity behind a top-25 builder merger (homesite count and 12% rate per Millrose's Oct. 27 release), a whole-company financing package Domain will be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Closed the acquisition of Beazer Homes on 2026-10-20 ($33.50 a share, about $878.4M), funded by $572.1M from a Millrose land bank facility and $675M of 12% Series B convertible preferred, about $488M of it bought by Millrose.

articles.title: Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback
articles.summary: Millrose Q3 2026: net income $130.0M, AFFO $0.80/share, invested capital about $9.25B, $3.4B of it outside Lennar across 21 non-Lennar counterparties; non-Lennar yield 10.8% vs 8.5% on Lennar; $250M buyback authorized.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is pricing non-Lennar option capital at about 10.8% and now pairs land banking with preferred equity to win whole-company deals, a benchmark for Domain bids and a package Domain will be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Millrose closed about $1.1B of capital support on Oct. 20, 2026 for the Beazer acquisition: about $580M of land banking across roughly 7,000 homesites plus about $488M of preferred equity at a 12% dividend.

articles.title: Lennar’s land bank spinoff Millrose bought 1,200 single-family rentals
articles.summary: Millrose bought 1,233 completed Lennar homes in 18 states for about $333M to hold as rentals, disclosed with Q3 results. Hunterbrook, a media outlet whose affiliate is short Lennar and Millrose, had reported the purchases; Lennar stock fell Oct. 2.
articles.why_it_matters: A competitor is taking finished homes off Domain's named customer's books, a service Domain does not offer Lennar, and the short report and lawsuit give Lennar a reason to spread land-bank business to other providers, Domain included.

suggested_update.text: In Q3 2026 Lennar sold 1,233 completed single-family homes in 18 states to Millrose for about $333M, to be held as rentals (per Millrose's Oct. 27, 2026 results release).

articles.title: Lennar snags 444 lots near TSMC’s $265B Phoenix project for $60M
articles.summary: AGWIP Asset Management, described as Lennar's land banker, paid $60.14 million cash for 444 lots on 132 acres near TSMC's north Phoenix site, closing Sept. 15. Seller Aroundtown Agua Fria plans about 2,000 more lots nearby.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar placed a $60 million Phoenix lot deal with a land banker other than Domain, and the seller has roughly 2,000 more lots coming within three years that will also need land-bank capital; worth confirming whose capital sits behind AGWIP.

suggested_update.text: AGWIP Asset Management, acting as Lennar's land banker, bought 444 lots (132 acres) near TSMC in north Phoenix for $60.14 million cash, closing Sept. 15, 2026 (Phoenix Business Journal via KTAR).

articles.title: Starwood Capital Group and Trez Capital Announce Strategic Partnership Focused on U.S. Residential Land Financing
articles.summary: Starwood Capital and Canada's Trez Capital announced Nov. 3, 2026 a partnership to originate land acquisition and development loans for US single-family communities, seeded with a $450M Trez loan portfolio and targeting more than $1B of originations a year.
articles.why_it_matters: Starwood is putting institutional capital behind A&D loans at $1B-plus a year, a debt alternative builders and developers can use instead of a Domain land bank; Anthony Murphy at Starwood and John Hutchinson at Trez lead it.

articles.title: Strata Land launches as builders face land-capital squeeze
articles.summary: Strata Land Partners launched Nov. 2, 2026, backed by Wafra and Hunt Companies and led by Michael Forsum, former Landsea Homes president. Its first projects cover about 1,300 lots; capital committed was not disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: A new land-capital platform aimed at public and especially private builders nationwide, run by an operator who knows builders personally, is a direct new competitor for Domain's mid-size builder deals.

articles.title: Millrose Properties, Inc. Announces Pricing of $1.0 Billion Senior Notes Offering
articles.summary: Millrose priced $1.0B of senior notes Sept. 22 and closed Oct. 6, 2026: $500M 6.500% due 2029 and $500M 6.750% due 2031. Proceeds and a $500M term-loan draw may buy Dream Finders–Beazer homesites and repay an $850M revolver balance.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose raised about $1.5B of fresh debt partly to take on Dream Finders–Beazer homesites; its 6.5%–6.75% unsecured cost of funds is a benchmark for how cheaply Domain's main rival can price option deals.

suggested_update.text: Millrose priced $1.0B of senior notes on Sept 22, 2026, partly to acquire homesites from the combined Dream Finders–Beazer; the 2031 tranche must be redeemed if the deal had not closed by May 13, 2027.

articles.title: Five Point Holdings, LLC Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
articles.summary: Five Point Q3 2026: revenue $14.6M, net loss $4.4M, no land sales closed, deferred to 2027; full-year net income guide about $20M; liquidity $576.2M. Hearthstone land banking: about $3.4B under management ($2.8B fee-paying), $6.5M quarterly fees ($18.2M year to date).
articles.why_it_matters: Five Point owns rival land banker Hearthstone, backed by Blue Owl-managed funds, so this sizes a competitor at about $3.4B under management and shows California land sellers deferring sales rather than cutting prices.

articles.title: Texas County and District Retirement System commits $200m to TPG Essential Housing IV
articles.summary: Texas County and District Retirement System committed $200M to TPG Essential Housing IV, a TPG Angelo Gordon closed-end fund seeking $3B of equity; Kern County's pension committed $50M in August.
articles.why_it_matters: TPG Angelo Gordon is raising a $3B fourth Essential Housing fund and pensions are writing $200M tickets, which means more competing land-bank capital chasing the same builders and the same LPs Domain courts.

articles.title: AREC raises $390 million to finance lot and land deals for builders
articles.summary: Avila Real Estate Capital raised $390M from an insurer and a university endowment, taking total capital above $750M. It lends against land, lots and homes for builders; investors include D.R. Horton, LGI, Century, Toll, Dream Finders and DRB.
articles.why_it_matters: A builder-backed lot lender with a stated goal of financing 100,000 lots in five years is competing capital for the finished-lot deals Domain funds, and six top-20 builders are its investors.
articles.collected_via: bing-news: capital-markets: homebuilders land spending lots earnings

articles.title: Millrose 8-K: amends Lennar founder's rights and Kennedy Lewis management agreements
articles.summary: On Aug. 27, 2026 Millrose amended its Founder's Rights Agreement with Lennar (Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right; its secured-financing collateral consent right) and its Kennedy Lewis management agreement (investment guidelines scope, reimbursable expenses). No figures disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: Changes to Lennar's priority claim on Millrose capital and to what Kennedy Lewis is allowed to invest in determine how much Millrose capacity is free to compete for Domain's other builders; the exhibits are worth reading.

suggested_update.text: On Aug. 27, 2026 Lennar and Millrose amended the Founder's Rights Agreement, adjusting the Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right and its secured-financing collateral consent right (amounts not stated in the 8-K body).

articles.title: Arixa Capital Surpasses $9 Billion in Loan Originations, Expands Homebuilder Finance Program
articles.summary: Arixa Capital passed $9 billion in loan originations and is expanding homebuilder finance under new EVP Jim Sawitzke, ex-Brio Homebuilder Solutions (Blackstone). Its Pro Builder program recently made $30M to $80M loans in seven states.
articles.why_it_matters: Another private lender is scaling acquisition-through-construction loans of up to $80 million to established builders, a substitute for land-bank capital, and Sawitzke is a contact worth knowing.

articles.title: Century Communities Triples Dallas-Fort Worth Footprint with Acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes
articles.summary: Century Communities bought substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes (HMH Lifestyles), a Dallas-Fort Worth builder founded in 1949, closing Oct. 7, 2026; price undisclosed. It roughly triples Century's DFW community count, adding 29 communities, in one Grapevine division.
articles.why_it_matters: The 10th-largest builder absorbed the 77th, consolidating DFW lot positions; any option or land-bank contracts HistoryMaker held now sit with Century, so Domain should check its exposure and approach Century's DFW land team.

suggested_update.text: Acquired substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes (DFW) on Oct 7, 2026 (price undisclosed), tripling its Dallas-Fort Worth community count.

articles.title: KB Home 8-K: real estate EVP Albert Praw to retire Nov 30, no successor named
articles.summary: KB Home's Albert Z. Praw, EVP Real Estate and Business Development, will retire November 30, 2026 after more than 30 years. He is expected to advise on land relationships and transactions for up to a year; no successor named.
articles.why_it_matters: KB Home's top land executive is leaving with no successor named, so whoever takes over land decisions at the seventh-largest builder is a person Domain should identify and call now, while Praw is still advising on land relationships.

suggested_update.text: Albert Z. Praw retires as EVP, Real Estate and Business Development effective November 30, 2026 (8-K filed November 16, 2026); he stays as a non-employee adviser on land relationships for up to one year and no successor has been named.

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: Jim Francescon named President from Jan 1; Robert stays CEO
articles.summary: Century Communities' board on Nov. 4, 2026 elected James (Jim) Francescon, 37, EVP of corporate operations, President effective Jan. 1, 2027, overseeing homebuilding, land and M&A. Robert Francescon stays CEO and sole principal executive officer; Dale Francescon stays Executive Chairman.
articles.why_it_matters: The next-generation leader at a top-10 builder is now named, and he comes from private equity and investment banking, so he is a person Domain should get in front of on land-capital decisions.

suggested_update.text: James Francescon (EVP, Corporate Operations) becomes President effective 2027-01-01; Robert J. Francescon remains CEO and becomes sole principal executive officer (8-K filed 2026-11-09).

articles.title: DAVID WEEKLEY HOMES NAMES NEW CFO AND ADDS CMO TO LEADERSHIP TEAM
articles.summary: David Weekley Homes named Adam Zylman CFO on Aug. 31, 2026, succeeding Heather Humphrey, who retires after 33 years and stays as an adviser. Zylman founded Grey Owl Partners and co-founded Sunland Capital.
articles.why_it_matters: David Weekley, the 17th-largest builder, has a new CFO from private equity. He now decides how it funds land, so Domain should introduce itself.

suggested_update.text: Adam Zylman named CFO (announced 2026-08-31), succeeding retiring CFO Heather Humphrey, who moves to an advisory role.

articles.collected_via: bing-news: builder-ma: homebuilder names chief financial officer

articles.title: S&P downgrades Dream Finders to ’B+’ following $2.2B acquisition of Beazer Homes
articles.summary: S&P cut Dream Finders to B+ from BB- (stable outlook) after it closed the $2.2B all-cash Beazer acquisition, citing about $720M of assumed Beazer notes and debt-like preferred; it cites $800M of land-bank capital from Millrose.
articles.why_it_matters: A single-B Dream Finders with leverage expected to stay elevated through 2028 needs off-balance-sheet lot capital more than ever, and the article names Millrose as its land-bank partner with $800M, so Domain is competing against Millrose for the combined company's lots.

suggested_update.text: Oct 20, 2026: S&P downgraded Dream Finders to B+ from BB- (stable) after closing the $2.2B Beazer acquisition; report cites $800M of Millrose land-bank capital.

articles.title: Lennar 424B5: prices $600M of senior notes due 2029 and 2032
articles.summary: Lennar priced $600M of senior notes Oct. 13, 2026 and closed them Oct. 15: $300M 5.700% due 2029 (T+80) and $300M 5.950% due 2032 (T+95), expected ratings Baa2/BBB/BBB+. Net proceeds about $594.5M for general corporate purposes.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar, a named Domain relationship, can still borrow unsecured for three to five years at under 6%, which is the cost of capital any land-bank proposal to it is measured against.

suggested_update.text: Priced $600M of senior notes on 2026-10-13: $300M 5.700% due October 2029 and $300M 5.950% due January 2032, net proceeds about $594.5M for general corporate purposes.

articles.title: Lennar 8-K: Q3 net earnings $284M on $8.0B revenue; delivery guide cut to 80,000-81,000
articles.summary: Lennar Q3 (Aug 31): net earnings $284M ($1.19/share) on $8.0B revenue; deliveries 20,840, orders down 9%, gross margin 15.8%. Controls about 488,000 homesites, under 2.5% owned; called rising option maintenance fees a real cost. Delivery guide cut to 80,000-81,000.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar is almost fully land-light with $7.33B of deposits and pre-acquisition costs outstanding, so its lower delivery guide and thinner margin bear directly on takedown pace and option pricing for its land bankers, Domain included.

suggested_update.text: At Aug 31, 2026 Lennar owned or controlled about 488,000 homesites with under 2.5% owned; homebuilding debt to total capital 16.6%; fiscal 2026 delivery guide lowered to 80,000-81,000 homes.

articles.title: Housing M&A shifts as global capital retargets residential futures
articles.summary: At the Zelman Housing Summit, Essential Housing CEO Steve Benson said land banking costs builders about 200-250 bp over blended capital cost and that the firm, with over $22B originated in five years, is raising about $10B more.
articles.why_it_matters: A direct competitor publicly stated its pricing (200–250 bp over builders' blended cost) and a roughly $10B capital raise, which tells Domain how a rival is pitching builders and how much capacity is coming.

suggested_update.text: At the Oct 2026 Zelman summit, Stanley Martin (Daiwa House) set a 10,000-closing target for 2027, said three recent acquisitions including Holiday Builders add about $1B of revenue, and is pausing single-family acquisitions to integrate them.

articles.title: Lennar 8-K: restates revolver at $3.795B, main tranche extended to Nov 2031
articles.summary: Lennar on Oct. 26, 2026 restated its unsecured revolver: commitments rise to $3.795B with a $750M accordion, and the main tranche extends to November 2031. It also drew $40M more term loan, to $1.75B due May 2028.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar has locked in more and longer bank liquidity at slightly lower cost, which sets the bank-debt benchmark Domain's land-bank pricing to Lennar is measured against.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility amended and restated 2026-10-26: commitments $3.795B plus $750M accordion, Class A maturity November 2031; term loan increased to $1.75B, due May 2028.

articles.title: LGI Homes 8-K: amends revolver to about $1.166B, $855M extended to Oct 2030
articles.summary: LGI Homes amended its revolver on Oct. 9, 2026: commitments about $1.166B (down from $1.1825B), $855M extended to Oct. 9, 2030, and an accordion of up to $175M (up from $95M) capped at $1.3B. Wells Fargo is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI just reset the bank line that funds its land, a natural moment to ask whether it wants off-balance-sheet lot capital alongside it.

suggested_update.text: Revolver amended 2026-10-09: commitments about $1.166B (down from $1.1825B), $855M now maturing 2030-10-09, accordion up to $175M (up from $95M) capped at $1.3B total; Wells Fargo agent.

articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: accordion adds $220M, revolver commitments to about $1.7B
articles.summary: Dream Finders Homes exercised a committed accordion on Oct. 9, 2026, raising its revolving credit commitments by $220M to about $1.7B. Other terms unchanged.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders was stacking bank capacity days before closing Beazer, alongside Millrose's land bank and preferred, showing how much outside capital this customer now needs.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility commitments increased by $220M to about $1.7B via accordion exercise on 2026-10-09.

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: credit facility raised to $1.2B, extended to Nov 2030
articles.summary: Century Communities amended its credit agreement on Sept. 30, 2026: commitments rise to $1.2B and maturity extends to Nov. 1, 2030 for extending lenders. Flagstar and Morgan Stanley join; BMO does not extend. U.S. Bank is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: Century has a larger, longer bank revolver to fund land on balance sheet, which reduces its near-term need for land-bank capital.

suggested_update.text: Credit agreement amended 2026-09-30: aggregate commitments increased to $1.2B and maturity extended to 2030-11-01 for extending lenders.

articles.title: Dream Finders 8-K: Q3 1,967 closings, net income $6.7M after $23M Beazer deal costs
articles.summary: Dream Finders Q3 2026: 1,967 closings; net income $6.7M after $23M of Beazer deal costs. Beazer acquisition closed Oct. 20, all cash, about $2.2B enterprise value. Controlled lots 52,574; lot deposits $490.2M; net debt-to-capital 48.1%.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders now carries Beazer at 48.1% net leverage and says it expects Q4 abandonment charges from terminating land deals that miss return thresholds, so its lot-option counterparties face walk-aways while the combined builder needs off-balance-sheet land capital.

suggested_update.text: Completed the all-cash acquisition of Beazer Homes on Oct. 20, 2026 at an enterprise value of about $2.2B; controlled lots were 52,574 and lot deposits $490.2M at Sept. 30, 2026.

articles.title: Forestar 8-K: chairman Tomnitz retires; CEO Anthony Oxley adds executive chairman role
articles.summary: Forestar executive chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired effective Oct. 31, 2026; CEO Anthony W. Oxley added the executive chairman role Nov. 1 as D.R. Horton's designee. Stacey H. Dwyer joined the board. Tomnitz advises through Sept. 2028.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar is D.R. Horton's majority-owned lot developer and an alternative to third-party land banking for the largest builder, so Oxley now holding both top roles is the person who sets how much of Horton's lot supply stays in-house.

suggested_update.text: At Forestar (D.R. Horton's majority-owned lot developer), Donald J. Tomnitz retired as Executive Chairman effective Oct. 31, 2026 and President/CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman as well on Nov. 1, 2026.

articles.title: HHHunt names CFO Ann Kelly as next CEO in 2027 C-suite reset
articles.summary: HHHunt will make CFO Ann Kelly CEO on July 1, 2027; CEO Buck Hunt stays chairman. SVP of finance and treasury Steve Brant becomes CFO; COO Steve Fritz stays.
articles.why_it_matters: HHHunt's finance chief is moving up and its treasurer is taking the CFO seat, so the people who would sign a land-bank deal there are changing and worth a call.

suggested_update.text: CFO Ann Kelly becomes CEO July 1, 2027 and SVP finance and treasury Steve Brant becomes CFO; Buck Hunt remains chairman (announced Oct 2026).

articles.title: Century Communities 8-K: Q3 2,442 deliveries, EPS $0.44, full-year guidance lowered
articles.summary: Century Q3 2026: 2,442 deliveries, EPS $0.44; full-year guidance lowered. Revolver upsized to $1.2B, extended to November 2030. Lots 60,969, 45.1% controlled; finished lot costs fell 3% sequentially. Record 343 communities; 360-370 expected at year-end including 29 from HistoryMaker.
articles.why_it_matters: Century's net leverage rose to 34.9% from 25.9% at year-end as it drew on its revolver and bought HistoryMaker, which makes it a builder with a reason to move more lots off balance sheet and one Domain should call (the revolver upsizing itself is scored on its own 8-K).

suggested_update.text: Acquired substantially all assets of HistoryMaker Homes on Oct. 7, 2026 (Dallas active communities from 12 to 41) and at the end of Q3 2026 upsized its revolver to $1.2B with maturity extended to November 2030.

articles.title: Lennar Financial Health, Subsidiary Spin-Off Draw Investor Suit
articles.summary: A Lennar shareholder filed a proposed securities class action in the Southern District of Florida against Lennar and two executives, alleging misleading statements about financial health and a subsidiary spinoff, including capitalized land-bank option costs.
articles.why_it_matters: The suit puts Lennar's accounting for land-bank option costs, and by extension the 2025 Millrose spin-off, under litigation scrutiny. That could change how Lennar and other builders structure and disclose option deals with Domain.

articles.title: Meritage 8-K: Q3 closings down 14% to 3,187, EPS $1.04; 31% of lots optioned
articles.summary: Meritage Q3 2026: 3,187 closings, down 14%; EPS $1.04; no Q4 guidance. Land spend $329M versus $528M. Of about 71,800 lots, 69% owned and 31% optioned, against a roughly 40% off-balance-sheet target. Net debt-to-capital 18.9%; revolver undrawn.
articles.why_it_matters: Meritage owns 69% of its lots against a 40% off-balance-sheet target while cutting land spend, so the fifth-largest builder has room to move lots into option structures; worth a call to its land and finance team.

articles.title: Forestar 8-K: FY2026 13,545 lots sold, $1.64B revenue; FY2027 guide 12,000-13,000 lots
articles.summary: Forestar fiscal 2026 (to Sept. 30): 13,545 lots sold, revenue $1.64B, net income $142.6M; Q4 average lot price $108,300. Owns 58,200 lots, controls 26,200; liquidity $1.3B. Fiscal 2027 guide: 12,000-13,000 lots, $1.4B-$1.5B revenue.
articles.why_it_matters: Forestar is the main finished-lot alternative to a land bank and is guiding to fewer lot deliveries next year, a read on builder takedown demand and on how much D.R. Horton lot supply it will cover.

articles.title: D.R. Horton 8-K: FY2026 84,202 closings, $33.0B revenue; 77% of 570,600 lots controlled
articles.summary: D.R. Horton fiscal 2026: 84,202 closings, $33.0B revenue, EPS $10.11. Lots 570,600, 23% owned and 77% controlled. Repaid $600M of 1.3% notes in October; bought back $3.6B of stock. FY2027 guide: 79,000 to 84,000 closings.
articles.why_it_matters: The largest builder moved to 77% controlled lots with 68% of closings on Forestar or third-party-developed lots, while total lots fell to 570,600 and guidance is flat to down, so its demand for new third-party lot capital is steady rather than growing.

suggested_update.text: At Sept. 30, 2026 D.R. Horton held 570,600 lots, 23% owned and 77% controlled (down from 591,900 a year earlier), and it repaid $600M of 1.3% senior notes at maturity in October 2026.

articles.title: KB Home 8-K: Q3 revenue down 20% to $1.30B, net income $65.3M; $722M land spend
articles.summary: KB Home Q3 (Aug 31): revenue $1.30B, down 20%; net income $65.3M; 61,581 lots, about 60% owned and 40% under contract; debt to capital 35.7%; $415M drawn on revolver; land spend $722M, up 40%.
articles.why_it_matters: KB Home still owns about 60% of its lots while leverage climbs and it borrows on its revolver to fund land, which is the profile of a builder that could use land-bank capital.

suggested_update.text: At Aug 31, 2026: 61,581 lots (about 60% owned, 40% under contract), debt to capital 35.7%, $415.0M drawn on the credit facility, total liquidity $942.4M.

articles.title: Smith Douglas 8-K: Q3 831 closings, net income $3.0M; gross margin 16.3% vs 21.0%
articles.summary: Smith Douglas Q3 2026: 831 closings, $262.5M home closing revenue, net income $3.0M; closing gross margin 16.3% versus 21.0% a year earlier. Controls 24,724 lots, about 92% optioned. Debt to book capitalization 18.8%, up from 9.0% at year-end.
articles.why_it_matters: Smith Douglas runs almost entirely on optioned lots, so a five-point margin drop and doubling leverage tell Domain how much room this kind of customer has left to pay option costs.

suggested_update.text: At Sept 30, 2026: 24,724 controlled lots, 22,693 optioned (about 92%); notes payable $101.4M; debt to book capitalization 18.8% (9.0% at Dec 31, 2025).

articles.title: LGI Homes 8-K: Q3 closings up 11.6% to 1,189, EPS $1.05; 2026 guide 4,600-4,800
articles.summary: LGI Homes Q3 2026: 1,189 closings, up 11.6%; EPS $1.05. Lots 58,400 (50,270 owned, 8,130 controlled). Net debt-to-capital 40.6%; liquidity $447.7M. 2026 closings guide narrowed to 4,600-4,800; targets 180-plus communities by end-2027 from 151, partly via developers' finished lots.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI still owns 86% of its lots at 40.6% net leverage and calls its position predominantly self-developed and on balance sheet, which makes it one of the larger untapped candidates for a land-bank conversation.

articles.title: LGI Homes, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
articles.summary: LGI Homes reported Q3 2026: net orders fell 61.2% to 609 and backlog to 685 homes. It owned 50,270 lots and controlled 8,130 at Sept 30; net debt-to-capital was 40.6% and liquidity $447.7M.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI owns most of its lots while orders collapse and its controlled count grows, so it is a candidate for land-light capital Domain could offer.

suggested_update.text: At Sept 30, 2026: 50,270 owned and 8,130 controlled lots, net debt-to-capital 40.6%, liquidity $447.7M (Q3 2026 results, Nov 3, 2026).

articles.title: NVR 8-K: Q3 settlements down 7% to 5,268, EPS $89.45; lots controlled up to 185,300
articles.summary: NVR Q3 2026: 5,268 settlements, down 7%; EPS $89.45; gross margin 18.3% versus 21.0%. Lots controlled rose to 185,300 from 175,300. About $24.8M of contract land deposit impairments. Repurchased $237.2M of stock.
articles.why_it_matters: NVR, the pure lot-option builder, wrote off about $24.8M of lot deposits in one quarter while still adding 10,000 controlled lots, a sign that option deals struck at earlier prices are being walked or reserved against.

articles.title: Downtown Las Vegas land sells for big new housing project
articles.summary: Nevada sold the roughly 23-acre former Grant Sawyer state office site in downtown Las Vegas for $10.6 million to a New York investment firm, which reportedly gave Lennar an option for a 1,000-plus-home project (snippet only; paywalled).
articles.why_it_matters: If the paywalled report holds, an unnamed New York investor is land-banking a Lennar site, so Domain should find out which firm is taking Lennar option deals in Las Vegas; scored from the snippet only.

suggested_update.text: Reported 2026-11-15: a New York investment firm bought the former Grant Sawyer site in downtown Las Vegas for $10.6 million and gave Lennar an option on it for a planned 1,000-plus-home project.

articles.title: IHP Capital Partners acquires 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas, for new residential community
articles.summary: IHP Capital Partners, with developer Scarborough Lane Development, agreed to buy 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas, for the Peachtree master plan (about 3,400 finished lots). A first phase of 206 acres and 535 lots has closed; price not disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: A rival residential land capital provider is committing to a multi-phase, roughly 3,400-lot Houston-area position, finished lots that builders there could buy instead of using a Domain land bank.

articles.title: M/I Homes 8-K: Q3 2,241 deliveries, EPS $2.56; 52% of 48,934 lots under contract
articles.summary: M/I Homes Q3 2026: 2,241 deliveries, down 2%; EPS $2.56. Lots 48,934, about 48% owned and 52% under contract. Q3 land spend $135.2M on purchases plus $154.4M on development. Homebuilding debt-to-capital 18%; undrawn $900M facility; $50M of buybacks.
articles.why_it_matters: M/I already has 25,509 lots under contract and keeps buying land with $620M of cash and an undrawn revolver, so it can self-fund and would use Domain only if the option cost beats very cheap balance-sheet capital.

articles.title: Why 2027 may turn into a land negotiation year for homebuilders
articles.summary: Scott Cox of SLC Advisors expects 2027 to bring land re-trades and real price cuts, with builders refusing roughly 10% land-bank carry and pushing slower takedowns. He predicts Millrose will cut option fees and ease takedowns to keep assets.
articles.why_it_matters: An opinion piece, but it is the argument builders' land teams will bring to Domain in 2027: lower option fees, softer takedowns, and a claim that Millrose's asset-based fee makes it concede first.
articles.collected_via: bing-news: capital-markets: homebuilders land market lot prices

articles.title: Why homebuilders and lot sellers no longer price risk the same way
articles.summary: Tony Avila (Builder Advisor Group, Avila Real Estate Capital) says patient-capital lot sellers can hold out while builders underwrite at lower margins; bank AD&C lending is ~$90B vs $200B+ in 2006, with private land capital filling the gap.
articles.why_it_matters: Describes a widening gap between lot-seller pricing and builder underwriting and names a private debt fund (AREC, backed by ~15 builders) competing to fund lots, which bears on Domain's option pricing and competing capital.
articles.collected_via: bing-news: capital-markets: homebuilders land spending lots earnings

articles.title: Millrose Properties: New Builder Capital Earns 210 Basis Points More
articles.summary: Investor analysis from September: Millrose's non-Lennar capital earned 10.6% against 8.5% on the legacy Lennar portfolio as of June, with shares near 0.87 times book. Since superseded by Q3 figures.
articles.why_it_matters: Shows the roughly two-point premium Millrose charges builders other than Lennar, a reference point for Domain's own option pricing.

articles.title: Tri Pointe 8-K: Q3 1,084 deliveries, $706.8M revenue; $21.1M inventory charges
articles.summary: Tri Pointe Q3 2026: 1,084 deliveries versus 1,217; home sales revenue $706.8M; gross margin 17.6% after $21.1M of inventory charges. Lots 32,444, about 51% owned and 49% controlled. Homebuilding debt-to-capital 25.9%; liquidity about $1.1B.
articles.why_it_matters: Tri Pointe's release refers to its integration into the Sumitomo Forestry Group, so land-financing decisions on its 15,761 controlled lots may now be shaped by a parent with its own capital rather than by third-party land bankers.

articles.title: Taylor Morrison Home stock ends after USD 6.8 billion deal
articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway closed its Taylor Morrison purchase July 24, 2026 at $72.50 a share (about $6.8B equity, $8.5B enterprise value), pairing it with Clayton Properties; it now calls itself the fourth-largest US builder and holds over 10% of Lennar.
articles.why_it_matters: Berkshire now owns a top-10 builder through Taylor Morrison and Clayton and holds over 10% of Lennar, a deep-pocketed owner that can fund land on balance sheet rather than through land bankers like Domain; the deal closed before the window, so no M&A floor.

suggested_update.text: Acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on Jul 24, 2026 at $72.50 per share cash (about $6.8B equity, $8.5B EV); delisted from NYSE and run alongside Clayton Properties Group.

articles.title: St. Cloud land sells for $38.85M as seller agrees to $2.2B acquisition
articles.summary: Orlando Business Journal reports a 38-acre St. Cloud, Fla., property sold for $38.85M; the seller had agreed to a $2.2B acquisition (Beazer, by Dream Finders). Paywalled; the URL names Millrose, but its role is unconfirmed.
articles.why_it_matters: If Millrose bought this Beazer land for Dream Finders' pipeline, it is a competitor taking Orlando lots from a top-25 builder; worth reading the article to confirm before scoring higher.
articles.collected_via: bing-news: trade press: site:bizjournals.com homebuilder land acquisition lots

articles.title: Beazer 8-K: to redeem $350M 7.25% notes due 2029 if Dream Finders merger closes
articles.summary: Beazer issued a conditional notice on Sept 28, 2026 to redeem all $350.0M of its 7.250% senior notes due 2029 at 101.208% on Oct 20, conditional on the Dream Finders merger closing and funds being received.
articles.why_it_matters: A mechanical follow-on of the Dream Finders takeover: Beazer's $350M 2029 bonds were retired at closing, so Beazer's funding, including for land, is now set at the Dream Finders level.

suggested_update.text: Conditional notice issued Sept 28, 2026 to redeem all $350.0M of 7.250% senior notes due 2029 at 101.208% on Oct 20, 2026, subject to the Dream Finders merger closing.

articles.title: Meritage Homes Corporation Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary
articles.summary: On its Q3 2026 call Meritage withheld Q4 and full-year guidance, expects 2026 land spend below $1.5B, targets mid-20s net debt-to-capital, cut inventory about 12%, sold five communities to build-for-rent buyers and bought back $285M of stock.
articles.why_it_matters: Meritage, the fifth-largest builder, is holding land spend down and favoring liquidity, so new option takedowns will be smaller; its lot-exit sales to build-for-rent buyers also show where its excess land is going.

articles.title: Atlanta homebuilder lands $50 million credit facility to fund future projects
articles.summary: Parkland Communities, a metro Atlanta homebuilder and developer, secured a $50M credit facility from Anchor Loans, a West Coast private lender, to fund expansion across Georgia (Nov 16, 2026).
articles.why_it_matters: A private lender providing borrowing-base production capital to a small Southeast builder, which is one more non-bank source competing with land-bank capital at the low end of the market.

articles.title: D.R. Horton 8-K: board authorizes new $5.0B share buyback, no expiry
articles.summary: D.R. Horton's board authorized a new $5.0B share repurchase program on Sept 15, 2026, with no expiry; about $53M remained on the prior one. The company now expects fiscal 2026 buybacks of at least $3.25B.
articles.why_it_matters: The largest builder is sending more than $3B a year back to shareholders rather than into owned land, which fits its continued reliance on optioned lots from third parties and Forestar.

suggested_update.text: Board authorized a new $5.0B share repurchase program on Sept 15, 2026 (no expiry); fiscal 2026 repurchases expected to be at least $3.25B.

articles.title: [제2회] 사라진 토지와 현금의 행방 ── 56억 달러 스핀오프와 15.5억 달러의 계약금
articles.summary: A Korean blog analysis of Lennar's 10-K questions its land-light story: owned land cut to about 0.1 years' supply and 98% of lots optioned. It focuses on a $5.6B spin-off and $1.55B of option deposits.
articles.why_it_matters: This is third-party scrutiny of how Lennar accounts for land-bank deposits after the Millrose spin-off, the same theme as the shareholder suit; it is context for Domain's Lennar relationship, not news.

articles.title: Dream Finders Homes, Inc. 8-K: Item 8.01 other events
articles.summary: Dream Finders is exchanging Beazer's $250M 7.500% 2031 and $400M 8.000% 2032 notes for its own notes, with consents stripping covenants; 99.22% and 98.28% tendered by Nov. 4. Settles about Nov. 23. September consents had waived change of control.
articles.why_it_matters: A mechanical follow-on of the Beazer takeover: Dream Finders now carries Beazer's $650M of bonds itself with the covenants stripped, a modest gain in flexibility for how it funds land, including option deals Domain could bid on.

suggested_update.text: Exchange offer for Beazer's $250M 7.500% notes due 2031 and $400M 8.000% notes due 2032 into new Dream Finders notes drew 99.22% and 98.28% by Nov. 4, 2026, with settlement expected Nov. 23, 2026.

articles.title: National Home Corp. targets 18% gross margin with pace focus
articles.summary: National Home Corp. buys finished lots and builds entry-level homes on fast turns. CEO Michael Bergman said July gross margin was about 18%; the company is pacing for more than 800 closings in 2026 and targets 1,500-1,800 in 2027.
articles.why_it_matters: A builder that only buys finished lots and plans to roughly double closings next year will need a much larger lot pipeline, making Bergman a prospect call for lot-option financing.

suggested_update.text: HousingWire (Sept 9, 2026) lists Michael Bergman as CEO and president, co-founder Wade Jurney as executive chairman and John Hayes as COO; the company is pacing for 800+ closings in 2026 and targets 1,500-1,800 in 2027.

articles.title: Green Brick Partners, Inc. 8-K: Item 2.02 results of operations; Item 8.01 other events
articles.summary: Green Brick Q3 2026: 978 closings; EPS $1.35; gross margin 28.0%. Lots 51,435, 79.5% owned. Retired $50M of 4.00% notes due August 2026; homebuilding debt-to-capital 13.1%. Declared the regular Series A preferred dividend payable Dec. 15.
articles.why_it_matters: Green Brick owns nearly 80% of its lots and self-develops at 13% leverage, so it has the balance sheet to keep ignoring land-bank capital; a low-probability prospect for Domain.

articles.title: Japanese-owned builders are cutting U.S. outlooks: what’s next?
articles.summary: Daiwa House cut its FY2026 US homebuilding revenue forecast to ~$4.88B from $5.08B. Sumitomo Forestry cut its 2026 US sales forecast by $776M to $7.01B and closings by 1,455 to 12,705. Both are shifting to cost cuts and synergies.
articles.why_it_matters: The Japanese owners of Stanley Martin, DRB and Tri Pointe are pivoting from acquisitions to capital efficiency, including less capital tied up in land, which could raise their demand for off-balance-sheet lot structures.
articles.collected_via: bing-news: builder-ma: Japanese homebuilder acquires U.S. builder

articles.title: PULTEGROUP INC/MI/ 8-K: Item 2.02 results of operations
articles.summary: PulteGroup Q3 2026: 6,876 closings, down 9%; EPS $2.53. Gross margin 24.8% after $26M of land impairments. Debt-to-capital 12.1%, net 3.0%; cash $1.37B; $350M of buybacks. The release gives no lot counts or guidance.
articles.why_it_matters: Pulte is nearly debt-free on a net basis with $1.37B of cash, so it has little balance-sheet pressure to pay land-bank pricing; the $26M of land impairments shows some positions are underwater.

articles.title: Toll Brothers underwrites lots for tomorrow’s market, not yesterday’s
articles.summary: At HousingWire's Homebuilder Summit, Toll Brothers' Rob Paul and Dustin Bowersett said Toll scores land on gross margin and IRR. Land sellers hold price but give on timing and takedown schedules.
articles.why_it_matters: Sellers giving on takedown schedules rather than price is a direct read on the option terms Domain competes with, from a top-ten builder.

articles.title: PHM Q3 deep dive: housing demand softens, but backlog and active adult segment offer resilience
articles.summary: PulteGroup's Q3 2026 revenue fell 9.8% to $3.97 billion and adjusted EPS was $2.53, both below estimates; backlog rose 3.4% to $6.44 billion and management said it may reduce land spend in 2027.
articles.why_it_matters: If the third-largest builder cuts 2027 land spend, it will need fewer new optioned lots, which shrinks one source of demand for land-bank capital.

articles.title: Pretium Expands Real Estate Debt Platform
articles.summary: Pretium (about $70B AUM) is expanding its residential real estate debt platform by adding London-based Hilltop Capital Partners' team for U.K. development lending; the platform has lent about $8B since its December 2024 launch, including to homebuilders.
articles.why_it_matters: Pretium's expansion is UK development lending, not US builder land, so it adds no new competing capacity against Domain this week; worth tracking only because the platform has lent to homebuilders before.

articles.title: Ashton Woods leans into discipline as orders and margins slide
articles.summary: Ashton Woods' fiscal Q1 2027: net orders down 6.7%, cancellations 24.9%, gross margin 22.7% versus 25.0%. Management called land the main margin pressure and said it underwrites to today's pricing.
articles.why_it_matters: Ashton Woods is cutting new land commitments while land sellers are slow to reprice, which points to slower option demand from a top-15 builder.

articles.title: No Relief: Credit Conditions for Builders Still Tightening
articles.summary: NAHB's Q3 2026 AD&C financing survey shows builder credit for land acquisition, development and construction still tightening, with a net easing index of -15.3, extending a long streak of net tightening.
articles.why_it_matters: Continued tightening of bank AD&C credit keeps smaller builders short of land financing, which supports demand for land-bank capital and is a useful data point for Domain's investor pitch.

articles.title: Millrose Properties, Inc. 10-Q: quarterly report
articles.summary: Millrose 10-Q for Sept. 30, 2026: homesites under option $9.90B (from $8.87B at year-end), Q3 option fee revenue $209.5M, net income $130.0M, corporate debt $3.13B, plus $332.7M of single-family rental homes carrying a $210.6M secured facility.
articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback" (kept as the better source).

articles.title: Millrose Advances AFFO, Launches New Share Repurchase Program

articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback" (kept as the better source).

articles.title: Millrose (MRP) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback" (kept as the better source).

articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback" (kept as the better source).

articles.title: Millrose Properties Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
articles.summary: Millrose Q3: AFFO $0.80 a share, invested capital about $9.25B. Lennar book yields 8.5%; other builders 10.8%. Closed about $1.1B for Dream Finders' Beazer purchase: $580M land bank on 7,000 homesites plus $488M of 12% preferred. $250M buyback authorized.
articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Millrose 8-K: Q3 net income $130M, about $9.25B invested capital, $250M buyback" (kept as the better source).

articles.title: Millrose Properties defends purchase of rental homes from Lennar
articles.summary: Millrose management defended buying single-family rental homes from Lennar, describing it as a pilot program meant to improve home affordability (Seeking Alpha news brief; full text paywalled).
articles.why_it_matters: Same Q3 rental-home disclosure already in the feed; adds only that management is framing the Lennar home purchases as an affordability pilot, a use of capital outside lot option deals.

articles.title: Five Point Holdings Earnings Call: Liquidity Over Profits
articles.summary: Five Point's Q3 call: $4.4M net loss, $576M liquidity, 16.2% debt to capital, and land sales deferred into 2027 rather than cut prices. Its Hearthstone land-banking arm reported about $3.4B of assets under management, $2.8B fee-paying.
articles.why_it_matters: Same event as "Five Point Holdings, LLC Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results" (kept as the better source).

articles.title: Five Point Holdings, LLC  (FPH) 10-Q (mentions land banking)

extras.title: Mandate screen: who clears a top-25 or top-50 cutoff
extras.subtitle: 100 ranked builders. 19 flagged to watch: near a cutoff (ranks 23-28 or 48-53) or changed hands since the list. 7 changed hands since the list was published; 6 now sit under another ranked builder.
extras.method: Inputs: the published 2026 Builder 100 (ranked by 2025 closings, published May 2026) for rank, tier and closings; each builder's recorded owner or parent; and deals since the list from the industry M&A list and the builders' own M&A records. Rule: rank and tier are shown exactly as published and are not recomputed. "Parent that is a ranked builder" is filled when the builder was bought by a ranked builder after the list (the acquirer on that deal), or when its recorded parent name matches another ranked builder; parents that are not homebuilders on the list (for example Berkshire Hathaway, Sumitomo Forestry, Daiwa House) are shown in the owner column only. "Watch" is raised for ranks 23 to 28 and 48 to 53 (within 3 places of the top-25 or top-50 line) and for any builder bought, or agreed to be sold, after the list; only whole-company deals count (Berkshire's minority stake in Lennar is left out). The source column is the deal's own source. What is missing: Domain's mandate wording (which list, brand or parent level, tested when) is not public, so this table does not decide eligibility; no pro forma league table is computed; builders ranked 101 and below are not in the data, so it cannot show who would move into a place a merger opens. Run 2026-11-19.

extras.title: Call sheet: who to call and why
extras.subtitle: The 30 builders with the strongest public reason for a land banker to call now (of 40 with at least one reason), highest score first. 29 have a named land or finance contact. Points are an estimate.
extras.method: Estimate. Each builder earns points for public reasons to call, added up: 30 if half or more of its lots are optioned and no land banker is publicly named (or 20 if it says it uses land banking but does not name the banker); 25 if any outstanding debt comes due by 2028-11-30 (same rules as the "Debt coming due" table); 20 for a builder acquisition since the list was published (May 2026), as buyer or as the company bought; 15 if the first line of its land strategy states a land-light or asset-light approach; 15 if a corporate land or finance executive took the seat in the last 12 months (on or after 2025-11-19); plus 10 for a top-25 builder or 5 for a top-50 builder. The top 30 are kept; ties go to the higher-ranked builder. The reason sentence lists the scoring facts, largest first, and the source column is the source of the largest. Person to call: a corporate land head first (someone whose title names land; acquisition before development), then treasury or capital markets, then the CFO, then any other corporate land-team executive, Verified before Reported before Inferred; if none is recorded the row says "no land or finance contact found" and no one else is substituted. Contact details are shown only when the company publishes them (pattern-built emails are left out). Named land bankers are read from the "Who banks whom" table (competitor research) so the names match it, falling back to the same name rules applied to the builder's own records if that table is missing; "none named" means none found in public sources, not that none exists. Left out: nonprofits (Habitat for Humanity International, NeighborWorks America) and build-to-rent operators and contractors (AMH, Middleburg Communities, BBL Building Co., Hancock Builders, Lifestyle Homes, Jim Chapman Construction Group). What is missing: the owned-versus-optioned split is public for only 21 builders and debt for 57, so private builders score low on thin data, not on low need; start dates are recorded for about a quarter of executives. The weights are a first guess, printed so they can be changed. Run 2026-11-19.

extras.title: Who banks whom: land bankers publicly linked to each top-100 builder
extras.subtitle: 19 builders have a publicly named land banker or lot-option financier (3 more have only other financing named); 9 are flagged white space (heavy option use or land-light, no banker named). Financing research is in for 100 of 100 builders.
extras.method: Facts, then one judgement. Each filled cell is a public link. "Land banking" means at least one source describes a land-bank, lot-option or homesite-option arrangement with that firm; "Other financing only" means the only public tie is another kind of financing (for example a term loan Kennedy Lewis agented for United Homes Group, or JV equity). Rows whose text records no link, an indirect or people-only link, or an unnamed counterparty are never counted (same rule as the app build). Each cell is a public link found either in that builder's financing research (its land_banking and competitor_links rows, from filings and press) or in the competitor profile for that financier; the bracket shows the strongest confidence tag, the largest disclosed amount and the latest date, and every underlying link with its source is in the "Builder-financier links" table. The white-space flag is our estimate, not a fact: it is set when no land banker or lot-option financier is publicly named for the builder AND at least one of these holds: 50% or more of controlled lots are optioned, the builder describes itself as land-light / asset-light, or it reports using land banking without naming the banker. A blank white-space cell with zero links means the builder owns most of its land or its option share is not public. Absence of a public link is not proof of no relationship: most land-bank deals are never announced, and Domain's own book is not public. Left out on purpose: developers, JV partners and affiliates selling lots, land sellers, owners and acquirers (e.g. Berkshire Hathaway), rental-community clients, builders that are only limited partners in a lender's fund, and historical (pre-2015) partners. Other named financiers include equity JV capital (e.g. GTIS/Brightshore, Presidio) and captive lot developers (Forestar for D.R. Horton), which compete for the same land.
